title: Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Doctoral Scholarships
description: The Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Doctoral Scholarships fund social sciences and humanities PhD students at Canadian universities with…
details:
The Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Doctoral Scholarships fund social sciences and humanities PhD students at Canadian universities with CAD 40,000 per year for three years plus up to CAD 20,000 annually for research travel, alongside a leadership curriculum of retreats and mentorship. International students enrolled in Canadian doctorates are eligible within the program’s quota.

Cycles open each autumn and close in winter, with universities involved in the process and roughly 15 to 20 scholars named annually. Selection prizes engagement with the Foundation’s themes, from human rights to environment, as much as academic records.
benefits: CAD 40,000 per year for three years toward tuition and living costs. An additional allowance of up to CAD 20,000 per year for research travel and knowledge dissemination. Membership in the Foundation's leadership program with retreats, mentors and a public-engagement curriculum. A network of scholars, fellows and mentors across Canadian public life. Freedom to pursue engaged scholarship with unusual travel resources. One of Canada's most prestigious doctoral brands for policy-facing careers.
requirements: Doctoral students in the humanities and social sciences (broadly defined) at Canadian universities, or Canadians studying abroad. International students enrolled or enrolling full-time in a Canadian PhD are eligible within the program's quota for non-Canadians. First or second year of the doctoral program at the time of taking up the award. Research engaging the Foundation's themes: human rights and dignity, responsible citizenship, Canada and the world, and people and their natural environment. Evidence of leadership, community engagement and public communication ability, since scholars join a leadership curriculum. Nomination or application per the current cycle's rules through your university and the Foundation portal.
required_documents: Application through the Foundation's portal in the annual cycle, with university endorsement steps as specified. Research statement tying your doctorate to the Foundation's four themes. CV emphasizing leadership and engagement beyond publications. Transcripts and proof of doctoral enrolment or admission. Reference letters per the cycle's instructions. Essays or video elements where the cycle requires them.
summary: The Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Doctoral Scholarships fund social sciences and humanities PhD students at Canadian universities with…

title: Carleton Prestige Scholarships (Canada)
description: Carleton University’s Prestige Scholarships, led by the Richardson and Chancellor’s awards, fund top incoming undergraduates up to full…
details:
Carleton University’s Prestige Scholarships, led by the Richardson and Chancellor’s awards, fund top incoming undergraduates up to full tuition for four years, sitting above automatic entrance scholarships that start at 80 percent admission averages. Selection weighs leadership and community impact alongside grades, judged from a dedicated application with essays.

The prestige application closes in early December for the following fall (historically December 1; confirm each cycle on the awards page), requiring the admission file to be in first. Ottawa’s government and tech co-op market makes the award compound over a degree.
benefits: Named prestige awards (including the Richardson and Chancellor's scholarships) reaching full tuition for four years. Automatic entrance scholarships of CAD 4,000 to 16,000 layered beneath the prestige tier for 80%+ averages. Ottawa placement beside Canada's federal government, tech sector and co-op employers. Prestige scholars join development programming and mentorship. Stackable with faculty and donor awards in later years. Carleton's strong co-op programs convert study into paid Canadian experience.
requirements: High-achieving students entering a first undergraduate degree at Carleton University in Ottawa. Admission averages in the high 90s realistically compete for the top named awards. International and Canadian applicants are both eligible for the prestige pool, with specific awards varying. Demonstrated leadership and community involvement, weighted heavily beside grades. A complete admission application by the early-winter scholarship cutoff. Renewal requires maintaining a high GPA on a full course load each year.
required_documents: Undergraduate admission application (via the OUAC 105 route for international applicants). High school transcripts with translations where needed. English proficiency evidence per admission rules. The prestige scholarship application with essays on leadership and impact. Reference support where the award requires it. Study permit documents after selection.
summary: Carleton University’s Prestige Scholarships, led by the Richardson and Chancellor’s awards, fund top incoming undergraduates up to full…

title: Sabanci University Scholarships (Turkey)
description: Sabanci University in Istanbul funds international students through merit scholarships reaching 100 percent tuition with stipends and dormitory…
details:
Sabanci University in Istanbul funds international students through merit scholarships reaching 100 percent tuition with stipends and dormitory support at the top tiers, while STEM graduate students commonly receive full waiver-plus-stipend packages. The campus is fully English-medium with an interdisciplinary program structure rare in Turkish higher education.

Scholarship consideration is automatic from the admission ranking, so the file itself is the competition, and intakes run effectively rolling across the year. For students weighing Türkiye Burslari odds, Sabanci offers a strong university-funded parallel route.
benefits: Undergraduate merit scholarships from 25 to 100 percent tuition, with top awards adding stipends and dormitory support. Graduate packages in STEM commonly combine full tuition waiver, monthly stipend and housing support. A fully English-medium campus with an interdisciplinary structure unusual in Turkey. Istanbul location with a dedicated, modern campus on the Asian side. Strong industry links through the Sabanci Group ecosystem. Renewable through the program subject to standing.
requirements: International applicants to Sabanci University's English-taught programs in Istanbul. Undergraduate scholarships are merit-ranked from the admission file (grades, testing, achievements) with no separate application. Graduate applicants in engineering and natural sciences are widely funded through tuition waivers plus stipends; social sciences and management offer tiered support. English proficiency per admission rules (TOEFL/IELTS or Sabanci's own ELAE pathway). All nationalities compete equally, with a substantial international cohort. Research-track graduate applicants benefit from aligning with faculty labs before applying.
required_documents: Online application through Sabanci's international admission portal. High school or university transcripts and diplomas with translations. Testing evidence for undergraduates where available (SAT and national exams strengthen ranking). English proficiency evidence or ELAE pathway acceptance. Statement of purpose and references for graduate programs. Passport copy.
summary: Sabanci University in Istanbul funds international students through merit scholarships reaching 100 percent tuition with stipends and dormitory…

title: American University of Sharjah Graduate Assistantships
description: American University of Sharjah funds graduate students through assistantships that combine tuition remission, often full, with a monthly…
details:
American University of Sharjah funds graduate students through assistantships that combine tuition remission, often full, with a monthly stipend and commonly housing support, in exchange for teaching or research duties. Programs span engineering, sciences and business at one of the Gulf’s most established American-accredited universities.

Applications run for fall and spring intakes with effectively rolling review, and contacting supervisors with funded projects raises assistantship odds meaningfully. Sharjah’s costs sit well below neighboring Dubai while keeping its job market in commuting range.
benefits: Tuition remission, full for many assistantship holders, plus a monthly stipend for duties. On-campus housing support commonly bundled for graduate assistants. UAE residence visa sponsorship through the university. An American-accredited curriculum in one of the Gulf's most established universities. Sharjah's lower living costs beside Dubai's job market. Teaching and research experience that strengthens PhD and industry applications.
requirements: Admitted graduate applicants to AUS master's and PhD programs in engineering, sciences, business and arts. A strong bachelor's (typically CGPA 3.0+) for master's entry, and a master's for doctoral tracks. English proficiency (AUS is fully English-medium; TOEFL or IELTS per program). Availability to work assistantship hours in teaching or research alongside full-time study. All nationalities eligible, with large South Asian and Arab student communities on campus. Research-track applicants strengthen files by contacting supervisors whose grants fund positions.
required_documents: Graduate admission application through the AUS portal. Transcripts and degree certificates, attested per UAE requirements. English scores (TOEFL/IELTS) per the program page. Statement of purpose and CV. Two to three recommendation letters. Assistantship application or indication within the admission process.
summary: American University of Sharjah funds graduate students through assistantships that combine tuition remission, often full, with a monthly…

title: Westlake University PhD Fellowship (China)
description: Westlake University in Hangzhou fully funds its PhD students with covered tuition and a monthly living stipend, inside…
details:
Westlake University in Hangzhou fully funds its PhD students with covered tuition and a monthly living stipend, inside a young, research-only institution built with Caltech-style density and internationally recruited faculty. Programs run in English across AI, physical sciences, engineering and life sciences, with supervisor match driving admissions.

Intakes and joint-program rounds run through the year, so applicants should email prospective labs first and apply on the portal with their support. For students wanting a funded China PhD outside the CSC machinery, Westlake is the standout modern option.
benefits: Full tuition coverage and a monthly living stipend for the doctoral duration. Subsidized housing options and insurance support on the Hangzhou campus. Labs led by internationally recruited faculty, including high-profile structural biology and AI groups. A new, exceptionally well-funded private research university backed by major Chinese philanthropy. Small cohorts with high supervision density compared with giant state universities. Hangzhou's tech ecosystem (Alibaba's home city) around the campus.
requirements: International and Chinese applicants with a bachelor's or master's degree in sciences, engineering or life sciences. Research-driven profiles: Westlake is a research-only university modeled on Caltech-style density. English-taught environment, so English evidence rather than Chinese is the norm for internationals. Strong grounding in the target field, from AI and physics to structural biology and genetics. Willingness to relocate to Hangzhou for a full-time doctoral program. Positive supervisor match, since admission runs through the joint or independent PhD tracks with named labs.
required_documents: Online application through Westlake's PhD admissions portal for your track. Transcripts and degree certificates with English translations. CV, research statement and publication list where available. Two to three recommendation letters submitted online. English proficiency evidence (program pages state accepted proofs). Passport copy.
summary: Westlake University in Hangzhou fully funds its PhD students with covered tuition and a monthly living stipend, inside…

title: University of Lausanne Master’s Grants (Switzerland)
description: The University of Lausanne Master’s Grants pay international students CHF 1,600 per month for the entire master’s, plus…
details:
The University of Lausanne Master’s Grants pay international students CHF 1,600 per month for the entire master’s, plus tuition exemption, on the Lake Geneva campus next to EPFL. Around ten grants go each year to applicants whose foreign bachelor’s results stand out and who could not otherwise afford Swiss study.

The application is a standalone dossier submitted by November 1 for the following September, judged by a university commission alongside regular admission. For students targeting Switzerland without Swiss-level savings, this is one of the few genuinely need-aware full-stipend routes.
benefits: CHF 1,600 every month from September through the master's standard duration, one of Europe's most generous university stipends. Exemption from the standard tuition, leaving only a small semester fee of around CHF 80. Study on the Lake Geneva campus shared with EPFL, in one of Europe's strongest research ecosystems. Around 10 grants awarded annually, so real but winnable competition. Access to UNIL strengths from HEC Lausanne to life sciences, sport sciences and criminology. Swiss residence during studies with the quality of life that entails.
requirements: International students holding a foreign bachelor's degree, applying to a master's at the University of Lausanne. The foreign degree must be recognized as equivalent by UNIL and distinguish itself by its quality (top-tier results expected). Applicants must not have been previously enrolled at UNIL and must not already hold a master's. All nationalities compete; the grant explicitly targets students who could not study in Switzerland without support. Language per program: French for most master's, with a set of English-taught options (proof at B2 to C1 by track). Commitment to full-time study in Lausanne for the program's duration.
required_documents: UNIL Master's Grant application form from the university's grants page. Bachelor's transcripts and diploma with certified translations where needed. Detailed CV and a motivation letter explaining need and fit. Two reference letters (academic). Language evidence per your chosen program (French or English). Copy of passport and any program-specific attachments.
summary: The University of Lausanne Master’s Grants pay international students CHF 1,600 per month for the entire master’s, plus…

title: Deutschlandstipendium (Germany)
description: The Deutschlandstipendium pays EUR 300 per month, half from the German federal government and half from private sponsors,…
details:
The Deutschlandstipendium pays EUR 300 per month, half from the German federal government and half from private sponsors, to high-performing students of any nationality at participating German universities, independent of income and stackable with other funding. Selection rewards grades plus social engagement and personal journey, and awards renew up to the standard study period.

Each university runs its own application window, most commonly in summer for winter semester, so international students already holding German admission should check their institution’s page immediately. The sponsor mentoring and events frequently matter as much as the money.
benefits: EUR 300 per month, half funded by the federal government and half by private sponsors. Paid regardless of income or parental means, on top of any other support. Awarded for at least two semesters and renewable up to the standard period of study. Sponsor networking events, mentoring and internships often accompany the money. Available at hundreds of German universities, from TU9 giants to applied-science universities. A recognized merit line on any German CV.
requirements: Students of any nationality enrolled (or accepted) at a participating German university; international students are explicitly eligible. Strong academic performance as the core criterion, with each university running its own selection. Community engagement, social commitment and personal circumstances (like being first in family to study) weigh into selection. All degree levels up to and including master's at participating universities. The award is compatible with BAföG and most other funding, since it is income-independent. Selection happens at your university, so criteria details vary by institution.
required_documents: Application through your own university's Deutschlandstipendium portal during its annual window. Transcript of records or university entrance qualification for new students. CV and a motivation letter covering achievements and engagement. Evidence of volunteering, awards or special circumstances where applicable. Enrolment certificate (or admission letter). Any university-specific forms.
summary: The Deutschlandstipendium pays EUR 300 per month, half from the German federal government and half from private sponsors,…

title: Politecnico di Milano Merit Scholarships (Italy)
description: Politecnico di Milano assigns merit scholarships automatically to its best-ranked international MSc admits: gold awards of about EUR…
details:
Politecnico di Milano assigns merit scholarships automatically to its best-ranked international MSc admits: gold awards of about EUR 10,000 per year and silver awards of about EUR 5,000, both with tuition waivers, plus waiver-only awards further down the list. There is no separate application, so the admission file in the early autumn round is the entire competition.

As Italy’s top technical university and a global top-10 name in design, Polimi pairs the awards with Milan’s industry ecosystem. Enrolled students can stack the income-based DSU regional scholarship on top for near-complete funding.
benefits: Gold-level awards around EUR 10,000 per year plus full tuition waiver for the very top admits. Silver-level awards around EUR 5,000 per year plus tuition waiver for the next band. Tuition-waiver-only awards extend further down the merit ranking. Study at Italy's top-ranked technical university, a global top-10 name in design and top-20 in architecture and engineering. Milan's industry ecosystem in design, fashion, energy and engineering feeds internships and jobs. Renewability into the second year with on-track credits.
requirements: International applicants to English-taught Laurea Magistrale (MSc) programs at Politecnico di Milano. Outstanding academic profiles: merit scholarships are assigned automatically to the best-ranked admitted candidates. A bachelor's degree qualifying for the chosen MSc in engineering, architecture or design. English proficiency per the admission requirement (commonly IELTS 6.0 or equivalent). No separate scholarship application; evaluation happens within admission rounds. Income-based DSU regional scholarships can be pursued separately after enrolment.
required_documents: Online admission application through the Polimi international portal in an admission round. Bachelor's transcripts and degree documents with translations. English certificate at the required level. CV and motivation elements per the program's requirements. Portfolio for architecture and design programs. Passport copy.
summary: Politecnico di Milano assigns merit scholarships automatically to its best-ranked international MSc admits: gold awards of about EUR…

title: GIST Scholarship (Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology)
description: GIST funds its international graduate students through a full-support model: tuition covered, monthly lab stipends, subsidized dormitories and…
details:
GIST funds its international graduate students through a full-support model: tuition covered, monthly lab stipends, subsidized dormitories and meal support, with all courses taught in English at one of Korea’s most citation-dense research institutions. Master’s and PhD cohorts draw heavily from South Asia, Southeast Asia and Africa.

Admissions run in two rounds each year on an effectively rolling rhythm, and contacting prospective supervisors before applying meaningfully raises success rates. For research-focused students who want funded Korean STEM study without the giant GKS competition, GIST is a dependable route.
benefits: Full tuition support for admitted graduate students under GIST's standard funding model. Monthly research stipends paid through your laboratory, plus subsidized dormitories and meal support. Additional incentives such as airfare support for new international students in many cycles. GIST ranks among the world's top institutions for citations per faculty, with intense research density. All-English coursework removes the Korean-language barrier that limits other Korean options. Strong pipelines into Korean industry R&D and international PhD or postdoc positions.
requirements: International applicants to GIST's graduate programs in engineering, natural sciences, AI and life sciences. A relevant bachelor's degree (for master's) or master's degree (for PhD) with strong grades. English-taught environment: GIST conducts all courses in English, so English evidence (IELTS/TOEFL) is required while Korean is not. Research orientation demonstrated through projects, theses or publications. All nationalities eligible, with large cohorts from South Asia, Southeast Asia and Africa. Willingness to join a research lab full time, since funding flows through the assistantship model.
required_documents: Online application through the GIST international admissions system for your intake. Degree certificates and transcripts with certified English translations. English proficiency scores per the admission guide. Statement of purpose naming target labs and research directions. Two recommendation letters submitted online. Passport copy and any publications or research outputs.
summary: GIST funds its international graduate students through a full-support model: tuition covered, monthly lab stipends, subsidized dormitories and…

title: Aarhus University Scholarships (Denmark)
description: Aarhus University awards its strongest non-EU master’s applicants tuition waivers, full or partial, with a subset of packages…
details:
Aarhus University awards its strongest non-EU master’s applicants tuition waivers, full or partial, with a subset of packages adding a living stipend for a fully funded Danish degree. There is no separate scholarship form: departments rank the regular admission files submitted by the annual January 15 deadline for autumn entry.

Aarhus is Denmark’s second-largest university and its host city consistently ranks among Europe’s best student towns, with a huge student population share. Combined with Denmark’s post-study job-seeking scheme, a waiver here becomes one of Scandinavia’s best value routes.
benefits: Full or partial tuition waivers for the two-year master's. A subset of awards additionally includes a living-cost stipend, making a genuinely full package. Study at Denmark's second-largest university, ranked in the global top 150 with famous strengths from agriculture to nanoscience. Aarhus regularly polls among the world's happiest student cities with a huge student share of the population. No separate scholarship application: admission excellence is the competition. Denmark's post-study establishment card allows job seeking after graduation.
requirements: Non-EU/EEA citizens who require a study permit and pay tuition for English-taught master's programs at Aarhus University. Outstanding academic records; scholarships go to the top applicants ranked by the admitting departments. A complete admission application through Denmark's application system by the winter deadline. English proficiency per program requirements (commonly IELTS 6.5). Applicants for all Aarhus faculties are assessed, with Natural Sciences and Technical Sciences among the largest award pools. EU/EEA citizens study tuition-free in Denmark and are outside this scheme.
required_documents: Master's admission application via the Danish application portal in the winter window. Bachelor's transcripts and diploma with translations. English test results per the program page. CV and any program-specific documents (motivation letters where required). Passport copy. Scholarship consideration is automatic from the admission file.
summary: Aarhus University awards its strongest non-EU master’s applicants tuition waivers, full or partial, with a subset of packages…

title: Khalifa University Scholarships (UAE)
description: Khalifa University in Abu Dhabi funds its graduate students with full tuition and monthly stipends, commonly around AED…
details:
Khalifa University in Abu Dhabi funds its graduate students with full tuition and monthly stipends, commonly around AED 8,000 for master’s and up to AED 12,000 for PhD researchers, plus health insurance and visa sponsorship. Programs span engineering, computing, science and medicine at one of the Gulf’s highest-ranked research universities.

Admissions run for fall and spring intakes with rolling review, and naming a potential supervisor in your statement strengthens research applications considerably. For students targeting a funded STEM degree in the Gulf, Khalifa sits alongside KAUST as the region’s most reliable full-support option.
benefits: Full tuition coverage for admitted graduate students under the university's standard support model. Monthly stipends for full-time research students, commonly around AED 8,000 at master's and up to AED 12,000 at PhD level. Health insurance and support with visa sponsorship in Abu Dhabi. Subsidized on-campus housing options for eligible students. Research inside one of the Gulf's top-ranked universities, with strengths in aerospace, robotics, energy and biomedical fields. Industry ties across Abu Dhabi's technology and energy ecosystem, from ADNOC to the space program.
requirements: International and UAE-based applicants to Khalifa University's graduate programs in engineering, science, medicine and computing in Abu Dhabi. A relevant bachelor's degree with a strong GPA (typically 3.0 minimum, competitive awards higher) for master's entry, and a master's for most PhD tracks. English proficiency of IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL iBT 91 for graduate admission. GRE requirements apply to some engineering PhD programs (and strengthen any file). Full-time commitment to study and research on campus. Undergraduate international applicants compete for separate merit scholarships with their own criteria.
required_documents: Online application through the Khalifa University admissions portal for your intake. Degree certificates and transcripts with attested translations where required. English scores (IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 91) and GRE where the program requires it. Statement of purpose aligned with a research area or supervisor. Two to three recommendation letters. Passport copy and CV.
summary: Khalifa University in Abu Dhabi funds its graduate students with full tuition and monthly stipends, commonly around AED…

title: Ibn Haldun University International Scholarships (Turkey)
description: Ibn Haldun University in Istanbul awards full scholarships to top international applicants covering tuition, dormitory housing and a…
details:
Ibn Haldun University in Istanbul awards full scholarships to top international applicants covering tuition, dormitory housing and a monthly stipend, with partial tiers from 25 percent upward for strong candidates below the top line. The university specializes in social sciences and humanities with a trilingual English-Turkish-Arabic model and deliberately international classes.

Applications run in cycles through the year on the university’s portal, with scholarship tiers assigned automatically from admission ranking. For students seeking a funded route into Turkey outside the giant Türkiye Burslari competition, it is one of the strongest private-university options.
benefits: Full scholarships covering tuition, university dormitory accommodation and a monthly cash stipend. Partial tiers covering 25 to 100 percent of tuition for strong but not top-ranked applicants. A purpose-built Istanbul campus with a comparative education model spanning English, Turkish and Arabic. Small class sizes and a graduate-heavy profile unusual among Turkish private universities. Istanbul's living costs remain moderate by European standards, and dormitory coverage removes the largest one. A strengthening reputation in social sciences with international faculty.
requirements: International students applying to Ibn Haldun University's programs in Istanbul across social sciences, humanities, law, psychology, management and Islamic studies. Strong academic records; full scholarships target the highest-scoring applicants of each cycle. Bachelor's applicants with high school completion, and graduate applicants with the relevant prior degree. English-taught programs require English evidence, while some programs use Turkish or Arabic; the university's language school supports gaps. All nationalities welcome, with an intentionally international cohort from dozens of countries. Separate scholarship tiers exist, so partial support remains possible below the full-award line.
required_documents: Online application through the Ibn Haldun international admission system. High school or university transcripts and diplomas with translations. Passport copy and photo. Language evidence for your track (English, Turkish or Arabic) or willingness to take preparatory classes. Motivation statement and references for graduate programs. Any program-specific items such as writing samples for selective departments.
summary: Ibn Haldun University in Istanbul awards full scholarships to top international applicants covering tuition, dormitory housing and a…

title: Université de Montréal Exemption Scholarships (UdeM)
description: Université de Montréal grants automatic tuition exemption scholarships to admitted international students at every level, reducing fees by…
details:
Université de Montréal grants automatic tuition exemption scholarships to admitted international students at every level, reducing fees by up to about CAD 13,000 per year with no separate application, and PhD students see international rates fall close to Quebec resident levels. The exemption level appears directly in the admission offer.

As Canada’s leading French-language university, UdeM anchors the MILA AI ecosystem and Montreal’s famously affordable student life. The winning strategy is simple: build the strongest possible admission file, then stack faculty scholarships and assistantships on top of the automatic exemption.
benefits: Automatic tuition reductions from admission, reaching roughly CAD 13,000 per year at the strongest levels. PhD students historically benefit most, with international fees brought close to Quebec resident rates. No application effort: the offer letter states your exemption level. Montreal combines North America's lowest big-city living costs with a massive student ecosystem. Stackable with faculty scholarships, assistantships and Mitacs funding at graduate level. Access to the MILA-anchored AI and research environment for graduate students.
requirements: International students admitted to Université de Montréal, Canada's leading French-language university. All admitted international students are assessed automatically; there is no separate scholarship application. Undergraduate, master's and doctoral levels each carry their own exemption scale (levels A through C). Sufficient French for French-taught programs, though a growing set of graduate options accommodate English. Maintaining full-time enrolment and academic standing keeps the exemption active. Quebec's separate fee framework means exemptions interact with program and level, detailed at admission.
required_documents: Admission application to your chosen UdeM program through the university portal. Transcripts and diplomas with certified translations where required. French proficiency evidence for French-taught programs (or English per program rules). CV, motivation letter and references for graduate programs. Passport copy. No separate scholarship forms: the exemption is assessed from the admission file.
summary: Université de Montréal grants automatic tuition exemption scholarships to admitted international students at every level, reducing fees by…

title: University of Calgary International Entrance Scholarship
description: The University of Calgary International Entrance Scholarship awards top incoming international undergraduates CAD 15,000 per year, renewable across…
details:
The University of Calgary International Entrance Scholarship awards top incoming international undergraduates CAD 15,000 per year, renewable across four years for a CAD 60,000 total, one of the largest entrance packages in Canada. Selection blends a competitive admission average with genuine leadership and community involvement, so the statements matter as much as the grades.

Applications run through the student portal with a deadline of December 1 for the following fall, requiring an admission application first. Calgary’s below-Toronto living costs and energy-sector job market make the award stretch even further.
benefits: CAD 15,000 per year, renewable across all four years for a total of CAD 60,000. One of the largest entrance awards any Canadian university offers international undergraduates. Calgary pairs strong engineering, business and kinesiology programs with Canada's energy-sector job market. Stackable with faculty awards and the university's other international scholarships. Alberta's living costs sit below Toronto and Vancouver, stretching the award further. Recipients join a recognized scholar cohort with development programming.
requirements: International students on a Canadian study permit entering their first year of any undergraduate degree at the University of Calgary. Admission for the fall term with a competitive admission average, typically well above the faculty minimum. Demonstrated leadership through school, community or extracurricular involvement, which the selection weighs heavily. A complete admission application submitted by the early-December scholarship deadline. Renewal each year requires maintaining a strong GPA over a full course load. Students transferring from another post-secondary institution are not eligible for this entrance award.
required_documents: Undergraduate admission application through the University of Calgary portal. High school transcripts (with certified translations where applicable). English proficiency evidence per admission rules (IELTS, TOEFL or approved alternatives). The scholarship application within the student portal, including leadership and involvement statements. Reference or activity verification where the form requests it. Study permit documentation after selection.
summary: The University of Calgary International Entrance Scholarship awards top incoming international undergraduates CAD 15,000 per year, renewable across…

title: Taiwan MOE Scholarship (Ministry of Education)
description: The Taiwan MOE Scholarship funds full degrees in Taiwan across bachelor’s, master’s and PhD levels, paying tuition up…
details:
The Taiwan MOE Scholarship funds full degrees in Taiwan across bachelor’s, master’s and PhD levels, paying tuition up to NTD 40,000 per semester plus a living stipend of NTD 15,000 to 20,000 per month for the standard program length. Applications go through the Taiwan embassy or TECO office serving your country during an annual window that typically runs February 1 to March 31.

Taiwan combines world-class engineering and semiconductor programs with low living costs, and many universities waive tuition beyond the scholarship cap for MOE scholars. Applicants pursue university admission simultaneously, since awards are confirmed against an admitted place.
benefits: Tuition and academic fees covered up to NTD 40,000 per semester, with any excess paid by the student or waived by the university. Monthly stipend of NTD 15,000 for bachelor's students and NTD 20,000 for master's and PhD students. Support for the full standard duration of each degree level. Taiwan's universities offer strong engineering, semiconductor and Chinese-language ecosystems at low living costs. Compatible with university-level tuition top-up waivers many institutions grant MOE scholars. A parallel Huayu Enrichment Scholarship exists for pure Mandarin language study.
requirements: International students (excluding nationals of mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau) applying for degree study at Taiwanese universities. High school completion for bachelor's applicants, or the relevant prior degree for graduate applicants, with strong academic records. Not holding Republic of China (Taiwan) nationality and not being an overseas Chinese student under separate schemes. Not simultaneously receiving another Taiwan government scholarship or already enrolled in the target degree level. Application is made through the Taiwan embassy, TECO office or representative office serving your country. Language evidence per your program: TOCFL for Chinese-taught or English tests for English-taught degrees.
required_documents: Scholarship application form from your local Taiwan representative office (TECO). Copies of your passport and highest degree certificate with transcripts (translated and notarized as required). Proof of university application to Taiwanese institutions for the same intake. Language certificates: TOCFL for Chinese-medium or IELTS/TOEFL for English-medium programs. Two recommendation letters where the office requires them. Study plan for graduate applicants.
summary: The Taiwan MOE Scholarship funds full degrees in Taiwan across bachelor’s, master’s and PhD levels, paying tuition up…

title: SNU Global Scholarship (Seoul National University)
description: The SNU Global Scholarship (GSFS) funds top international admits at Seoul National University with full tuition and a…
details:
The SNU Global Scholarship (GSFS) funds top international admits at Seoul National University with full tuition and a monthly living allowance across bachelor’s, master’s and PhD programs. Selection happens inside the regular admission process, with the strongest files in each spring and autumn cycle picked automatically, and departmental assistantships often stack on top at graduate level.

SNU is Korea’s most prestigious university, and its admission cycles run roughly February-March for autumn entry and September for spring. Applicants should also run the separate Global Korea Scholarship process in parallel to maximize funding chances.
benefits: Full tuition coverage for the standard duration of the degree. Monthly living allowance, with graduate awards commonly around KRW 1,200,000 or more. Study at Korea's most prestigious university, with the strongest domestic employer recognition. Department assistantships and professor-funded positions frequently top up graduate support. SNU's Gwanak campus offers extensive dormitories priced well below Seoul market rents. Renewable each semester subject to academic standing.
requirements: International students applying for admission to Seoul National University, Korea's top-ranked institution. Glaring academic excellence, since GSFS (Global Scholarship for Foreign Students) awards go to the strongest admits in each cycle. Both undergraduate and graduate applicants are considered, with graduate awards more numerous. No separate nationality restrictions; applicants from Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nigeria and worldwide compete equally. Language requirements follow the program: many graduate programs run in English, while Korean (TOPIK) strengthens any file. Applicants should also consider the parallel Global Korea Scholarship, which uses a separate government process.
required_documents: SNU admission application for your intake through the international admissions portal. Academic transcripts and degree certificates with certified translations. Study plan and personal statement per the admission forms. Recommendation letters (typically two for graduate programs). Language evidence: English scores or TOPIK depending on the program. Scholarship indication within the admission application where prompted.
summary: The SNU Global Scholarship (GSFS) funds top international admits at Seoul National University with full tuition and a…

title: Rotary Global Grant Scholarships
description: Rotary Global Grant Scholarships fund graduate study abroad with a minimum of USD 30,000 per award, for degrees…
details:
Rotary Global Grant Scholarships fund graduate study abroad with a minimum of USD 30,000 per award, for degrees that advance Rotary’s focus areas: health, water and sanitation, education, peace, economic development and the environment. Every scholarship is sponsored by a local Rotary club and district, which partner with a host district near your university to build the grant.

There is no central deadline: districts run their own selections year-round, so the winning move is approaching clubs in your city about twelve months before you plan to start. For service-minded applicants, the two-community backing and mentorship make this far more than a check.
benefits: Scholarships funded at a minimum of USD 30,000, frequently higher when districts add funds. Coverage can include tuition, living costs, travel and insurance as budgeted in the grant. Backing from two Rotary communities, home and host, providing mentorship and networks on both ends. Open field of universities worldwide, as long as the program matches a focus area. Strong alumni identity within Rotary's global service network of 1.4 million members. Possible multi-year support for longer graduate programs where districts agree.
requirements: Graduate-level applicants whose planned studies fall within Rotary's areas of focus: peacebuilding and conflict prevention, disease prevention and treatment, water and sanitation, maternal and child health, basic education and literacy, community economic development, and the environment. Sponsorship by a local Rotary club or district in your home country, which co-creates the grant with a host district near your university. Admission (or strong prospects of admission) to a graduate program abroad aligned with the chosen focus area. A record of community service and a credible plan to apply your degree to measurable impact. No fixed nationality restrictions; availability depends on your local district's funding and priorities. Rotary members and their close relatives face restrictions, so check the participation rules.
required_documents: Application materials required by your sponsoring Rotary club or district (formats vary). University admission letter or evidence of application to the intended graduate program. Study and impact plan linking your degree to a Rotary focus area. CV, transcripts and references demonstrating academic and service records. Budget worksheet for the grant developed with the sponsoring district. Interview participation at club and district levels.
summary: Rotary Global Grant Scholarships fund graduate study abroad with a minimum of USD 30,000 per award, for degrees…

title: Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarship (TU Delft)
description: The Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarship is TU Delft’s flagship award, covering the full tuition fee…
details:
The Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarship is TU Delft’s flagship award, covering the full tuition fee and a monthly living allowance for the entire two-year MSc at the Netherlands’ most famous engineering university. It is open to all nationalities with a bachelor’s GPA of at least 80 percent of the scale maximum.

There is no separate application portal: candidates simply submit a complete, excellent MSc admission file by December 1 for the following September and mark the scholarship option. For engineering students wanting a genuinely fully funded European master’s, this is one of the continent’s premier targets.
benefits: Full coverage of the TU Delft tuition fee for the entire two-year MSc. A monthly allowance contributing to living costs for the program's duration. Study at the Netherlands' largest and most famous technical university, ranked among the world's best for engineering. Membership of the Justus & Louise van Effen scholars community with its events and network. Access to Delft's aerospace, civil, computer science and design programs that anchor global rankings. A prestige award that reliably signals excellence to employers and PhD committees.
requirements: Excellent international students holding a non-Dutch bachelor's degree, applying to a TU Delft MSc program. A cumulative GPA of at least 80 percent of the scale maximum in your bachelor's. A complete admission application to TU Delft submitted by the scholarship deadline (December 1). All nationalities are eligible, with the award targeted at the very top of the applicant pool. English proficiency at TU Delft's MSc standard (commonly IELTS 6.5 overall or TOEFL 90). No simultaneous full scholarship for the same program.
required_documents: TU Delft MSc admission application completed in the university portal by December 1. Academic transcripts demonstrating the 80 percent-plus GPA requirement. English test results at the required level. CV and motivation letter as part of the admission file. Two academic references submitted through the admission system. Passport copy and degree certificates (or expected graduation statement).
summary: The Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarship is TU Delft’s flagship award, covering the full tuition fee…

title: Slovak National Scholarship Programme (NSP)
description: The Slovak National Scholarship Programme funds mobility stays of one to ten months in Slovakia for master’s students,…
details:
The Slovak National Scholarship Programme funds mobility stays of one to ten months in Slovakia for master’s students, PhD candidates, researchers and university teachers from anywhere in the world, with no country restrictions. Master’s-level visitors receive EUR 620 per month and doctoral researchers EUR 1,025.50, comfortable amounts for Slovak living costs, with travel allowances for distant countries.

Applications run twice a year with fixed deadlines of April 30 and October 31, and the key requirement is an invitation letter from a Slovak university or Slovak Academy of Sciences institute. For students wanting a funded European research semester without a massive competition, the NSP is one of the most accessible routes on the continent.
benefits: Monthly scholarship of EUR 620 for master's-level students and EUR 1,025.50 for PhD students and researchers. Freedom to arrange a mobility stay of one to ten months at any accredited Slovak university or SAS research institute. A simple, genuinely worldwide program with no country list, unusual for European government scholarships. Two application rounds every year (late April for winter semester starts, late October for summer semester starts). Central European living costs make the stipend comfortably sufficient in cities like Bratislava and Košice. Travel allowance available for scholarship holders from more distant countries.
requirements: University students from any country invited for a mobility stay at a Slovak university during their master's-level studies. PhD students and doctoral candidates whose home institution is outside Slovakia. University teachers, researchers and artists invited by a Slovak host institution are also covered under separate categories. An official acceptance or invitation letter from the Slovak host university or research institute. The stay must fit within the program's mobility windows and cannot fund a full degree enrolled in Slovakia from the start. Strong academic record and a study or research plan agreed with the Slovak host.
required_documents: Online application at stipendia.sk (scholarships.sk) in Slovak or English. Acceptance or invitation letter from the Slovak host institution for the planned period. Motivation letter and a study or research program for the stay. Two recommendation letters for student applicants (from home-university teachers). Transcript or record of studies and confirmation of current enrolment (or PhD status). CV and passport copy.
summary: The Slovak National Scholarship Programme funds mobility stays of one to ten months in Slovakia for master’s students,…

title: Invest Your Talent in Italy Scholarship (IYT)
university: Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MAECI), ITA & Uni-Italia
description: Invest Your Talent in Italy is the Italian government’s career-focused scholarship, funding English-taught master’s degrees in engineering, economics…
details:
Invest Your Talent in Italy is the Italian government’s career-focused scholarship, funding English-taught master’s degrees in engineering, economics and management, or design and architecture at top Italian universities, with a mandatory internship at an Italian company built into the program. Winners receive about EUR 10,800 across nine months plus a full tuition waiver, with renewal possible for two-year degrees.

Eligibility is limited to 23 countries including Bangladesh, India, Turkey, Egypt, Ghana and Ethiopia (Pakistan and Nigeria are currently not on the list). The 2026 call closed on May 11, and the next edition is expected in spring 2027 on a similar timeline.
benefits: A scholarship of about EUR 10,800 paid over nine months (roughly EUR 1,200 monthly, disbursed quarterly). Full exemption from university tuition fees, apart from small regional taxes and stamp duty. A place on one of 250+ English-taught master's courses at top Italian universities including Politecnico di Milano and Politecnico di Torino. A mandatory internship with an Italian company or trade association built into the program, a rare scholarship-plus-work-experience combination. Italian language and culture study included alongside your degree. Renewal possible for the second year of two-year Laurea Magistrale programs with sufficient credits.
requirements: Citizens and permanent residents of the 23 program countries: Argentina, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Egypt, Ethiopia, Ghana, India, Indonesia, Iran, Kazakhstan, Mexico, Mongolia, Paraguay, Peru, China, Tunisia, Turkey, Uruguay and Vietnam. Note that Pakistan and Nigeria are not on the current country list, so applicants from there should look at the Italian Government MAECI scholarships instead. A qualification valid for enrolment in a participating master's or postgraduate course; current undergraduates are not eligible. English at B2 minimum (a degree taught in English can count as C1 proof). A pre-admission application to one of the English-taught IYT courses in engineering and high technologies, management and economics, or design and architecture. Not currently studying at an Italian university and not holding an Italian degree.
required_documents: Passport and completed online application on the IYT platform. Final transcript with all exams and the bachelor's degree certificate (or completion letter). English language certificate at B2 or above, or university confirmation of English-medium instruction. A one-minute motivation video, a distinctive IYT requirement worth preparing well. CV and reference letters as requested by the platform. Proof of pre-admission application to a participating IYT course.
summary: Invest Your Talent in Italy is the Italian government’s career-focused scholarship, funding English-taught master’s degrees in engineering, economics…

title: Griffith Remarkable Scholarship (Australia)
description: The Griffith Remarkable Scholarship halves tuition fees for high-achieving international students across the full length of undergraduate and…
details:
The Griffith Remarkable Scholarship halves tuition fees for high-achieving international students across the full length of undergraduate and postgraduate coursework degrees at Griffith University in Queensland, Australia. The 50 percent deduction is applied to fee invoices every trimester, from business and IT to engineering, health and design.

Applicants need a GPA of at least 5.5 on Griffith’s 7-point scale, a Letter of Offer and a personal statement written in their own words, and Griffith’s Gold Coast campus counts as regional Australia for post-study visa advantages. Rounds close before each trimester; the Trimester 1, 2027 round is expected to close around late November 2026.
benefits: 50 percent reduction of tuition fees for the standard length of the degree, deducted before each trimester's census date. Applies across Griffith's coursework portfolio: business, IT, engineering, health, design, environment and more. Griffith's Gold Coast and other campuses sit in areas classed as regional Australia, which can improve post-study work visa options. Unsuccessful candidates are typically considered for Griffith's 25 percent Academic Excellence and 20 percent Academic Merit scholarships. Three intakes per year (trimesters) give flexible timing for planning. A well-established award at a top-2-percent world university with strong industry placement culture.
requirements: Citizens of any country other than Australia or New Zealand applying for full-time undergraduate or postgraduate coursework study at Griffith University. Minimum GPA of 5.5 on Griffith's 7-point scale (or equivalent) in previous studies; competition means stronger records win. An application to study at Griffith submitted by the scholarship closing date, meeting all academic and English entry requirements for the chosen programme. Excludes research degrees, online-campus programmes, non-award study, the Masters Qualifying Program, the MBA and offshore partner-delivered programmes. A personal statement of 250 to 500 words in your own words is a core part of the assessment. Award numbers are limited each trimester and close once filled, so early applications matter. Recipients must stay in the same programme, remain full-time and keep a cumulative GPA of 5.5 to hold every trimester's deduction.
required_documents: Griffith admission application resulting in a Letter of Offer for your programme. Online scholarship application submitted by the closing date for your commencing trimester. Academic records and transcripts for all prior study. Personal statement of 250 to 500 words on why Griffith, your achievements and your ambassador potential. Evidence of English proficiency per programme requirements. Passport copy as proof of citizenship.
summary: The Griffith Remarkable Scholarship halves tuition fees for high-achieving international students across the full length of undergraduate and…

title: Zawadi Africa Education Fund Scholarship (Women)
description: The Zawadi Africa Education Fund provides full university scholarship placements for academically gifted young women from Africa who…
details:
The Zawadi Africa Education Fund provides full university scholarship placements for academically gifted young women from Africa who come from financially disadvantaged backgrounds, with study destinations across the USA, Kenya, Uganda, Ghana and South Africa. Modeled on the historic Kennedy-Mboya airlifts, it has built a sisterhood of African women leaders since 2002.

Rather than a fixed cash award, Zawadi runs a nine-month preparation program of test coaching, essay support and leadership training, then places scholars into full scholarships at partner universities. Top national exam results, leadership and resilience drive selection, and applying is completely free. The annual window opens each February; Kenya’s 2026 round closed March 16.
benefits: Placement into full scholarships at partner universities in the USA and across Africa rather than a fixed cash award, following the model of the historic Kennedy-Mboya airlifts. Nine months of intensive coaching: standardized test preparation, application and essay support, and interview readiness. Leadership development and life-skills training that continues through university, building a pipeline of African women leaders. Mentorship and a sisterhood network of Zawadi scholars and alumnae across the continent and the diaspora since 2002. Support with travel and transition for scholars placed abroad. An each-one-teach-one culture in which scholars give back to the next cohorts.
requirements: Young women from Africa, with active application offices in Kenya, Uganda and Ghana; study placements span the USA, Kenya, Uganda, Ghana and South Africa. Completed secondary school within roughly the last two years with top national examination results (for Kenya, an A or A- in KCSE; equivalent top grades elsewhere). Demonstrated leadership in school, community, faith settings or peer activities. Coming from a financially disadvantaged background, with need verified in the application. Resilience matters: the fund explicitly looks for young women who achieved excellence despite serious hardship such as poverty or harmful socio-cultural practices. Willingness to commit to a rigorous nine-month preparation programme before university applications. The programme is completely free; anyone asking for payment is a fraudster.
required_documents: Online or downloadable application form from the Zawadi Africa website during the annual window. Biography and passport photograph. Academic certificates and transcripts, including national examination results. Recommendation letter and identification documents. Personal essay of about 500 to 650 words telling your story, leadership and goals. List of activities, honours and community service.
summary: The Zawadi Africa Education Fund provides full university scholarship placements for academically gifted young women from Africa who…

title: Politecnico di Torino TOPoliTO Scholarship (Italy)
description: The TOPoliTO Scholarship at Politecnico di Torino awards EUR 8,000 per academic year to top international students joining…
details:
The TOPoliTO Scholarship at Politecnico di Torino awards EUR 8,000 per academic year to top international students joining bachelor’s and master’s programs at one of Europe’s oldest technical universities, in Turin, Italy. Combined with Italy’s comparatively low tuition and income-based fee reductions, it covers a large share of total study costs.

The scholarship is open to students with foreign qualifications who have already been admitted through the Apply@polito portal, across engineering and architecture, with many English-taught master’s tracks. Annual calls have recently closed around July and August for the following academic year, and admitted students can also pursue Italian government MAECI grants in parallel.
benefits: Gross scholarship of EUR 8,000 per academic year for the standard duration of the degree (two years for a master's). Study at one of Europe's oldest technical universities, in Turin's strong industrial and automotive ecosystem. Combined with Italy's comparatively low tuition (and income-based fee reductions), the award covers a large share of study costs. English-taught master's options across engineering fields plus architecture and design. International admits can also compete for Italy's MAECI government grants and regional right-to-study support in parallel. Turin's living costs are moderate for Western Europe, stretching the scholarship further.
requirements: International students holding a qualification obtained outside Italy: a foreign secondary diploma for the bachelor's track or a foreign bachelor's degree for the master's track. Admission first: TOPoliTO applications can only be submitted by students already admitted to a Politecnico di Torino programme through the Apply@polito portal. Programmes span the university's Engineering and Architecture offer, including many English-taught master's tracks. Meeting the academic and language requirements of the chosen programme (English or Italian per track). Selection is merit-based on the admission ranking and application file; award numbers are small (recent master's rounds offered around eight scholarships split between engineering and architecture). Renewal across the programme years requires regular academic progress. Holders should check compatibility rules before stacking with other Italian aid such as regional EDISU grants.
required_documents: Apply@polito account with a completed admission application and evaluation outcome. TOPoliTO scholarship application submitted through the portal during the call window. Academic transcripts and diploma (secondary school or bachelor's) with translations where required. English or Italian language certificates per the programme. Passport or identity document. Any call-specific forms listed in the published TOPoliTO call.
summary: The TOPoliTO Scholarship at Politecnico di Torino awards EUR 8,000 per academic year to top international students joining…

title: Université de Montréal Exemption Scholarship (Canada)
description: The Université de Montréal Exemption Scholarship automatically reduces international tuition for admitted students at Canada’s leading francophone research…
details:
The Université de Montréal Exemption Scholarship automatically reduces international tuition for admitted students at Canada’s leading francophone research university, with no scholarship application at all. Undergraduate awards reach about CAD 13,740 per year, graduate awards range up to full exemption to the Quebec rate, worth about CAD 22,900 per year for the strongest files.

Every eligible admitted international student is assessed on academic record alone, and the award letter arrives shortly after you accept admission, renewing across the whole programme with full-time study. Most programs are taught in French. Apply for the autumn 2027 intake by February 1, 2027 (September 1, 2026 for the winter intake).
benefits: Substantial reduction of the international tuition supplement for the entire length of the programme, applied directly against tuition bills. Top graduate files pay the same tuition as Quebec students, one of the lowest rates in North America. No scholarship paperwork at all: the admission file is the scholarship file, and the award letter arrives by email shortly after you accept admission. Stackable with UdeM's graduate funding, assistantships and external awards. Study at Canada's leading francophone research university, with over 10,000 international students in Montreal. Montreal's relatively low living costs and post-graduation work permit pathways add to the value.
requirements: International students admitted to a full-time degree programme (bachelor's, master's or PhD) at Université de Montréal; French and French-speaking Belgian citizens are excluded because they already pay Quebec rates. Not applicable to independent studies, certificates, minors, short programmes or preparatory-year study. Automatic evaluation: every eligible admitted candidate is assessed, and the strength of your academic record on the transcripts in your admission file is the only criterion. Undergraduate awards come in two levels (Level A about CAD 13,740 per year; Level B about CAD 6,548 per year), and files below Level B receive no award. Graduate students receive partial exemptions (about CAD 15,150 per year for research programmes; about CAD 10,789 for non-research), with full exemptions to the Quebec rate for the strongest files. Holding valid study authorizations (CAQ and study permit) for every session, staying continuously enrolled full time, and not combining with another tuition exemption. Most programmes are taught in French, so French proficiency is required for admission to the majority of degrees.
required_documents: Admission application submitted through the UdeM admission portal with all programme documents. Official transcripts for all previous studies, since these alone determine the exemption level. Degree certificates and identity documents per the admission checklist. Proof of French proficiency for French-taught programmes (some graduate programmes accept English evidence). After admission: CAQ (Quebec acceptance certificate) and Canadian study permit for every session. No separate scholarship form exists.
summary: The Université de Montréal Exemption Scholarship automatically reduces international tuition for admitted students at Canada’s leading francophone research…

title: Tampere University Scholarships (Finland)
description: Tampere University Scholarships cut the cost of English-taught bachelor’s and master’s degrees in Finland’s second-largest student city. The…
details:
Tampere University Scholarships cut the cost of English-taught bachelor’s and master’s degrees in Finland’s second-largest student city. The tuition fee scholarship covers 50 percent of fees for the whole programme, while the national Finland Scholarship gives the most merited new master’s students their entire first-year tuition plus a EUR 5,000 relocation grant.

You apply for the scholarships inside the admission application itself on Studyinfo.fi, with no separate portal or fee, and early bird and graduation discounts soften costs further for others. For studies starting autumn 2027, the application window runs December 14, 2026 to January 7, 2027, so prepare documents before the holidays.
benefits: Tampere University tuition fee scholarship covering 50 percent of the tuition fee for the standard programme duration (three years bachelor's, two years master's). Finland Scholarship for new master's students: the full first-year tuition fee plus a EUR 5,000 relocation grant paid to your Finnish bank account. Early bird offer of EUR 2,000 off the first-year fee for admitted fee-paying students without the main scholarship who confirm within two weeks. Graduation scholarship: Tampere bachelor's graduates who finish within three years get EUR 2,000 off their first master's year at Tampere. Study in Finland's second-largest student city with strong programmes in technology, health and society. Note: living costs (about EUR 800 to 1,200 per month) are not covered, so budget beyond the waiver.
requirements: Citizens of countries outside the EU, EEA and Switzerland who are liable to pay tuition fees (EUR 10,000 to 12,000 per year) in English-taught bachelor's or master's programmes at Tampere University. Admission to the chosen programme through Finland's national Studyinfo.fi application service; the scholarship is applied for inside the admission application, not separately. Merit-based selection: only a limited number of highly qualified applicants receive the tuition fee scholarship, and Finland Scholarships go to the most merited master's applicant per programme. Bachelor's scholarship applicants write a scholarship application letter (up to 3,000 characters); master's applicants add a short academic merit summary in the motivation letter. Students in joint or Erasmus Mundus programmes and transfer or open-university routes are not eligible. Continuation of the fee scholarship requires normal study progress (completing the required credits each year). Students not awarded the main scholarship can still take the early bird reduction by accepting their place and paying quickly.
required_documents: Admission application on Studyinfo.fi during the national application window. Scholarship section completed inside the same application (letter for bachelor's applicants; merit summary for master's applicants). Degree certificates and transcripts per programme requirements, with certified copies posted after admission. English proficiency evidence accepted by the programme. Programme-specific items such as SAT results for some science and engineering bachelor's tracks. No separate scholarship portal or fee applies.
summary: Tampere University Scholarships cut the cost of English-taught bachelor’s and master’s degrees in Finland’s second-largest student city. The…

title: Deakin Vice-Chancellor’s International Scholarship (Australia)
description: The Deakin Vice-Chancellor’s International Scholarship is one of Australia’s strongest university awards, waiving 100 percent of tuition for…
details:
The Deakin Vice-Chancellor’s International Scholarship is one of Australia’s strongest university awards, waiving 100 percent of tuition for the very top international applicants and 50 percent for the remaining awardees, across the full length of a bachelor’s or master’s coursework degree at Deakin University in Victoria.

Candidates need roughly an 85 percent academic average, a genuine personal statement and evidence of leadership, and scholars join the Vice-Chancellor’s Professional Excellence Program with priority access to campus housing. Applications are assessed on a rolling basis before each trimester (March, July and November intakes), and unsuccessful candidates are automatically considered for the 25 percent Deakin International Scholarship.
funding_type: Partial to Fully Funded (up to 100% tuition)
benefits: 100 percent tuition waiver for the very top candidates, or 50 percent for the remaining awardees, applied every trimester for the standard length of the degree. Participation in the Vice-Chancellor's Professional Excellence Program, a structured leadership and employability track exclusive to these scholars. Priority access to on-campus accommodation (paid at your own cost, subject to availability). Automatic consideration for the 25 percent Deakin International Scholarship if you are not selected, so one application covers both. Study at a large Victorian university with strong industry links across Melbourne, Geelong and Warrnambool campuses. Geelong and Warrnambool count as regional Australia, which can add post-study visa advantages.
requirements: International students (citizens of countries other than Australia or New Zealand) starting an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree at Deakin University. Academic benchmark of about 85 percent average (or equivalent) in previous studies, for example 80 percent across the first four semesters of a bachelor's for postgraduate applicants; competition often pushes successful scores higher. Meeting Deakin's English requirements (around IELTS 6.0 for undergraduate and 6.5 for postgraduate programmes). New commencing students only, and not holders of another Deakin scholarship or bursary. The Doctor of Medicine programme is excluded, as are research degrees (which use Deakin's HDR scholarships instead). A personal statement in your own voice and evidence of leadership and community involvement carry real weight in selection. Recipients must join the Vice-Chancellor's Professional Excellence Program and maintain strong results to keep the waiver.
required_documents: Deakin course application submitted first, so you hold (or are processing) a Letter of Offer. Completed Deakin International Scholarship Program application form (PDF) emailed to Deakin International Admissions. Personal statement of about 300 words on why Deakin, your activities and why you would be a strong ambassador. Two references highlighting community involvement and leadership. Academic transcripts for all previous study. Evidence of extracurriculars or work experience where available; an interview may follow.
summary: The Deakin Vice-Chancellor’s International Scholarship is one of Australia’s strongest university awards, waiving 100 percent of tuition for…

title: DAAD Leadership for Africa Scholarship (Germany)
description: The DAAD Leadership for Africa Scholarship funds master’s degrees in Germany for young graduates and refugees from selected…
details:
The DAAD Leadership for Africa Scholarship funds master’s degrees in Germany for young graduates and refugees from selected African countries, backed by the German Federal Foreign Office. Scholars receive a monthly stipend of about EUR 934 plus insurance at tuition-free German universities, along with up to six months of funded German language training, rent subsidy and family allowances.

Each annual call names its target countries (recent cycles covered South Sudan, Uganda, Cameroon, Senegal and Togo) and reserves places for recognized refugees hosted there. Almost all fields qualify except medicine, law and a few regulated professions. Calls typically open in April and close by mid-June for the following winter intake.
benefits: Monthly DAAD stipend (around EUR 934) plus health, accident and liability insurance for the full master's. Study at tuition-free public or state-recognized German universities, so the stipend goes to living costs. Up to six months of funded German language training in Germany before the degree starts, including test fees, pocket money and accommodation during the course. Rent subsidy and monthly allowances for accompanying spouse and children where applicable. Membership of the LEAD! network, which regularly brings Leadership for Africa scholars together for leadership training. Funded by the German Federal Foreign Office and running since 2021 with dedicated slots for refugees.
requirements: Nationals of the year's target countries and refugees hosted in them; recent calls covered South Sudan and Uganda (East Africa) and Cameroon, Senegal and Togo (West and Central Africa), with country lists announced before each call. Refugee applicants must hold formally granted refugee status in the host country by the cutoff date stated in the call. Bachelor's degree completed with strong results, qualifying for master's admission in Germany. All fields are eligible except Medicine, Veterinary Medicine, Dentistry, Law, Fine Arts, Architecture and health-care fields like Nursing and Midwifery. A convincing study plan: the main selection criterion is your description of the planned studies and a suitable choice of programmes in the DAAD study-course profile form. Language evidence for the chosen programmes (TOEFL or IELTS for English-taught, TestDaF or DSH for German-taught), or proof you can reach the level through the funded German course. Leadership motivation, since the programme exists to educate future leaders for African societies.
required_documents: DAAD portal application submitted online during the call window (no other channels are accepted). DAAD application form and the study-course profile form naming your chosen master's programmes. Curriculum vitae and a motivation letter. Bachelor's degree certificate and transcripts, translated into English or German where needed. Language certificates for the chosen programmes, or proof supporting your ability to reach them. Refugee applicants add proof of refugee status; optional extras include employment certificates, recommendation letters and prior German admissions.
summary: The DAAD Leadership for Africa Scholarship funds master’s degrees in Germany for young graduates and refugees from selected…

title: University of Macau International Student Scholarship
description: The University of Macau International Student Scholarship waives both tuition and on-campus accommodation fees for the normal length…
details:
The University of Macau International Student Scholarship waives both tuition and on-campus accommodation fees for the normal length of a bachelor’s or master’s degree, a substantial package in one of Asia’s fastest-rising universities. Awards renew each year on satisfactory performance, and consideration happens alongside admission with no heavy separate dossier.

The scheme targets international students educated outside China, with priority for applicants from UM’s strategic partner countries, and pairs English-medium teaching with a residential college system in the Greater Bay Area. Admission rounds for 2027 entry are expected to close around March 13, 2027, and PhD candidates should apply instead for the UM Macao PhD Scholarship.
benefits: Waiver of tuition fees for the normal period of the degree (four to five years for bachelor's, two years for master's). Waiver of on-campus accommodation fees for the same period, a major saving in Macao. Automatic or simple consideration alongside admission, with no heavy separate scholarship dossier at most intakes. Study at a fast-rising research university (top 200 globally in recent rankings) with English-medium teaching and a residential college system. Macao's location in the Greater Bay Area adds internship and career exposure across Macao, Hong Kong and Guangdong. High-performing students can stack university academic prizes and donor scholarships on top.
requirements: International applicants to full-time bachelor's or master's degree programmes at the University of Macau; applicants originally from mainland China, Macao, Hong Kong or Taiwan are not counted as international for this scheme. Executive degree programmes and admission through the Macao four-institution joint examination are excluded. Meeting the admission requirements of the chosen programme; the scholarship is competitive on top of admission. Selection criteria include academic excellence, research ability or potential, and communication and interpersonal skills, with recommendations from the academic unit. Priority to applicants educated outside China (at primary, secondary or higher level) and to applicants from UM's strategic partner countries. Continuation each year depends on an annual review of satisfactory academic performance. PhD applicants should look instead at the separate UM Macao PhD Scholarship (MPDS), which funds doctoral students with a monthly stipend.
required_documents: University of Macau admission application submitted online for your bachelor's or master's programme. Academic transcripts and certificates (secondary results for bachelor's; degree documents for master's). English proficiency evidence per programme requirements. CV, personal statement and references where the programme requests them. Scholarship indication through the Global Affairs Office channel where the application asks for it. Passport or identity documents.
summary: The University of Macau International Student Scholarship waives both tuition and on-campus accommodation fees for the normal length…

title: JDS Scholarship (Japan, Project for Human Resource Development)
description: The JDS Scholarship (the Project for Human Resource Development Scholarship by Japanese Grant Aid) sends young government officials…
details:
The JDS Scholarship (the Project for Human Resource Development Scholarship by Japanese Grant Aid) sends young government officials and professionals from 28 partner countries to Japan for fully funded English-taught master’s and PhD degrees. It covers full tuition, a monthly living allowance sufficient for Japan, round-trip flights and arrival support.

Partner countries include Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, the Philippines, Mongolia, Ghana, Kenya, Senegal, India and the Central Asian republics, with each national JDS office running its own quota, priority fields and schedule. Fellows have risen to deputy minister and ambassador level back home. Most national windows close between October and December 2026, so contact your JDS office now.
benefits: Full tuition at the host Japanese university, paid by the programme. Monthly allowance sufficient for living costs in Japan for the two-year master's (three-year PhD). Round-trip air tickets and other transportation, arranged and provided by JDS.
