Arrival orientation, settling-in support and research-related cost coverage, including study trips where the programme provides them. Small, well-supported national cohorts (for example six fellows per year from Fiji) with close follow-up from the JDS office. A powerful alumni track record: returned fellows have risen to deputy minister and ambassador levels across partner countries.
requirements: Highly capable young officials, mainly from government, in the 28 JDS partner countries, including Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, the Philippines, Mongolia, Kyrgyz Republic, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Laos, Cambodia, Ghana, Kenya, Senegal, Mozambique, India, Fiji, Papua New Guinea and others. Each country's JDS project sets its own age range, target organizations, priority fields and quota through a bilateral steering committee. Bachelor's degree with a solid record for the master's track; the PhD track is mainly open to returned JDS master's alumni. English-taught programmes, so working English is required; courses are hosted at strong Japanese universities such as IUJ, GRIPS, Meiji, Hiroshima, Ritsumeikan APU and others. Official nomination or endorsement from your employing organization is required in most countries, and public-sector applicants dominate the intake. Applicants may not hold another scholarship at the same time. Commitment to return and apply the skills in your country's development administration is central to selection.
required_documents: Country-specific application kit obtained from your national JDS project office (paper or online via the TAO system where offered). Official nomination or consent from your employing organization, often routed through the responsible ministry. Academic certificates and transcripts with English translations. Confidential reference statement from your supervisor on the official form. Research or study plan matched to your country's priority fields. English evidence and identity documents as listed in your country's guidelines.
summary: The JDS Scholarship (the Project for Human Resource Development Scholarship by Japanese Grant Aid) sends young government officials…

title: Islamic University of Madinah Scholarship (Saudi Arabia)
description: The Islamic University of Madinah Scholarship gives international Muslim students a fully funded seat in the city of…
details:
The Islamic University of Madinah Scholarship gives international Muslim students a fully funded seat in the city of the Prophet’s Mosque, Saudi Arabia. The package includes tuition-free study, a monthly allowance, free furnished housing for unmarried students, healthcare, subsidized meals, an arrival flight and a free return ticket home every academic year.

Undergraduate seats are currently offered to male applicants aged 17 to 25, while postgraduate windows cover master’s and doctoral study; programs span Sharia, Qur’an, Hadith, Arabic language and modern science and engineering faculties, mostly taught in Arabic with a language institute pathway for newcomers. Applications are free and windows open per intake throughout the year on the university portal.
benefits: Tuition-free study seat granted by the Saudi government for the full programme. Monthly allowance, plus an extra allowance for students who achieve the grade of excellence. Free furnished accommodation for unmarried students and quality healthcare at the university hospital. Flight on admission and a free return ticket at the end of each academic year under the university's guidelines. Subsidized meals at the university restaurant, free daily transport to and from the Prophet's Mosque, and organized Umrah trips. Study in Madinah with access to the university's academic, sports and social facilities and a large international student community.
requirements: Muslim students of good conduct from outside Saudi Arabia; the university's external scholarship seats are granted by the Saudi government to non-Saudi students residing abroad. Undergraduate applicants: male students aged 17 to 25 with a secondary school certificate (12 years of education) no more than five years old and strong grades (about 80 percent or higher is competitive). Master's applicants: bachelor's degree (16 years of education) with a very good average (about 3.75 out of 5); the university requests aptitude evidence such as the QIYAS test for Gulf applicants or a GRE quantitative score for others, and a recent degree. Arabic is the language of instruction for most programmes, so Arabic proficiency matters; the university runs an Arabic language institute pathway for admitted students who need it. Medically fit and able to abide by the university's rules and Saudi regulations. Fields span Sharia, Qur'an, Dawah, Hadith, Arabic language, and science and engineering faculties on the modern campus. All application documents must be in Arabic or English (or officially translated).
required_documents: Online application through the university's admission portal for international students. Educational certificates and transcripts (secondary certificate for undergraduate; degree and transcript for postgraduate). Birth certificate or national ID, and passport where available. Testimony of good conduct (character certificate). Medical report. Recommendation letter, with all documents in Arabic or English; admitted students later present originals attested by the Saudi Embassy or a recognized authority.
summary: The Islamic University of Madinah Scholarship gives international Muslim students a fully funded seat in the city of…

title: PTDF Overseas Scholarship Scheme (Nigeria)
description: The PTDF Overseas Scholarship Scheme is Nigeria’s flagship government scholarship for postgraduate study abroad, funded by the Petroleum…
details:
The PTDF Overseas Scholarship Scheme is Nigeria’s flagship government scholarship for postgraduate study abroad, funded by the Petroleum Technology Development Fund. It fully funds MSc study in the United Kingdom, Germany, France and Malaysia and PhD study in Germany, France and Malaysia (with a UK split-site doctoral track), covering tuition, living allowances, flights and health insurance.

Fields span petroleum, chemical, mechanical and electrical engineering, geosciences, computer science and cyber security, renewables and energy management. Applicants need a strong first degree, an NYSC certificate and a verified NIN, and selection balances candidates across all 36 states and the FCT. The annual advert opens on the PTDF portal early each year; the 2026 round closed February 27.
benefits: Full tuition and bench fees at partner universities abroad, paid by the Fund. Allowances covering accommodation and living expenses for the duration of the programme. Return flight tickets and health insurance. Placement within structured partnerships, including the PTDF/DAAD track in Germany and named UK, French and Malaysian partner institutions. Selection balanced across Nigeria's 36 states and the FCT, giving strong candidates from every state a fair path. One of Nigeria's most established government scholarship pipelines for the energy sector, with thousands of alumni.
requirements: Nigerian citizens with strong academic records applying for postgraduate study relevant to the oil, gas and energy sector. MSc track: study at partner universities in the United Kingdom, Germany, France and Malaysia, normally requiring a Second Class Upper degree (a Second Class Lower with solid industry experience can be considered). PhD track: Germany, France and Malaysia, while the UK PhD now runs as a split-site programme anchored at the PTDF College of Petroleum and Energy Studies in Kaduna with UK partner universities. Relevant fields are broad: petroleum, chemical, mechanical, electrical and civil engineering, geosciences, computer science and cyber security, renewable energy and environment, plus management fields such as law, accounting and economics. NYSC discharge or exemption certificate, a verified National Identity Number, and a course of study consistent with your academic background. PhD applicants submit a research proposal of up to six pages, and those targeting the PTDF/DAAD Germany route must secure a supervisor before final interviews. One application only; previous PTDF scholars cannot reapply for the same or a lower level, and current beneficiaries of other scholarships are excluded.
required_documents: Online application through the PTDF Scholarship Management Portal (scholarship.ptdf.gov.ng) after NIN verification. First degree certificate or statement of results and full transcripts. NYSC certificate or exemption letter. WAEC, GCE, SSCE or NECO results and your admission letter where already obtained. Statement of purpose (undergraduate and MSc applicants) explaining the industry relevance and national impact of your study. PhD applicants add the second degree certificate and the six-page research proposal on a listed research area, plus certificate of state of origin matching your other documents.
summary: The PTDF Overseas Scholarship Scheme is Nigeria’s flagship government scholarship for postgraduate study abroad, funded by the Petroleum…

title: British Council Scholarships for Women in STEM (UK)
description: The British Council Scholarships for Women in STEM fund one-year master’s degrees at leading UK universities for women…
details:
The British Council Scholarships for Women in STEM fund one-year master’s degrees at leading UK universities for women from around 30 eligible countries, including Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Nepal. Each award is worth at least GBP 40,000 and covers tuition, a living stipend, travel, the visa fee, the health surcharge and English support.

The program targets women from disadvantaged backgrounds who will return home as visible role models in science, technology, engineering and mathematics, and it has placed about 500 scholars with 43 UK universities so far. Applications go directly to each partner university, with the 2027-28 round expected to open in early 2027 and university deadlines falling around February to April 2027.
benefits: Fully funded one-year STEM master's at a leading UK university, with each award worth a minimum of GBP 40,000. Tuition fees, monthly living stipend, travel costs, visa fee and the Immigration Health Surcharge all covered. English language support, including IELTS costs at several partner universities. Around 90 scholarships per cycle across roughly 30 countries; the programme has awarded about 500 scholarships with 43 UK universities since it began. Access to the UK's research-intensive STEM departments and the British Council alumni network. An explicit mission focus: scholars return as visible role models for women and girls in science.
requirements: Women (as defined under UK legislation) from eligible countries and territories announced each cycle; recent cycles covered around 30 countries across South Asia (including Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Nepal), Southeast Asia, the Americas and other regions. Passport holder and permanent resident of an eligible country, able to obtain a UK student visa. Bachelor's degree completed, meeting the entry requirements of the chosen UK master's, including academic equivalencies and English (IELTS is often not required at the application stage). Demonstrated financial need: the programme targets women from socioeconomically disadvantaged contexts who could not otherwise study in the UK. Active engagement or work experience in a STEM field, with a plan and passion to engage other women and girls in STEM at home. No previous UK degree or recent UK residence, and dual British citizens are not eligible. Commitment to return to your home country for at least two years after the scholarship.
required_documents: Direct application to each chosen partner university's eligible master's course through its own portal. British Council Women in STEM application form uploaded with the university application where the university requires it. Academic transcripts and degree certificate. Personal statement covering financial need, STEM engagement and plans to champion women and girls in STEM. References per the university's requirements. English test results by the university's condition deadline (often around August 1) rather than at application.
summary: The British Council Scholarships for Women in STEM fund one-year master’s degrees at leading UK universities for women…

title: Malaysia MTCP Scholarship (Malaysian Technical Cooperation Programme)
description: The Malaysia MTCP Scholarship, run by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs under the Malaysian Technical Cooperation Programme, fully…
details:
The Malaysia MTCP Scholarship, run by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs under the Malaysian Technical Cooperation Programme, fully funds master’s degrees at Malaysian public universities for citizens of developing countries, including Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal and much of Africa and Southeast Asia. It pays full tuition directly to the university, a monthly living allowance and a return flight.

Applicants must be under 45 with a strong bachelor’s degree (CGPA around 3.5 of 4) and, crucially, an admission offer from a listed Malaysian university before applying. Priority fields include ICT, STEM, trade, food security, Islamic finance and public administration. The annual window typically runs to mid-June; plan for a June 12, 2027 style deadline for the next round.
benefits: Full tuition fees for the master's, paid directly to the host university for 24 to 36 months. Monthly living allowance deposited to your Malaysian bank account throughout the approved study period. One return economy flight from your nearest international airport to Malaysia and back after completion. Choice of coursework, mixed-mode or research master's at more than 20 Malaysian universities, including UM, UKM, USM, UPM, UTM and IIUM. Membership of a South-South cooperation alumni network running since 1980. Note: visa fees, the pre-departure medical examination and health insurance are the scholar's own responsibility.
requirements: Citizens of MTCP recipient countries across Asia (including Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Afghanistan and Nepal), Africa, the Middle East, Latin America, the Caribbean and the Pacific. Under 45 years of age at the time of application. Bachelor's degree with at least Second Class Upper honours or a CGPA of 3.5 out of 4 (or equivalent). Holding a valid admission offer from at least one listed Malaysian university (mainly public universities) for a full-time master's, and not having completed more than one semester if already registered. Proof of English proficiency (IELTS, TOEFL, PTE, MUET or an official letter confirming English-medium instruction in your last degree). Priority fields include ICT, economy and trade, STEM, food security and agritech, Islamic finance, law, public administration and sustainability; nursing, medicine and clinical pharmacy are excluded. Excellent certified health, with the medical check-up at your own cost.
required_documents: Online application through the official MTCP portal (mtcp.kln.gov.my/scholarship). Valid full admission offer letter from a listed Malaysian university for the target intake. Two recommendation letters using the MTCP template. Statement of intent describing your study plan and its value to your home country. Certified academic transcripts and degree certificates, with an official explanation of your grading system. English proficiency certificate or official English-medium letter, CV, passport copy (12+ months validity) and the MTCP-template medical report.
summary: The Malaysia MTCP Scholarship, run by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs under the Malaysian Technical Cooperation Programme, fully…

title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at University of Pretoria
description: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Pretoria fully funds undergraduate, honours and master’s study at…
details:
The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Pretoria fully funds undergraduate, honours and master’s study at one of Africa’s leading research universities in South Africa. Scholars receive tuition, accommodation, a monthly stipend, book and supply allowances and medical aid, plus mentoring, psychosocial support, internships and leadership training.

The program is built for academically talented Africans facing economic barriers, with deliberate inclusion of young people with disabilities and refugees or displaced persons. Admission to an eligible UP program comes first, then the scholarship application. Windows run annually around the middle of the year, with the next expected to close around June 30, 2027 for the following January intake.
benefits: Full tuition and fees at one of Africa's leading research universities, running since 2014 and expanded under Phase 2 from 2024. Accommodation, a monthly stipend, and allowances for books, supplies and printed materials. Medical aid cover and travel support. Comprehensive wraparound support: mentoring, psychosocial support, leadership development, internships and entrepreneurship training. Membership of the pan-African Mastercard Foundation Scholars community and its alumni network. A transition focus that helps scholars move into work or further study that benefits their home communities.
requirements: Citizens of African countries who are academically talented but face economic and social barriers, including young people living with disabilities and refugees or internally displaced persons. Admission first: you must apply to and be accepted into an eligible full-time programme at the University of Pretoria before the scholarship application proceeds. Undergraduate track: applying for a first bachelor's degree with a grade average around 70 percent or higher and no prior degree. Postgraduate track: entering the first year of an honours or master's programme with at least 70 percent, and not already holding a master's. Eligible programmes span several faculties, including Natural and Agricultural Sciences, Engineering, Economic and Management Sciences, and Humanities; extended and non-degree programmes are excluded. Demonstrated leadership, community involvement and commitment to Africa's transformation. Community service, internships and entrepreneurship activities are built into the programme, so willingness to participate is required.
required_documents: University of Pretoria admission application via the UP online portal (a UP student number is required before the scholarship step). Official Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program application form for your level (undergraduate or postgraduate) with all supporting documents. Academic transcripts and certificates showing results around 70 percent or above. Proof of financial need and family circumstances. Evidence of leadership and community engagement, plus personal statements. Identity or refugee documentation, and a passport for international scholars to allow prompt visa processing.
summary: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Pretoria fully funds undergraduate, honours and master’s study at…

title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Ashesi University
description: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Ashesi University offers fully funded undergraduate study at one of Africa’s most…
details:
The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Ashesi University offers fully funded undergraduate study at one of Africa’s most respected universities, in Ghana. The award covers tuition and fees, room and board, learning resources including a laptop, stipends and travel, wrapped in mentoring and leadership development throughout the degree.

Ashesi was one of the Foundation’s nine pioneering partners in 2012, and scholars can even join the accelerated pathway that adds an Arizona State University master’s within about five years. Selection targets academically excellent young Africans with financial need and leadership spirit. Apply for admission and financial aid together; the main 2027-intake deadline is reported for November 16, 2026.
benefits: One of Ashesi's most comprehensive packages: tuition and all fees, accommodation and meals, plus learning resources including a laptop. Stipends and travel support so that finances never interrupt the degree. Socio-economic transition support, mentoring and leadership development woven through the scholar experience. Access to the Ashesi-Arizona State University accelerated pathway, letting scholars finish a bachelor's plus a master's in about five years. Membership of the continent-wide Mastercard Foundation Scholars network and Ashesi's alumni community across 40+ countries. Study at one of Africa's most respected liberal-arts and engineering universities, known for its honour code and ethics-centred education.
requirements: Academically talented young people from African countries who face financial barriers to university; Ashesi was one of the nine pioneering Mastercard Foundation partners in 2012. Applying for admission to an undergraduate programme at Ashesi University in Ghana (business administration, computer science, engineering, and related fields). Strong secondary school results and evidence of leadership and community involvement. Demonstrated financial need through Ashesi's general financial aid application. Commitment to giving back: scholars are expected to serve as role models and engage in community service during and after their studies. Refugee and displaced students can request an application fee waiver by contacting the admissions office. You do not choose this scholarship directly; the Admissions and Financial Aid Office assigns the most suitable award, including the Mastercard Foundation award, based on your file.
required_documents: Ashesi University admission application submitted online for the intended intake. Secondary school transcripts and national examination results (for example WASSCE). Ashesi financial aid and scholarship application with honest details of family finances. Essays and recommendation letters as required by the admission form. Evidence of leadership and community activities. Refugee applicants: an email to the admissions office requesting the fee waiver questionnaire.
summary: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Ashesi University offers fully funded undergraduate study at one of Africa’s most…

title: EducationUSA Opportunity Funds Program (OFP)
description: The EducationUSA Opportunity Funds Program (OFP) tackles the hidden barrier to studying in the United States: the up-front…
details:
The EducationUSA Opportunity Funds Program (OFP) tackles the hidden barrier to studying in the United States: the up-front cost of applying. Run by EducationUSA advising centres at US embassies, it pays for standardized tests, up to eight university application fees, translations, the visa and SEVIS fees, airfare and a settling-in allowance for high-achieving, low-income students.

OFP does not pay tuition. Instead, its advisers coach you through a full application cycle aimed at winning complete financial aid from US universities themselves, and cohorts regularly land full rides at selective institutions. Each country’s centre runs its own annual call, so find your local EducationUSA office and ask when the next window opens.
benefits: Payment of standardized test costs (TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo, plus SAT or GRE where needed), including logistics and score reports. US university application fees covered, typically for up to eight institutions, plus document translation costs. Student visa fee, SEVIS fee, airfare to the US and a one-time settling-in allowance once you win a funded place. Intensive, personalized advising from EducationUSA counselors through every stage, modeled on how US admissions offices think. A strong track record: cohorts routinely place students at highly selective universities with full financial aid packages. Participants become US government exchange alumni with access to alumni grants and networks.
requirements: High-achieving, low-income students who are strong candidates for full financial aid at US colleges and universities but cannot afford the up-front costs of applying. Offered country by country through EducationUSA advising centres at US embassies; each country's call sets its own level (undergraduate, graduate or both) and dates. Top-of-class academic record; undergraduate calls typically target final-year secondary students or very recent graduates who have not started university. Strong English ability, leadership and extracurricular or community involvement. Demonstrated financial need of the family, evidenced in the application. Commitment of significant weekly time to the programme's advising sessions, test preparation and application work across the cycle. Recent calls have also stressed compliance: clear intent to study in the US on a proper student visa and respect for immigration rules.
required_documents: Online application through your country's EducationUSA OFP portal during its national window. Academic transcripts and national examination results (for example WAEC for the Nigerian undergraduate call). Evidence of family income demonstrating financial need. Essays written in your own words, which double as a writing sample. Recommendation letters and a list of leadership and extracurricular activities. Identity document; shortlisted candidates then sit interviews and an English assessment.
summary: The EducationUSA Opportunity Funds Program (OFP) tackles the hidden barrier to studying in the United States: the up-front…

title: Government of Ireland Fellows Programme (Irish Aid)
university: Government of Ireland (Department of Foreign Affairs)
description: The Government of Ireland Fellows Programme is a fully funded one-year master’s scholarship in Ireland for early to…
details:
The Government of Ireland Fellows Programme is a fully funded one-year master’s scholarship in Ireland for early to mid-career professionals from eligible countries across Africa, Asia, Latin America, Small Island Developing States and Palestine. It covers programme fees, flights, accommodation, a monthly living allowance and insurance for the full 10 to 16 month degree.

Candidates need a strong bachelor’s degree, two to three years of relevant work experience and demonstrated leadership tied to the Sustainable Development Goals. Selection runs in three stages with interviews in early 2027. Stage 1 applications for the 2027-28 intake are open now and close on July 26, 2026, so act immediately.
benefits: Full programme fees at an Irish higher education institution for a 10 to 16 month master's. Economy return flights between your home country and Ireland. Accommodation costs covered for the duration of the programme. Monthly living allowance for food, transport and personal expenses, plus insurance and support services through the Irish Council for International Students. Named prestige strands in some countries, such as the Roger Casement Fellowship (Nigeria) and Kader Asmal Fellowship (South Africa). An alumni network of nearly 4,000 Ireland Fellows from 79 countries built since 1974.
requirements: Early to mid-career professionals with leadership potential from eligible countries under the programme strands: Africa (about 24 countries including Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Ethiopia, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia and Zimbabwe), Asia (Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos and others), Latin America, Small Island Developing States, and Palestine. Resident nationals of the eligible country with two to three years of substantial work experience directly relevant to the proposed study (the exact requirement varies by country). Bachelor's degree with a GPA of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale from a recognized institution, awarded in 2015 or later; a good second-class degree can be considered with strong relevant experience. Not already holding a master's degree, and applying to start a new master's-level programme in Ireland in August or September 2027. Three programmes selected from the official Directory of Eligible Programmes, with a clear understanding of their academic and English requirements. Demonstrated leadership, commitment to the Sustainable Development Goals in your country, and interest in building links with Ireland. Maximum of two lifetime applications, and in several countries (including Kenya, Zambia, Malawi and Sierra Leone) applications are by invitation through Irish Aid partner organizations only.
required_documents: Stage 1 preliminary application form submitted online (or to the relevant Embassy of Ireland, per your country's guidance note). Identity document and academic transcripts with certificates. Evidence of relevant work experience. Your shortlist of three eligible programmes from the official directory. Stage 2 detailed application for those shortlisted, followed by an interview at stage 3. English test evidence: shortlisted candidates without certification sit the Duolingo English Test (or IELTS in January 2027 if their chosen institution requires it).
summary: The Government of Ireland Fellows Programme is a fully funded one-year master’s scholarship in Ireland for early to…

title: Cambridge Africa Changemakers Scholarship (University of Cambridge)
description: The Cambridge Africa Changemakers Scholarship is a full-cost PhD award at the University of Cambridge reserved for citizens…
details:
The Cambridge Africa Changemakers Scholarship is a full-cost PhD award at the University of Cambridge reserved for citizens of African countries. Funded through the Cambridge Trust, it pays international tuition, an annual maintenance stipend, the UK visa fee and health surcharge, plus travel and research costs for the whole doctorate.

Priority goes to research that advances Africa’s development and climate-resilient, sustainable futures, in any subject and at any Cambridge college, and 55 scholars were funded in a single recent cycle. There is no separate form: apply for your PhD course by the Cambridge funding deadline, typically December 3, 2026 for October 2027 entry, and tick the funding section.
benefits: University tuition fee at the full international rate for the whole PhD. Annual maintenance stipend sufficient for a single person, for the duration of the degree. UK student visa cost and the Immigration Health Surcharge paid, which many scholarships leave out. Allowances for travel and research costs during the PhD. Membership of the Cambridge Trust scholar community at one of the world's leading research universities. A rare full-cost route into a Cambridge doctorate specifically reserved for African students.
requirements: Citizens of any country in Africa applying for a full-time PhD at the University of Cambridge. Open to any subject except premium-rate courses, and tenable at any Cambridge college. Aimed at talented students who need financial assistance to take up their Cambridge place; financial need is part of the assessment. Priority goes to research that contributes to the development of the African continent and to climate-resilient, sustainable futures for Africa and the world. Applicants must meet the normal academic entry requirements of their chosen Cambridge PhD, typically a strong master's degree in a relevant field. The programme is closely affiliated with the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Cambridge, and dozens of awards have been made per cycle (55 in the 2023-24 round). No separate scholarship form exists; eligibility is assessed from the admission application itself.
required_documents: University of Cambridge graduate application submitted through the Applicant Portal for your chosen PhD course. Research proposal that makes the contribution to Africa's development and climate-resilient futures explicit. Academic transcripts and degree certificates for all previous study. Academic references as required by the course. English language evidence where required by the university. The funding section of the application completed, ticking consideration for Cambridge Trust funding; no separate Felix-style form is needed.
summary: The Cambridge Africa Changemakers Scholarship is a full-cost PhD award at the University of Cambridge reserved for citizens…

title: MINDS Scholarship Programme for Leadership Development (Study in Africa)
description: The MINDS Scholarship Programme for Leadership Development funds Africans to study in another African country, building leaders with…
details:
The MINDS Scholarship Programme for Leadership Development funds Africans to study in another African country, building leaders with genuinely pan-African networks. Run by the Mandela Institute for Development Studies, it covers tuition, accommodation, meals, a return flight and a stipend worth up to about USD 15,000 per year for honours and master’s degrees.

Applicants must be African citizens aged 18 to 45, already accepted at a MINDS-preferred university outside their home country, with at least 70 percent in recent studies and clear leadership evidence. Applications are open year round on a rolling basis, so the smart move is to apply as soon as your admission letter is in hand.
benefits: Tuition fees, accommodation and meals covered at your host university. One return flight between your home country and the study country for the duration of the programme. A fixed stipend toward day-to-day expenses, with medical aid where applicable; total support up to about USD 15,000 per year. Tailored leadership development activities throughout the scholarship, built around a pan-African development mindset. Membership of a scholar network drawn from across the continent since 2017, with cohort gatherings and alumni activities. A rare programme that funds Africans to study within Africa, keeping costs realistic while building cross-border networks.
requirements: Nationals of an African country who are residing in Africa and want to study in another African country (refugees hosted in an African country may study in their host country). Aged 18 to 45 at the time of application. Formally accepted by one or more MINDS-preferred institutions outside your country of citizenship or residency; partner universities span East, West, Southern and North Africa. Admitted to start a full-time one- or two-year honours or master's degree in the upcoming academic year; any field of study is welcome. At least 70 percent in every subject or course over the last two completed years of study. Clear evidence of leadership experience or potential and a commitment to Africa's development, demonstrated through the application questions. A complete application with every required document; incomplete files are disqualified.
required_documents: Online application through the MINDS scholarship portal (each file in PDF, maximum 2 MB). Copy of the data page of your passport. Certified academic transcripts or results for the last two years of study. Official university acceptance letter addressed to you, stating the degree, its start year and its duration. Valid study permit or visa, or proof that you have applied for one. Curriculum vitae of no more than four single-sided pages (optional but recommended). Two reference letters of up to three pages each, addressing your integrity, leadership and commitment to Africa's development.
summary: The MINDS Scholarship Programme for Leadership Development funds Africans to study in another African country, building leaders with…

title: King Abdulaziz University Scholarship (Study in Saudi Arabia)
university: King Abdulaziz University / Saudi Ministry of Education
description: The King Abdulaziz University Scholarship is a fully funded award for international students at one of Saudi Arabia’s…
details:
The King Abdulaziz University Scholarship is a fully funded award for international students at one of Saudi Arabia’s top-ranked universities, located in Jeddah. Scholars study tuition-free with a monthly stipend of about SAR 850 to 1,900 depending on level, free university housing, healthcare, subsidized meals and an annual round-trip flight home.

Bachelor’s, master’s and PhD seats are offered through the national Study in Saudi platform, with most graduate programs taught in English. Undergraduate applicants must be 17 to 25, master’s applicants 30 or under and PhD applicants 35 or under. Application windows open per intake throughout the year, and there is no application fee.
benefits: Tuition-free scholarship seat at one of Saudi Arabia's highest-ranked universities (Jeddah), covering the full programme. Monthly stipend (about SAR 850 for bachelor's, SAR 900 for master's and SAR 1,900 for PhD), plus a preparation allowance of two months' stipend on arrival. University accommodation, free healthcare at the university hospital, and subsidized meals at campus restaurants. Annual round-trip air ticket to your home country, plus arrival compensation for newcomers. Extra excellence allowance for top academic performance, thesis printing allowance, and a graduation allowance for shipping books. Separate male and female campuses, each with full academic, cultural and sports facilities.
requirements: Non-Saudi students residing outside the Kingdom without a Saudi residency permit at the time of application; both men and women can apply. Undergraduate applicants must be 17 to 25 years old with a secondary school certificate no more than three years old and strong grades. Master's applicants must be 30 or under and PhD applicants 35 or under, with a recognized prior degree at a very good grade or better. Good conduct and medical fitness are required, and previous scholarship dismissals from Saudi institutions disqualify an applicant. Most graduate programmes at KAU are taught in English (a statement of purpose in English is required except for Islamic Studies and Arabic), while some tracks are Arabic-taught. Health-profession fields such as Medicine, Dentistry and Pharmacy are not open to international scholarship students. Female applicants should note the university applies Saudi guardian (mahram) regulations, so read the current admission guide carefully before applying.
required_documents: Online application through the KAU admission portal or the national Study in Saudi platform. Secondary school certificate (undergraduate) or degree certificate and transcript (graduate), certified or attested as instructed. Curriculum vitae and a statement of purpose in English (Arabic for Islamic Studies and Arabic language programmes). Two recommendation letters from former professors for graduate applicants. Copy of a passport valid for at least one year. Medical report and a certificate of good conduct. Certified translations where documents are not in Arabic or English.
summary: The King Abdulaziz University Scholarship is a fully funded award for international students at one of Saudi Arabia’s…

title: Australian Government Research Training Program (RTP) Scholarship
description: The Research Training Program (RTP) is the Australian Government’s flagship funding scheme for research degrees, and it is…
details:
The Research Training Program (RTP) is the Australian Government’s flagship funding scheme for research degrees, and it is the main engine behind fully funded PhDs in Australia for international students. It combines a full tuition fees offset with a tax-free living stipend of roughly AUD 32,000 to 42,000 per year, and many universities add health cover and relocation allowances.

Every Australian university receives RTP funding and runs its own competitive round, so one strong application, ideally with a supervisor already on board, often ranks you for university scholarships too. Main international rounds for 2027 commencement close between August and October 2026, with October 31 a common cutoff at major universities.
benefits: RTP Fees Offset covering the full international tuition fees of the research degree. RTP Stipend for living costs, indexed annually; most universities pay roughly AUD 32,000 to 42,000 per year tax-free for full-time candidates. Stipend duration up to three to four years for a PhD (with possible extension provisions) and up to two years for a research master's, per university rules. Many universities bundle overseas student health cover for the candidate (sometimes family) and offer relocation or thesis allowances. RTP is the main engine of funded PhDs in Australia, so a single application often also ranks you for university-funded equivalents. Graduates hold an Australian research degree with post-study work visa pathways.
requirements: Domestic and international candidates admitted to a higher degree by research (research master's or PhD) at an Australian university; every Australian university receives RTP funding and runs its own competitive selection. Strong academic record, normally first-class honours, a research master's, or a bachelor's plus substantial research output such as publications or a strong thesis. A viable research proposal and, at most universities, a supervisor who has agreed in principle to supervise the project before you apply. English proficiency at the university's HDR level (commonly IELTS 6.5 to 7.0 or equivalent). International places are limited at each institution, so rankings are competitive and strong applicants apply to more than one university. You cannot hold another equivalent Australian Government scholarship at the same time. Fields are unrestricted, from engineering and health to humanities, wherever the university has supervision capacity.
required_documents: University HDR (higher degree by research) application through each university's admission portal. Research proposal in the university's format. Evidence of supervisor contact or support, where the university requires it before submission. Academic transcripts and degree certificates for all prior study. CV including publications, and copies of research outputs where available. English test results meeting HDR requirements. Referee reports as specified by the university.
summary: The Research Training Program (RTP) is the Australian Government’s flagship funding scheme for research degrees, and it is…

title: JICA SDGs Global Leader Scholarship (Japan)
description: The JICA SDGs Global Leader Scholarship is a fully funded master’s and PhD program in Japan for young…
details:
The JICA SDGs Global Leader Scholarship is a fully funded master’s and PhD program in Japan for young government officials, academics and professionals from JICA partner countries across Asia, Africa, the Middle East, the Pacific and Latin America. JICA pays full tuition directly to the university and provides a monthly allowance of about JPY 146,000, a research grant, airfare and arrival support.

Study fields follow each country’s development priorities, from public policy and finance to disaster risk reduction and regional development, at leading Japanese universities. Each national JICA office runs its own call, with most windows closing between September and November 2026 for the following intake, so contact your country office early.
benefits: Full tuition, entrance and school support fees paid by JICA directly to the university. Monthly living allowance calculated at Japanese Government (MEXT) scholarship standards, around JPY 146,000 during the research-student phase. Research support grant for books, equipment, conference participation and research trips. International airfare and arrival support, with programme staff assisting your setup in Japan. Master's track of about two years and doctoral track of about three years, often preceded by a six-month research-student period at the university. A policy-focused network: SDGs Global Leader alumni move into senior government and academic roles across JICA partner countries.
requirements: Young and mid-career government officials, academics and other leading professionals from JICA partner countries across Asia, the Pacific, Africa, the Middle East, Central Asia, Europe and Latin America. Age limits in principle: 35 or under for master's applicants and 40 or under for doctoral applicants. Bachelor's degree (master's for doctoral track) with a strong academic record and English ability (TOEFL or IELTS evidence is requested in most national calls). Endorsement or nomination through your employer and the JICA office responsible for your country is usually required, especially for public-sector applicants. Research topics must support your country's sustainable development policy, for example public policy, finance, trade and investment, international relations, disaster risk reduction, maritime issues or regional development. You must not hold or plan to hold another Japanese Government scholarship during the programme. Acceptance is conditional on passing the entrance screening of a partner Japanese university from JICA's agreement list.
required_documents: Application form for the SDGs Global Leader programme from your national JICA office, including consent from your current employer where required. Officially certified graduation certificates and complete academic transcripts, in English or with official translations. Research plan aligned with your country's development priorities and the target university's faculty list. English test certificate (TOEFL or IELTS) photocopy. Passport or photo ID copy, passport-size photographs and a health certificate. Recommendation or endorsement documents from your agency as specified in the national call.
summary: The JICA SDGs Global Leader Scholarship is a fully funded master’s and PhD program in Japan for young…

title: Ashinaga Africa Initiative Scholarship
description: The Ashinaga Africa Initiative is a fully funded undergraduate scholarship for orphaned students from Sub-Saharan Africa, created by…
details:
The Ashinaga Africa Initiative is a fully funded undergraduate scholarship for orphaned students from Sub-Saharan Africa, created by Japan’s Ashinaga Foundation. It covers everything: tuition, accommodation, a monthly stipend, flights and settling-in costs at partner universities in Japan, Europe, the UK, the USA and Brazil, plus a fully supported preparatory year before the degree begins.

Candidates must have lost one or both parents, rank near the top of their class, and commit to returning to contribute to Sub-Saharan Africa after graduation. Applications are free and open on a rolling cycle basis: Francophone and Lusophone students apply online directly, while Anglophone students are now nominated through Ashinaga partner schools.
benefits: Full financial support for an undergraduate degree abroad: tuition, accommodation, a monthly stipend, flights between home and the study country, and settling-in costs. Study destinations at partner universities across Japan, Europe, the UK, the USA and Brazil, chosen together with Ashinaga during preparation. A fully supported preparatory year with academic training, language study and leadership development before university starts. Ongoing mentorship, internships and field-research opportunities through the Ashinaga network and its Kenjin-Tatsujin advisory council. Membership of a pan-African scholar community from nearly every Sub-Saharan country since 2014. There is no application fee, and you should never pay anyone to apply on your behalf.
requirements: Young people from Sub-Saharan Africa who have lost one or both parents, with citizenship of and schooling in one of the 48 to 49 eligible countries. Completed secondary school and national exams recently (within roughly the last two years), or receiving final results by the cutoff stated in the current call; technical and vocational qualifications are not accepted. Consistently ranked around the top 10 percent of your class in the final years of secondary school; strong grades are essential. Proficient in English or French, with a birth-date limit set in each call (the programme targets recent school leavers). Without the financial means to attend university abroad, and with no dependents that would interfere with full-time study. Committed to returning to Sub-Saharan Africa after graduation to contribute to your community, and able to complete Ashinaga's two preparatory programmes over about a year before university. Since August 2024, students in Anglophone countries are identified through selected partner high schools rather than open applications, while Francophone and Lusophone applicants apply directly online.
required_documents: Online eligibility registration, after which eligible students receive the application form link by email. Passport, national ID card or birth certificate. Death certificate of the deceased parent or parents, or alternative official proof of orphan status. All term reports or transcripts from the last two years of secondary school. Final national examination results certificate, sent as soon as available if results are pending. Recommendation letters with an official signature or stamp, plus certificates for extracurriculars or work where available. Francophone and Lusophone candidates use the dedicated online forms; Anglophone candidates go through their partner school's nomination.
summary: The Ashinaga Africa Initiative is a fully funded undergraduate scholarship for orphaned students from Sub-Saharan Africa, created by…

title: P.E.O. International Peace Scholarship (USA and Canada)
description: The P.E.O. International Peace Scholarship has funded women from outside the United States and Canada for graduate study…
details:
The P.E.O. International Peace Scholarship has funded women from outside the United States and Canada for graduate study in North America since 1949, making it one of the longest-running awards of its kind. It provides up to USD 12,500 per academic year based on demonstrated financial need, renewable by re-application while full-time coursework remains.

The scholarship is designed as gap funding, so applicants show how it completes a realistic budget alongside other resources, and commit to returning home to foster peace through their education. The eligibility form for the 2027-28 year must be submitted between September 15 and December 15, 2026.
benefits: Up to USD 12,500 for the academic year, sized to each student's documented need. One of the longest-running awards for international women in North America, funded since 1949 by the P.E.O. Sisterhood. Renewal is possible by re-applying in later cycles while eligible coursework remains. International students attending Cottey College, the P.E.O.-owned women's college, are also eligible. The application is free and the process is transparent, with a published calendar each year. Recipients join a values-driven network centered on education and international friendship.
requirements: Women from countries outside the United States and Canada pursuing (or admitted to) a graduate degree at an accredited college or university in the US or Canada. US or Canadian citizens and permanent residents are not eligible, though residency for tax purposes only is permitted. A full year of formal coursework must remain, and you must be enrolled and in residence for the entire school year. Doctoral students who have finished coursework and are working only on the dissertation cannot apply as first-time applicants. Scholarships are not given for online-only study, research-only periods, internships or practical training without coursework. Applicants must intend to return to their home country to apply their education and foster peace. The award is need-based, and you must show additional resources (family funds, assistantships, waivers or other scholarships) that make your budget realistic.
required_documents: Online eligibility form submitted during the eligibility window (September 15 to December 15). Full application materials issued to eligible candidates, completed through the P.E.O. online system. Proof of admission or enrollment at your US or Canadian graduate school. Academic transcripts. Budget and financial documentation showing need and your other funding sources. References and personal statements as specified in the application packet.
summary: The P.E.O. International Peace Scholarship has funded women from outside the United States and Canada for graduate study…

title: Margaret McNamara Education Grants (US-Canada Program)
description: Margaret McNamara Education Grants (MMEG) support women from developing countries who are already enrolled at universities in the…
details:
Margaret McNamara Education Grants (MMEG) support women from developing countries who are already enrolled at universities in the United States or Canada and need help closing a funding gap. The US-Canada program awards a one-time grant of up to USD 15,000 that can go toward tuition, living costs, books or even childcare.

Applicants must be women aged 25 or older with a record of working for the wellbeing of women and children, and an intention to continue that work. The grant stacks neatly on top of assistantships and partial scholarships. The application window runs from September 15, 2026 to January 15, 2027, with awards announced in April.
benefits: Grant historically up to USD 15,000, paid once and sized to your proposal and need. Freedom to use the funds for tuition, fees, books, living costs or childcare that keeps your studies on track. Run by a volunteer-led non-profit founded in 1981 that has supported hundreds of women from developing countries. Recipients join the MMEG grantee community and are announced publicly each year, a meaningful recognition for women-and-children-focused careers. Sister programmes exist for South Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean, France and Trinity Washington University if the US-Canada window does not fit. The award stacks well on top of assistantships or partial scholarships since it targets the funding gap.
requirements: Self-identifying women aged at least 25 at the application deadline. Nationals of a country on the current MMEG country-eligibility list (lower- and middle-income countries); US or Canadian citizens, permanent residents and landed immigrants are not eligible. Already registered, not just accepted, at an accredited in-person institution in the United States or Canada when applying; exclusively online programmes do not qualify. Enrolled for at least one more full academic semester after the award is made in April, and planning to graduate within three years of the award. Demonstrated financial need and a track record of working for the wellbeing of women and children, with plans to continue that work. Not related to staff, spouses or retirees of the World Bank Group, IMF or Inter-American Development Bank, or to MMEG board members. Certificate, undergraduate, graduate and post-doctoral students are all welcome in the US-Canada programme.
required_documents: Online application through the MMEG portal during the application window. Proof of current registration at your US or Canadian institution. Academic transcripts. Evidence of nationality (passport bio page). Financial information demonstrating need, per the application checklist on the MMEG site. Essays describing your commitment to improving the lives of women and children and your plans after graduation. References as specified in the checklist.
summary: Margaret McNamara Education Grants (MMEG) support women from developing countries who are already enrolled at universities in the…

title: East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship (Hawaii, USA)
description: The East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship funds master’s and doctoral students from across Asia, the Pacific and the…
details:
The East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship funds master’s and doctoral students from across Asia, the Pacific and the United States to study at the University of Hawai’i at Mānoa while living and learning together at the East-West Center in Honolulu. The award covers full tuition and fees, residence-hall housing and a partial stipend, a package worth about USD 22,000 per year.

Beyond funding, fellows join a genuine leadership program with seminars, service projects and a network spanning more than 60 countries, including Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, the ASEAN states and the Pacific islands. Applications for the Fall 2027 cohort close December 1, 2026, with supporting documents due by January 10, 2027.
benefits: Full-time graduate tuition and fees at UH Mānoa for the academic year, paid at the general graduate rate. Housing in an East-West Center residence hall plus a stipend that partially covers food and incidentals; total value around USD 22,000 per year, with need-based supplements possible. Renewable for a second academic year subject to funding and satisfactory progress, up to about 20 months in total. A genuine leadership programme: the Community Building Institute in August, seminars, service projects and a network across 60+ countries. All GDF applicants are automatically considered for extra EWC alumni and foundation scholarships, and competitive field-study and conference travel grants run during the award. Permission to work limited hours on campus can top up living funds.
requirements: Citizens or permanent residents of the United States, or citizens of countries across Asia and the Pacific, including Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Afghanistan, the ASEAN states, China, Japan, Korea, Mongolia, Russia and the Pacific island nations. Applying for (or already enrolled in) a classified master's or doctoral programme at the University of Hawai'i at Mānoa. Four-year bachelor's degree (or equivalent) completed before the award starts, from a recognized institution. English proficiency for UH admission: minimum TOEFL 79, IELTS 6.5 or Duolingo 95 where required. Priority goes to applicants with a demonstrated commitment to the Asia-Pacific region and to fields relevant to the East-West Center's mission. Fellows live in EWC residence halls (single fellows and couples without children) and take part in the residential leadership programme, so willingness to join community life is essential. Non-US fellows attend on a J-1 exchange visitor visa.
required_documents: Online East-West Center fellowship application (portal opens in early August, closes December 1 at 11:59 PM Hawai'i time). Curriculum vitae or resume. UH Mānoa application acknowledgment (screenshot or PDF) if you are applying to the university simultaneously. Passport biodata page for international applicants. Official transcripts from every college or university attended, submitted per the GDF handbook instructions. Official TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo score sent by the testing agency where English proof is required. UH statement of objectives and any departmental items (references, GRE where a department requires it) completed by the January 10 documents deadline.
summary: The East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship funds master’s and doctoral students from across Asia, the Pacific and the…

title: Felix Scholarship (Oxford, Reading and SOAS)
description: The Felix Scholarship is a fully funded postgraduate award for students from India and other developing countries at…
details:
The Felix Scholarship is a fully funded postgraduate award for students from India and other developing countries at three UK universities: the University of Oxford, the University of Reading and SOAS University of London. It covers 100 percent of tuition, an annual living grant of about GBP 19,000 at Oxford, and one return airfare home.

Around 20 scholarships are awarded each year to first-class graduates who could not otherwise afford UK study, with financial need weighed alongside merit. Note the staggered timeline: Oxford candidates must apply by their course’s December 2026 or January 2027 deadline, while the separate SOAS Felix application runs to early March 2027.
benefits: 100 percent of tuition fees at the international rate for the full fee liability of the course, up to three years for a PhD. Annual living grant of about GBP 19,000 at Oxford and about GBP 17,894 at Reading; SOAS confirms its maintenance package on award. One economy return airfare between your home country and the UK. Around 20 scholarships across the three universities each year, with over 400 scholars supported since the early 1990s. Access to the Felix alumni community and the standing of a fully funded UK award on your CV. Note: spouse or family costs and pre-sessional English courses are not covered.
requirements: Primarily for Indian nationals with at least a first-class bachelor's degree from a recognized Indian university, applying for full-time postgraduate study at the University of Oxford, University of Reading or SOAS University of London. A small number of awards (one at Oxford and one at SOAS) go to nationals of other developing countries; SOAS gives priority to candidates from Afghanistan, Syria, Iran, Iraq and the Palestinian territories living in their home country. You must not already hold a degree from a university outside your home country, and you must not have studied abroad for a year or more. Demonstrated financial need is assessed alongside academic merit. Candidates need an offer of admission from applications submitted by the university's scholarship-relevant deadline; deferred offers are not eligible. Exceptionally at SOAS, an upper-second bachelor's with a first-class master's can be considered, and Felix master's alumni with a SOAS distinction can apply for the PhD route. Scholars are expected to return home after their studies; part-time programmes are excluded.
required_documents: Complete postgraduate admission application to Oxford, Reading or SOAS for your chosen course. At Oxford there is no separate Felix form: the graduate application itself, including the nationality and residence section, is the scholarship application. At SOAS and Reading, a separate Felix scholarship form is completed after (or alongside) the admission application through the university portal. Academic transcripts and degree certificates showing first-class standing. References and statement of purpose as required by the course. Evidence relevant to financial need, and English test results early where your offer is conditional on them.
summary: The Felix Scholarship is a fully funded postgraduate award for students from India and other developing countries at…

title: University of Geneva Excellence Master Fellowship (Switzerland)
university: University of Geneva Faculty of Science
description: The University of Geneva Excellence Master Fellowship rewards outstanding international students joining a Master of Science at the…
details:
The University of Geneva Excellence Master Fellowship rewards outstanding international students joining a Master of Science at the Faculty of Science in Geneva, Switzerland. Fellows receive CHF 10,000 to 15,000 per year with no teaching duties, renewable for the full length of the master’s when first-semester results are strong.

Eligible fields include astronomy, biology, chemistry and biochemistry, computer science, mathematics, physics, pharmaceutical sciences and environmental sciences, taught in one of the world’s great scientific cities. Candidates should belong to the top 10 percent of their bachelor’s cohort. The application, submitted as a single PDF, is due by February 28, 2027 for the September 2027 intake.
benefits: Grant of CHF 10,000 to 15,000 per year with no teaching or assistantship duties attached. Awarded for one year and extended for the standard length of the chosen programme (three or four semesters) if your first-semester results are strong. Study in a faculty hosting Swiss National Centres of Competence in Research and many European projects, with genuine research-track training. Geneva's international organizations (UN, WHO, CERN nearby) create unusual internship and career openings for scientists. The fellowship is purely merit-based and open to every nationality. Note: Geneva is expensive, so treat the grant as a strong contribution rather than a full cost-of-living package.
requirements: Outstanding students from any university worldwide who intend to pursue a Master of Science at the University of Geneva's Faculty of Science. Disciplines span astronomy, biology, chemistry and biochemistry, computer science, mathematics, physics, pharmaceutical sciences, earth and environmental sciences. Bachelor's degree completed, or expected within about six months of the application, in a relevant field. Belonging to the top of your cohort (roughly the best 10 percent of your bachelor's programme) is the key selection signal. You must also meet the admission criteria of the specific master's programme you choose. French is not a formal requirement for the Faculty of Science; programmes run in English or in English and French. Students who have already started a master's at the Faculty of Science cannot apply.
required_documents: One single PDF file containing the entire application, submitted through the online platform. Scan of your passport or national identity card. Curriculum vitae of at most two pages. Complete bachelor's transcript with all grades. Motivation letter describing your scientific interests and why you want this master's at Geneva. If possible, two reference letters from professors, ideally emailed by them directly to the Faculty's fellowship address. Any extra evidence such as GRE or TOEFL results strengthens the file.
summary: The University of Geneva Excellence Master Fellowship rewards outstanding international students joining a Master of Science at the…

title: Chalmers IPOET Scholarship (Sweden)
description: The Chalmers IPOET Scholarship reduces tuition fees by 75 percent for talented fee-paying master’s students at Chalmers University…
details:
The Chalmers IPOET Scholarship reduces tuition fees by 75 percent for talented fee-paying master’s students at Chalmers University of Technology in Gothenburg, Sweden, and students who excel in year one see the reduction rise to 85 percent for the second year. Around 35 awards are made each cycle, funded by the Swedish Council for Higher Education.

All Chalmers master’s programs are eligible, from computer science and data science to architecture, biotechnology and electrical engineering. Selection is based on relative academic excellence, so a strong GPA and a solid home university matter most. Apply through universityadmissions.se and submit the scholarship form by January 15, 2027.
benefits: 75 percent reduction of tuition fees across all four semesters of the two-year master's programme. Students who excel in year one can have the reduction increased to 85 percent for the second year. Around 35 IPOET scholarships each year, funded by the Swedish Council for Higher Education and administered by Chalmers. Your financial situation is not assessed, and holding other partial funding does not hurt your chances. Chalmers also runs the Adlebertska (Adlebert) scheme for students from developing countries, assessed from the same application. Note: no cash is transferred to you; the waiver is applied directly to your tuition invoices, so budget separately for living costs in Gothenburg.
requirements: Citizens of countries outside the EU/EEA (and Switzerland) who are required to pay tuition fees for Swedish university studies. Applying to the first year of a master's programme at Chalmers University of Technology in Gothenburg; all master's fields are eligible. Meeting the general and programme-specific admission requirements of the chosen programme. Selection is on relative academic excellence, mainly your weighted average grade (roughly 80 percent of the scale maximum or better to be competitive). The standing of your home university, including global rankings, is also weighed. Ranking Chalmers as your first priority among Swedish applications significantly improves your chances. Only prospective (not current) Chalmers students can apply, and the award is made before your first year starts.
required_documents: Master's application submitted at universityadmissions.se, where you receive an eight-digit application number. Separate Chalmers scholarship application form, completed with that application number before the scholarship deadline. Academic transcripts and degree certificates uploaded to universityadmissions.se per Swedish national rules. Proof of English proficiency (IELTS or TOEFL) per programme requirements. CV and any programme-specific documents listed for your master's choice. Note that the scholarship deadline matches the programme application deadline, not the later deadline for supporting documents.
summary: The Chalmers IPOET Scholarship reduces tuition fees by 75 percent for talented fee-paying master’s students at Chalmers University…

title: TU/e Scholarship for Excellence (Eindhoven University of Technology)
description: The TU/e Scholarship for Excellence funds top international master’s students at Eindhoven University of Technology in the Netherlands,…
details:
The TU/e Scholarship for Excellence funds top international master’s students at Eindhoven University of Technology in the Netherlands, in the departments driving microchip and semiconductor innovation: Applied Physics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, and Mathematics and Computer Science. The award pays EUR 7,500 per year across the two-year master’s, backed by the Dutch national Beethoven Program.

Eindhoven sits at the heart of the Brainport high-tech region next to ASML, NXP and Philips, which makes internships and thesis placements unusually accessible. There is no separate application: every eligible applicant with a GPA of at least 7.5 out of 10 is considered automatically. Apply for the September 2027 intake by February 1, 2027.
benefits: EUR 7,500 per year for each of the two master's years, paid in monthly installments to a Dutch or SEPA bank account. Around 35 scholarships each year, funded by the Beethoven Program, the Dutch government's strategic investment in the microchip sector. Study in Eindhoven's Brainport region next to ASML, NXP, Philips and a dense high-tech job market with strong internship and thesis placements. Second-year payment continues if you earn at least 45 ECTS in year one and remain on track to graduate within 36 months. No separate application workload: eligible applicants are considered automatically. Note: this is a partial scholarship; you must still show sufficient funds for your visa and cover the rest of tuition and living costs.
requirements: Applicants to a full-time TU/e master's programme (or eligible track) in the Departments of Applied Physics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or Mathematics & Computer Science, the fields shaping microchip and semiconductor innovation. Completed secondary education and bachelor's degree outside the Netherlands, with no completed higher education in the Netherlands (exchange semesters are allowed). Not eligible for the Dutch study grant and loan system. Excellent academic results, with a GPA of at least 7.5 out of 10 (or equivalent) on your latest transcript. Not holding another scholarship or Dutch study grant. Meeting all requirements for a Dutch entry visa and residence permit. Not applying for the joint JADS master's with Tilburg or a European Double Degree; note the selection rate is around 2 percent, so treat it as a bonus on top of a solid funding plan.
required_documents: Complete TU/e master's application submitted through the university's online application system before the deadline. Certified copy of your bachelor's degree or most recent academic transcript showing a GPA of 7.5/10 or higher. Official English (or Dutch) translations of transcripts where applicable. Curriculum vitae and motivation letter as required by the master's application. Proof of English proficiency per the programme's admission requirements. No separate scholarship form exists; the master's file itself is the scholarship file.
summary: The TU/e Scholarship for Excellence funds top international master’s students at Eindhoven University of Technology in the Netherlands,…

title: Science@Leuven Scholarship (KU Leuven, Belgium)
description: The Science@Leuven Scholarship supports outstanding international students joining English-taught master’s programs at the Faculty of Science of KU…
details:
The Science@Leuven Scholarship supports outstanding international students joining English-taught master’s programs at the Faculty of Science of KU Leuven, one of Europe’s oldest and most innovative universities. The award is worth up to EUR 12,000 for the year and always covers tuition, insurance and basic health cover, with renewal possible for the second year on excellent results.

Eligible programs include astronomy and astrophysics, biology, biophysics, chemistry, geography, mathematics, physics and statistics. Selection rewards top-of-class students with strong references and clear motivation. Applications for the September 2027 intake close on February 15, 2027, together with the program application.
benefits: Scholarship of up to EUR 12,000 for the academic year, with the exact amount set by the Science@Leuven Fund board. Always includes the tuition fee for one year plus insurance and basic Belgian health cover; the remainder contributes to living costs. Continued for the second year of two-year programmes if your first-year results are outstanding. Study at one of Europe's oldest and highest-ranked universities, founded in 1425, with strong research across the sciences. Membership of an alumni-backed scholarship community and an ambassador role that looks strong on a CV. Note: even with the full amount, budget some personal funds for books and living extras in Leuven.
requirements: International students with a bachelor's degree from a non-Belgian university that gives access to the chosen programme; you must not already hold a master's or PhD. Applying to an eligible international master's programme of the KU Leuven Faculty of Science (for example astronomy, physics, chemistry, mathematics, statistics, biology, geography or geology; interuniversity options have extra conditions). Excellent academic record, comparable to at least a Distinction at KU Leuven. English proficiency of at least IELTS 7.0 overall or TOEFL 94. No previous study or work at KU Leuven. Strong motivation for the Faculty of Science and willingness to act as an ambassador for the programme; awardees sign a contract accepting the conditions. The number of scholarships per year is limited (roughly 10 to 15), so competition is stiff.
required_documents: Completed KU Leuven master's application via the university's online application tool, submitted before the scholarship deadline. Separate online registration for the Science@Leuven Scholarship, uploading the confirmation that your programme application was submitted. Full list of completed courses with ECTS sizes and grades, with an explanation of the grading scale where it is not ECTS. Two reference letters from professors, ideally internationally known in the field. Proof of English proficiency (IELTS 7.0 or TOEFL 94 minimum). Motivation statement for the chosen Faculty of Science programme. Your scholarship registration is complete only after you receive the confirmation email.
summary: The Science@Leuven Scholarship supports outstanding international students joining English-taught master’s programs at the Faculty of Science of KU…

title: ENS Paris International Selection Scholarship (France)
description: The ENS Paris International Selection is one of France’s most selective scholarships, admitting a small group of outstanding…
details:
The ENS Paris International Selection is one of France’s most selective scholarships, admitting a small group of outstanding international students each year to the École normale supérieure in Paris. Winners receive EUR 1,000 per month for three years plus a room on an ENS campus, while completing the ENS diploma alongside a master’s degree.

Around 20 to 30 places are offered across sciences and arts and humanities, and candidates must be under 26 and not have lived in France during the qualifying period. Selection involves a demanding written and oral examination. Applications for the 2027 session are expected to close in early December 2026.
benefits: Monthly scholarship of EUR 1,000 for three years, which is rare for master's-level funding in France. A room on an ENS campus in Paris, removing the hardest cost of student life in the capital. Study at one of the world's most selective institutions, whose alumni include Nobel laureates and Fields medalists, within the PSL university group. Graduates leave with both the prestigious ENS diploma and a master's degree in their specialty. A three-week welcome programme with intensive French lessons, conferences and cultural visits eases arrival. Direct access to top research labs and, for many scholars, a natural route into fully funded PhD positions afterwards.
requirements: Outstanding undergraduates worldwide: about 10 places in Sciences and 10 in Arts & Humanities are awarded each year through a competitive examination. Under 26 years old at the time set in the call (you must not have passed your 26th birthday). At least one year of undergraduate study completed at a foreign (non-French) university in the calendar year before applications open, and two years completed by the September 1 following admission. You must not have lived in France for more than 10 months during the selection year or the year before, and you may apply to the International Selection only once in your life. Sciences disciplines include mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology, computer science, earth science and cognitive science; Arts & Humanities span philosophy, history, literature, economics, political studies, linguistics and more. For Arts & Humanities a good command of French is strongly recommended (about B1 or better), and the motivation letter is written in French; Sciences interviews can be taken in English or French. Selection is on academic excellence plus curiosity, open-mindedness and a taste for research.
required_documents: Initial online application form on the ENS platform, which triggers access to the document-upload system (Dematec). Detailed application form, passport or national ID, and high-school diploma. Full university transcripts with grades. Motivation letter (in French for Arts & Humanities; some disciplines ask for French and English versions). Research project of up to about three pages describing what you want to study at ENS. Curriculum vitae, all merged and uploaded as instructed; exam reports from previous years on the ENS site show what examiners expect.
summary: The ENS Paris International Selection is one of France’s most selective scholarships, admitting a small group of outstanding…

title: Université Paris-Saclay International Master’s Scholarship (IDEX)
description: The Université Paris-Saclay International Master’s Scholarship (IDEX) funds talented international students joining master’s programs at one of continental…
details:
The Université Paris-Saclay International Master’s Scholarship (IDEX) funds talented international students joining master’s programs at one of continental Europe’s highest-ranked universities. Scholars receive EUR 10,000 per year paid over ten months, plus a flat travel and visa allowance of up to EUR 900 depending on home country.

Paris-Saclay awards these scholarships purely on academic merit to newly admitted students in fields spanning mathematics, physics, engineering, life sciences, economics, law and more.
