You apply for admission first, and eligible admitted students are invited to the scholarship stage. The next cycle for September 2027 entry is expected to close around March 31, 2027.
benefits: EUR 10,000 per academic year, paid monthly over ten months from September to June. Awarded for one or two years depending on whether you enter at M1 or M2 level, renewed for the second year subject to earning the required credits. Up to EUR 900 as a one-off contribution to travel and visa costs, scaled by country of origin. Administrative support and help with the search for accommodation on arrival. Study within one of continental Europe's highest-ranked universities, with clear pathways into Paris-Saclay doctoral schools. Note: the scholarship is paid only after you arrive in France and register in your programme; no advance payment is made.
requirements: International (non-French) students admitted to a master's programme of Université Paris-Saclay operated by AgroParisTech, CentraleSupélec, ENS Paris-Saclay, INSTN-CEA, IOGS, Université Évry Paris-Saclay, Université Paris-Saclay or UVSQ. First-time enrollment in France: you must not have been registered at a French higher-education institution before, apart from exchange programmes, Erasmus Mundus joint degrees without a French diploma, internships or language courses. Aged 30 or under during the year of selection. All Paris-Saclay master's programmes are eligible except apprenticeship (vocational) tracks. Particularly aimed at students who intend to continue to a PhD at Paris-Saclay, though this is not a formal requirement for M1 applicants. Selection is by invitation: programme coordinators pre-select the strongest admitted candidates, who then receive a personal link to the scholarship form. A bonus system applies for refugee students and those under subsidiary protection.
required_documents: Complete master's application submitted on the Paris-Saclay admissions platform (this is the gateway to being pre-selected). Online scholarship form, completed via the personal invitation link sent by email after pre-selection. Names and email addresses of two referees (professors or internship supervisors), who each complete an online recommendation before the closing date. Academic transcripts and diplomas already provided in your admission file. Statement of your academic project and motivation, including PhD intentions where relevant. Both recommendations must be received for the application to count as complete; you are responsible for chasing your referees.
summary: The Université Paris-Saclay International Master’s Scholarship (IDEX) funds talented international students joining master’s programs at one of continental…

title: International Max Planck Research Schools (IMPRS) PhD Positions
description: The International Max Planck Research Schools (IMPRS) are structured PhD programs run by Max Planck Institutes together with…
details:
The International Max Planck Research Schools (IMPRS) are structured PhD programs run by Max Planck Institutes together with German universities, and they are one of the most reliable fully funded doctoral routes in Europe. Every admitted student receives a funding contract or salary at German public-sector levels, and there are no tuition fees.

Around 60 schools cover practically every field, from astrophysics, computer science and quantum optics to molecular biology, law and human development, all taught in English. Each school runs its own admission call, with most deadlines falling between October and January, so applications are effectively open somewhere all year round.
benefits: Full funding for the whole PhD through a funding contract or employment contract, at levels that comfortably cover living costs in Germany. Doctorate awarded by a partner German university while you research at a Max Planck institute, one of the world's leading research organizations. Structured training: courses, retreats, soft-skills workshops and a thesis advisory committee rather than a single supervisor. Excellent facilities and generous research budgets typical of the Max Planck system. Strong career outcomes in academia and industry, supported by the Max Planck alumni network. No tuition fees, and relocation and visa support are provided by the host institute.
requirements: Master's degree (or equivalent, and in some schools an excellent four-year bachelor's) in a field matching the chosen research school, completed before the programme starts. There are dozens of IMPRS across Germany, each a partnership between Max Planck institutes and universities, covering fields from astrophysics, neuroscience and molecular biology to computer science, economics and law. Open to applicants of all nationalities; English is the working language of the schools, so proof of English is normally required, and German is not. Strong grades and research experience appropriate to the field; many schools ask for a research statement tailored to their groups. Each school runs its own selection with its own deadline, often once or twice a year with main calls in autumn and winter. Letters of reference (usually two) are standard across schools. Check the individual IMPRS page for exact requirements, as details differ between schools.
required_documents: Online application through the chosen school's own portal (each IMPRS has its own system). Curriculum vitae and academic transcripts for all degrees. Motivation letter or research statement referring to the school's groups and topics. Contact details or letters from usually two academic referees. Proof of English proficiency where requested (many schools accept evidence of English-medium education). Degree certificates, with translations where documents are not in English or German.
summary: The International Max Planck Research Schools (IMPRS) are structured PhD programs run by Max Planck Institutes together with…

title: Georg Forster Research Fellowship (Germany, Developing Countries)
description: The Georg Forster Research Fellowship, run by the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation, funds postdoctoral and experienced researchers from…
details:
The Georg Forster Research Fellowship, run by the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation, funds postdoctoral and experienced researchers from developing and transition countries to pursue their own research project in Germany. Fellows receive about EUR 3,000 per month for up to 24 months, plus family allowances, a German language course and travel support.

The distinctive requirement is relevance: your research should address questions important to the further development of your home country or region. Any discipline qualifies, from public health and agriculture to engineering and social sciences. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis, and Pakistan, Nigeria, Kenya, Bangladesh and most of Africa, Asia and Latin America are on the eligible country list.
benefits: Monthly fellowship in the region of EUR 3,000 for postdoctoral researchers, with a higher rate for the experienced-researcher track. Fellowship duration of 6 to 24 months (postdocs) or 6 to 18 months (experienced researchers), divisible into several stays. Family allowances, a travel lump sum, insurance contributions and an intensive German language course before or during the stay. Research-cost subsidy available to the German host, plus individual support from the Foundation's staff. Alumni benefits designed for development contexts, including return fellowships and equipment or literature support to help you re-establish research at home. Entry into the worldwide Humboldt Network, one of the strongest academic alumni communities anywhere.
requirements: Researchers who are nationals of a developing or emerging country on the Foundation's current country list and whose main residence and work is there. Postdoctoral applicants completed their doctorate within the last four years; experienced researchers within the last twelve years with an independent profile. Your research project must be relevant to the further development of your home country or region, which is the defining feature of this fellowship compared with the standard Humboldt Research Fellowship. A written hosting agreement from an academic host at a German university or research institution is required before applying. Above-average academic record with key publications in internationally reviewed journals. Applicants may not have lived in Germany for extended periods immediately before applying, mirroring the Humboldt mobility rules. All disciplines are eligible, from agriculture and health to engineering, social sciences and governance.
required_documents: Online application through the Humboldt Foundation application portal. Research proposal explaining both the science and its relevance to development in your home country or region, agreed with your host. Host's statement and confirmation of research facilities at the German institution. Curriculum vitae and full publication list with key papers. Doctoral degree certificate. Expert reviews arranged according to the portal instructions.
summary: The Georg Forster Research Fellowship, run by the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation, funds postdoctoral and experienced researchers from…

title: Humboldt Research Fellowship (Germany)
description: The Humboldt Research Fellowship is Germany’s most prestigious postdoctoral award, funding researchers of any nationality and any discipline…
details:
The Humboldt Research Fellowship is Germany’s most prestigious postdoctoral award, funding researchers of any nationality and any discipline to carry out a self-designed project at a German host institution. Postdocs receive EUR 3,000 per month for 6 to 24 months, while experienced researchers receive EUR 3,600 per month for 6 to 18 months, with generous family, language and travel benefits on top.

There are no quotas by country or field: the only criterion is the quality of your research record and proposal, endorsed by a German host. Applications are accepted year round, with selection meetings three times a year, and the new call system opens intake windows in March, July and November.
benefits: Monthly fellowship of EUR 3,000 (postdoctoral) or EUR 3,600 (experienced researchers), including mobility and insurance components. Fellowships of 6 to 24 months (postdoc) or 6 to 18 months (experienced), which can be split into up to three stays within three years. Family allowances (around EUR 340 per month for a partner and EUR 270 per child), a travel lump sum and an intensive German course of two to four months. The German host can apply for a research-cost subsidy, and the Foundation provides individual mentoring throughout. Lifelong membership of the Humboldt Network of more than 30,000 alumni, including dozens of Nobel laureates, with alumni sponsorship and return-visit funding. Roughly 20 to 25 percent of applications succeed, making it demanding but realistic for strong profiles.
requirements: Researchers of all nationalities and all disciplines who want to carry out their own research project in Germany. Postdoctoral track: doctorate completed within the last four years; experienced-researcher track: doctorate completed within the last twelve years with an independent academic profile. A written agreement from an academic host at a German university or research institution is required before applying; the Foundation does not match you with hosts. Key publications in peer-reviewed venues; fresh PhD graduates should wait until the main thesis papers are published or accepted. The project should be a clear step beyond your doctoral work, and returning to a former long-term supervisor or host is generally rejected. Applicants must have lived outside Germany for at least 12 of the 18 months before applying. Language: good English is sufficient for the natural sciences and engineering; humanities and social sciences may require German where the project needs it.
required_documents: Online application through the Humboldt Foundation portal. Research proposal agreed in detail with your German host, including timeline and duration. Host's statement and confirmation of research facilities (uploaded by the host; your file is only forwarded once the host documents are in). Curriculum vitae and complete list of publications, with key publications highlighted and available. Doctoral certificate and, where relevant, evidence of academic independence for the experienced track. Two expert reviews arranged as specified in the portal instructions.
summary: The Humboldt Research Fellowship is Germany’s most prestigious postdoctoral award, funding researchers of any nationality and any discipline…

title: ISTA PhD Program (Institute of Science and Technology Austria)
university: Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA)
description: The ISTA PhD Program at the Institute of Science and Technology Austria offers fully funded, salaried doctoral positions…
details:
The ISTA PhD Program at the Institute of Science and Technology Austria offers fully funded, salaried doctoral positions just outside Vienna in Klosterneuburg. There are no tuition fees and no application fee: every admitted student is employed with an internationally competitive salary and full social security for the entire PhD.

ISTA is unusual because students are admitted to the institute first and choose their research group after rotations, across biology, neuroscience, physics, mathematics, computer science, chemistry and data science. A bachelor’s degree is sufficient to apply. The annual deadline for the 2027 intake is January 8, 2027, and all study is in English.
benefits: Employment at ISTA with an internationally competitive salary and full social security for the whole PhD, typically on five-year contracts. No tuition fees at any point and no fee to apply. First-year rotations in different groups so you choose your thesis lab after seeing the science from the inside. Access to top facilities in bioimaging, electron microscopy, nanofabrication and high-performance computing on a modern campus 25 minutes from Vienna. Funding for conferences and workshops plus structured career development for academia and industry. ISTA has ranked among the world's strongest young institutes, including a top-three normalized Nature Index ranking.
requirements: Bachelor's or master's degree in biology, chemistry, neuroscience, mathematics, computer science, physics, data science and scientific computing, astronomy, earth science or a related area. Bachelor's-only entrants join a combined track with a coursework phase before full research, so a master's is not required. Open to all nationalities; the working language of the institute is English. Strong academic record and demonstrated research potential; prior research experience through internships or thesis work strengthens the file considerably. Three referees willing to submit letters of recommendation through the online system. Willingness to complete rotations in up to three research groups in the first year before affiliating with a lab. The programme starts uniformly on September 15 each year and the start date is non-negotiable.
required_documents: Online application through the ISTA application portal (open from late October to the deadline; desktop browser required). Statement of Purpose describing your research experience, motivation, skills and the ISTA groups that interest you. Short written answers naming up to three preferred research groups and discussing a paper by an ISTA professor (with DOI) in your own words. University transcripts and diplomas for all degrees, in English and the original language. Curriculum vitae. Contact details for three referees; letters are due January 12, 2027 (23:59 CET).
summary: The ISTA PhD Program at the Institute of Science and Technology Austria offers fully funded, salaried doctoral positions…

title: Vienna BioCenter PhD Program (Austria)
university: Vienna BioCenter (IMP, IMBA, GMI, Max Perutz Labs)
description: The Vienna BioCenter PhD Program is a fully funded, salaried doctoral position at one of Europe’s leading life…
details:
The Vienna BioCenter PhD Program is a fully funded, salaried doctoral position at one of Europe’s leading life science hubs, home to institutes such as IMP, IMBA, GMI and the Max Perutz Labs. PhD students are employed with a gross salary of roughly EUR 39,000 to 42,900 per year, full social insurance and no tuition barrier.

Research spans molecular biology, neuroscience, immunology, plant science, biochemistry and computational biology, all in English within an international community of more than 40 nationalities. Selection runs twice a year, and the main autumn call closes on October 15, 2026 for interviews in Vienna with paid travel.
benefits: Full employment contract as a PhD researcher with a salary of roughly EUR 39,000 to 42,900 gross per year (2025 level), plus Austrian social insurance. Four-year structured PhD across more than 70 research groups at the IMP, IMBA, GMI and Max Perutz Labs, with degrees awarded by the University of Vienna or the Medical University of Vienna. Access to world-class core facilities; the campus motto is that there is virtually no experiment that cannot be done at the VBC. Help with visas and residence permits, refunded permit costs for newcomers, German courses and an active welcome office. Training programme covering scientific writing, presentation and career development, with funds for conferences. Vienna is regularly ranked among the most liveable cities in the world, and students can live comfortably on the salary.
requirements: Master's degree (or equivalent) in the life sciences or a related field such as molecular biology, biochemistry, genetics, chemistry, physics, computer science or medicine. The official master's certificate and transcripts must be available at the latest six months after the application deadline. Prior full-time research experience (for example a master's thesis project or internships) makes an application much stronger. High proficiency in written and spoken English; a formal test (IELTS, TOEFL or CPE) is recommended but not mandatory. Open to all nationalities; around 25 to 30 students are admitted per call from more than 2,000 applicants. Two referees are mandatory (a third is optional) and must submit before the deadline. Students with only a bachelor's degree are advised to complete a master's first, for example in Vienna.
required_documents: Online application through the VBC application portal (opens with each call). Three short essays inside the form: past research experience, scientific interests for the PhD, and a motivation letter. University transcripts and diplomas from all degree programmes, in English and in the original language. Curriculum vitae. Contact details of two mandatory referees (third optional), who submit their letters through the reference module. English test result (IELTS, TOEFL or CPE) if available; recommended but not required.
summary: The Vienna BioCenter PhD Program is a fully funded, salaried doctoral position at one of Europe’s leading life…

title: Rotary Yoneyama Memorial Scholarship (Japan, Overseas Applicants)
description: The Rotary Yoneyama Memorial Scholarship is Japan’s largest private scholarship for international students, and its overseas application route…
details:
The Rotary Yoneyama Memorial Scholarship is Japan’s largest private scholarship for international students, and its overseas application route lets you apply before ever setting foot in Japan. It pays a generous monthly stipend of JPY 100,000 to 145,000 depending on level, plus an arrival airfare reimbursement, while you complete a degree at a Japanese university.

What makes Yoneyama special is the Rotary community itself: every scholar is paired with a counselor and a local Rotary club, turning the scholarship into a genuine cultural bridge rather than just funding. The overseas application window is fixed each year from October 1 to October 31, and candidates apply roughly 18 months before enrollment.
benefits: Monthly stipend of JPY 100,000 for undergraduates or JPY 140,000 for master's and doctoral students, paid for the scholarship period set by the Foundation (two years for graduate students). Economy airfare to Japan reimbursed up to JPY 250,000 after arrival. Personal mentoring through a local Rotary club, which is unusual among Japanese scholarships and gives real community support. One of Japan's largest privately funded scholarship programmes, with a nationwide alumni network. A Certificate of Acceptance from the Foundation that serves as financial proof for the student visa process. Note: tuition and entrance fees are not covered, though the stipend can be combined with university tuition waivers.
requirements: Non-Japanese citizen residing outside Japan who is scheduled to enroll in a regular degree programme (bachelor's, master's or doctoral) at a Japanese university or graduate school. Applies to enrollment in April or in the fall (September/October) of the following year; research students and language-school students are not eligible. You must apply to your chosen Japanese university or graduate school yourself before applying for this scholarship, and submit a copy of that admission application. Basic Japanese ability of around JLPT N4 level is expected (requirements can vary by Rotary district). Graduate applicants need a recommendation letter from a supervisor or professor at the target graduate school. Recipients join a local sponsor Rotary club (sewa club), attend monthly meetings, give talks and submit activity reports in Japanese. The scholarship generally cannot be combined with another scholarship of a similar nature.
required_documents: Application for Scholarship form (downloaded from the Foundation website). Research plan at the Japanese university (graduate applicants). Essay on the set topic: why you chose to study in Japan and your plans after studying in Japan. Recommendation letter (from your target graduate school supervisor for graduate applicants). Copy of your application for admission to the Japanese university or graduate school. Japanese language proficiency evidence (JLPT result if available). Passport or identity document and academic transcripts as instructed in the guidelines.
summary: The Rotary Yoneyama Memorial Scholarship is Japan’s largest private scholarship for international students, and its overseas application route…

title: Schlumberger Foundation Faculty for the Future Fellowship (Women in STEM)
description: The Schlumberger Foundation Faculty for the Future Fellowship is a fully funded PhD and postdoctoral award for women…
details:
The Schlumberger Foundation Faculty for the Future Fellowship is a fully funded PhD and postdoctoral award for women in STEM from developing and emerging countries. It funds doctoral or postdoctoral research in science, technology, engineering and mathematics at leading universities abroad, with grants of up to USD 50,000 per year sized to actual study and living costs.

The fellowship exists to build a pipeline of women who return home to take up faculty positions and inspire the next generation into science. Since 2004 it has supported more than 800 women from over 80 countries, and it renews yearly until the degree is complete. Applications for the 2027 award year are open until November 6, 2026.
benefits: Grant based on actual eligible expenses, up to USD 50,000 per year for PhD studies and up to USD 40,000 per year for post-doctoral research. Renewable each year through to completion, subject to performance, supervisor recommendations and evidence of re-integration plans in the home country. Covers costs such as tuition and fees, living expenses, travel and other approved study costs at your host university. Membership of a global community of more than 900 Faculty for the Future alumnae from over 90 countries. Strong career signal: the programme is one of the best-known fellowships for women scientists from the Global South.
requirements: Woman and a citizen of an eligible developing or emerging economy where women are underrepresented in STEM; the country list is reviewed every year on the Foundation's website. Not a holder of dual citizenship where one citizenship is of a developed country. Preparing for a PhD degree or post-doctoral research in science, technology, engineering or mathematics; the current call especially welcomes Physical Sciences, Engineering, Computer Science and Mathematics. Applied to, admitted to, or currently enrolled at a university or research institute abroad (outside your home country) at the time of application. Excellent academic record with demonstrated leadership, community outreach, and a track record of encouraging girls and women into STEM. Committed to returning to your home country after the fellowship to strengthen STEM teaching, research or policy there. Master's-level study is not funded, and awards in biological sciences are limited to interdisciplinary research with the physical sciences.
required_documents: Online application submitted through the Faculty for the Future portal (fftf.slb.com). Academic CV and full academic transcripts. Proof of application, admission or enrollment at a university or research institute abroad. A clear research statement and budget describing your PhD or post-doc plans. Reference letters submitted through the online system. Evidence of leadership, outreach and activities encouraging women and girls in STEM strengthens the file. Information on any other funding sources you have applied for or hold.
summary: The Schlumberger Foundation Faculty for the Future Fellowship is a fully funded PhD and postdoctoral award for women…

title: Rotary Peace Fellowship – Professional Development Certificate
university: The Rotary Foundation (Rotary International), via the Rotary Peace Center at Chulalongkorn University, Thailand
description: The Rotary Peace Fellowship Professional Development Certificate is offered by The Rotary Foundation (Rotary International) through a Rotary…
details:
The Rotary Peace Fellowship Professional Development Certificate is offered by The Rotary Foundation (Rotary International) through a Rotary Peace Center, delivered for the Asia program at Chulalongkorn University in Thailand. It is a fully funded, shorter alternative to the master’s fellowship, designed for experienced mid-career professionals in peace and development.

The award is fully funded, covering full tuition and programme fees, room and board during the residential sessions, round-trip international airfare, and field-study and social-change-initiative expenses, for a roughly three-month professional development certificate (combining intensive residential study with applied project work). Fellows access Rotary Peace Center faculty and research resources.

Eligibility is for mid-career professionals with at least five years of relevant work experience in peacebuilding, conflict resolution, humanitarian action, or development, who bring a social-change initiative to develop during the programme and have a strong commitment to cross-cultural understanding. You apply through the Rotary Peace Fellowship online application, with support from a local Rotary district, submitting a CV showing your experience, a personal essay on your peace work, your social-change-initiative proposal, and three recommendation letters, by the annual deadline (around 15 May). For experienced practitioners seeking a shorter, fully funded programme, it is a strong option; confirm the current host and cycle on the Rotary website. (Note: this certificate has historically been hosted at Chulalongkorn University; confirm the current location.)
benefits: Full tuition and programme fees. Room and board during the residential sessions in Thailand. Round-trip international airfare. Field-study and social-change-initiative expenses. Access to Rotary Peace Center faculty and research resources.
requirements: Mid-career professional with at least five years of relevant work experience in peacebuilding, conflict resolution, humanitarian action, or development. Bring a social-change initiative to develop during the programme. A strong commitment to cross-cultural understanding and peace. Support from a local Rotary district.
required_documents: Completed Rotary Peace Fellowship online application. Curriculum vitae showing 5+ years of relevant experience. Personal essay on peace work and social-change initiative. Social-change-initiative proposal. Three letters of recommendation.
summary: The Rotary Peace Fellowship Professional Development Certificate is offered by The Rotary Foundation (Rotary International) through a Rotary…

title: Saudi Arabia Government Scholarship (Ministry of Education)
university: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Ministry of Education (MOE)
description: The Saudi Arabia Government Scholarship is offered by the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Education through the…
details:
The Saudi Arabia Government Scholarship is offered by the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Education through the Study in Saudi platform to support international students across diploma, bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral study at Saudi universities. It is a fully funded national scheme that opens Saudi higher education to students from around the world.

The award is fully funded, covering full tuition fees, a monthly living allowance, free accommodation, return airfare, health insurance, and Arabic language training, for the duration of the chosen programme. It supports study across a network of Saudi universities, with a strong package for living and study in the Kingdom.

Eligibility is by level, generally under 25 for a bachelor’s, under 30 for a master’s, and under 35 for a PhD, with a good-health certificate, no criminal record, and not currently holding another Saudi scholarship. You apply through the Study in Saudi platform, selecting your preferred universities and programmes, and submit your academic certificates and transcripts, identity documents, a medical report, and language results by the intake deadline, with placement and award subject to the Ministry’s selection. For international students aiming at Saudi Arabia, it is a generous, fully funded national scholarship; confirm the current intake windows on the Study in Saudi platform.
benefits: Full tuition fees. Monthly living allowance. Free accommodation. Return airfare. Health insurance and Arabic language training.
requirements: Generally under 25 for a bachelor's, under 30 for a master's, and under 35 for a PhD. A good-health certificate. No criminal record. Not currently holding another Saudi scholarship. Meet the academic and language requirements for the chosen programme.
required_documents: Study in Saudi platform application. Academic certificates and transcripts. Identity documents. Good-health or medical report. Language test results. Recommendation letters and a research proposal for postgraduate study.
summary: The Saudi Arabia Government Scholarship is offered by the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Education through the…

title: University of Copenhagen Tuition Fee Waiver (Master’s)
description: The University of Copenhagen Tuition Fee Waiver is offered by the University of Copenhagen (UCPH), Scandinavia’s largest and…
details:
The University of Copenhagen Tuition Fee Waiver is offered by the University of Copenhagen (UCPH), Scandinavia’s largest and highest-ranked university, to support fee-paying international master’s students. It is a tuition waiver that rewards a strong academic record and helps non-EU students study at a leading Danish university. It is distinct from the university’s salaried PhD fellowships.

The award is partial funding, providing a full or partial tuition fee waiver (tuition for non-EU master’s students ranges from around 75,000 to 120,000 Danish kroner a year), for the duration of the master’s programme. It does not cover living costs, but Copenhagen offers an outstanding quality of life, a strong cycling culture, and good work-life balance.

Eligibility is for non-EU/EEA citizens required to pay tuition fees who have applied for an English-taught master’s programme at the University of Copenhagen, with a strong academic record and meeting all the chosen programme’s admission requirements. You apply for your master’s programme through the university’s online application, indicating interest in the tuition waiver where required, and submit your transcripts, motivation letter, references (for some programmes), and English proficiency by the deadline, with competitive merit-based selection. For fee-paying master’s students aiming at Denmark, it is a valuable tuition award; confirm the current scheme on the University of Copenhagen scholarships page.
benefits: Full or partial tuition fee waiver (tuition for non-EU master's students ranges from around DKK 75,000 to 120,000 a year). Study at Scandinavia's largest and highest-ranked university. An outstanding quality of life, cycling culture, and work-life balance. A Danish residence permit for the study period (the scholarship does not cover living costs).
requirements: Non-EU/EEA citizen required to pay tuition fees. Applied for an English-taught master's programme at the University of Copenhagen. A strong academic record. Meet all admission requirements of the chosen programme. Distinct from the university's salaried PhD fellowships.
required_documents: University of Copenhagen online application. Bachelor's degree certificate and transcripts. English language proficiency (IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL 83). Curriculum vitae. Motivation letter. Reference letters (for some programmes). Passport copy.
summary: The University of Copenhagen Tuition Fee Waiver is offered by the University of Copenhagen (UCPH), Scandinavia’s largest and…

title: KTH Tuition Fee Scholarship
description: The KTH Tuition Fee Scholarship is offered by KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Sweden’s most prestigious technical university,…
details:
The KTH Tuition Fee Scholarship is offered by KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Sweden’s most prestigious technical university, to support fee-paying international students undertaking a master’s. It is a tuition waiver that rewards academic excellence and helps non-EU students study engineering and technology in Stockholm.

The award is partial funding, providing a full or partial tuition fee waiver (tuition is roughly 155,000 to 310,000 Swedish kronor a year depending on the programme), for the one or two years of the master’s programme. It does not cover living costs, but it gives access to Sweden’s leading technical university in Stockholm, a major innovation hub.

Eligibility is for non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens required to pay tuition fees who have applied for a master’s programme at KTH through universityadmissions.se, with excellent academic performance and meeting the chosen programme’s admission requirements. You first apply to your KTH master’s programme via universityadmissions.se as a fee-paying student and pay the application fee, then submit the KTH scholarship application during the scholarship round, with merit-based selection. For excellent fee-paying master’s students aiming at Sweden, it is a valuable tuition award; confirm the current dates on the KTH scholarships page.
benefits: Full or partial tuition fee waiver (tuition is roughly SEK 155,000 to 310,000 a year depending on programme). Access to Sweden's most prestigious technical university. Study in Stockholm, a major innovation hub. A Swedish residence permit for the study period (the scholarship does not cover living costs).
requirements: Non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizen required to pay tuition fees. Applied for a master's programme at KTH through universityadmissions.se. Excellent academic performance in prior studies. Meet the admission requirements of the chosen programme.
required_documents: Application through universityadmissions.se. Bachelor's degree certificate and transcripts. English language proficiency (IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL 90). Curriculum vitae. Motivation letter (for some programmes). Letters of recommendation (for some programmes).

title: MEXT Scholarship – Embassy Recommendation (Japan)

details:
The AFR (Aides a la Formation-Recherche) PhD Grant is offered by the University of Luxembourg together with the Luxembourg National Research Fund (FNR) to support doctoral researchers, with a master’s funding option also available. It is a salaried PhD scheme open to candidates of any nationality, funding research at Luxembourg host institutions.

The AFR PhD provides an employment contract with a salary contribution of around 44,322 euros a year (the employer may top up to a maximum gross of around 62,461), plus a 6,000-euro training and mobility allowance and a one-off travel lump sum, for up to four years. A separate master’s option offers low enrolment fees (around 200 euros per semester for most programmes) plus the Guillaume Dupaix International Master’s Scholarship of 11,000 euros a year for up to two years.

Eligibility for the AFR Incoming PhD is open to candidates of any nationality who secure a doctoral position at an eligible Luxembourg host institution and spend more than 50 percent of the time in Luxembourg; the application is submitted jointly by the candidate and the host institution. You identify a doctoral position and supervisor at a Luxembourg host (for example the University of Luxembourg) and submit the AFR application jointly with the host by the annual deadline through the FNR system. For doctoral researchers aiming at Luxembourg, the AFR grant is a well-paid, employment-based route.

The University of Helsinki, Finland’s leading research university, offers scholarships to non-EU/EEA international students undertaking English-taught master’s programmes. The awards are tuition-fee waivers (with some including a relocation grant) that reward academic excellence and help international students afford study in Finland.

The award is partial funding, providing a full or partial (50 percent) tuition fee waiver (covering fees of around 13,000 to 18,000 euros a year), renewable on completing about 55 ECTS per year; a limited number of Finland Scholarships add a 100 percent waiver plus a 5,000-euro relocation grant. The scholarships do not cover living costs, but a Finnish residence permit allows part-time work and a pathway to a post-study work permit.

Eligibility is for non-EU/EEA/Swiss students liable to pay tuition fees, eligible for and applying to an eligible English-taught master’s programme at Helsinki, with excellent previous results and motivation. There is no separate scholarship form: you answer the scholarship questions within the same master’s application on Studyinfo.fi during the application round (around mid-January) and submit the required attachments by the document deadline. Programmes award 50 or 100 percent tuition-fee waivers (the majority are 50 percent). For non-EU master’s students aiming at Finland, it is a valuable tuition award.

The award provides a full tuition waiver and an annual stipend of around 22,000 US dollars, for the duration of the graduate programme (appointed by semester or year). Assistants commit a set number of hours per week to research, gain hands-on research experience, and study in the United States, often without an IELTS requirement.

Eligibility for this representative position is for applicants with a B.S. in wildlife, ecology, biology, forestry, zoology, or a related field, with strong quantitative skills and familiarity with R and spatial software such as QGIS or ArcGIS, who can conduct independent fieldwork in challenging conditions, communicate well, and work in a team (a driver’s license is preferred). title: Slovak Government Scholarship

details:
The Slovak Government Scholarship, delivered through the National Scholarship Programme (NSP) of the Ministry of Education, supports international students, PhD candidates, researchers, and lecturers to undertake mobility stays at Slovak universities and research institutions. It is open to citizens of all countries and funds study and research periods rather than full degrees.

The award provides a tuition waiver at a Slovak public university, a monthly stipend (from around 280 euros for students to 580 for PhD candidates and researchers), accommodation support through university dormitories, and access to university facilities and research labs, for mobility stays (one to two semesters for students; one to ten months for PhD students, researchers, and lecturers).

Eligibility is for citizens of any country other than Slovakia who are master’s-level students (having completed at least about 2.5 years in the same programme), PhD students, or university teachers, researchers, or artists whose home studies or work are outside Slovakia, and who are accepted or invited by a Slovak host; you cannot hold another publicly funded scholarship for the same stay. You secure an acceptance or invitation letter from your Slovak host, then apply online via the NSP portal with your enrolment confirmation, transcripts, and supporting documents. For students and researchers seeking a funded stay in central Europe, it is a flexible, supportive scheme.
benefits: Full tuition waiver at a Slovak public university. Monthly stipend of EUR 280 (student) to EUR 580 (PhD or research). Accommodation support through university dormitories. Access to university facilities and research labs. Cultural integration support.
requirements: Citizen of any country other than Slovakia. A master's-level student (having completed at least about 2.5 years in the same programme), a PhD student, or a university teacher, researcher, or artist whose home studies or work are outside Slovakia. Accepted or invited by a Slovak higher education or research institution for a mobility stay. Cannot hold another publicly funded scholarship for the same stay (e.g. Erasmus+, CEEPUS, Visegrad). Good academic standing.
required_documents: Online application form via the SAIA / NSP portal. Academic transcripts and degree certificates. Curriculum vitae. Research or study plan. Letter of acceptance from a Slovak host (or confirmation of contact). Passport copy. Health certificate.

title: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology (Skoltech) PhD Fellowship

details:
The Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology (Skoltech) is a private graduate research university near Moscow, founded in collaboration with international partners and focused on science, technology, and innovation. It offers fully funded master’s and doctoral places, taught in English, in fields such as data science, engineering, life sciences, and energy.

The award is fully funded, covering full tuition, a monthly stipend (around 40,000 rubles for the MSc and 75,000 for the PhD), medical insurance, academic mobility and conference funding, and a one-time airfare grant for international students, for the programme duration (two years for the master’s, three to four for the PhD). Scholars work with world-class labs and equipment.

Eligibility is for those who hold (or are completing) a bachelor’s for the MSc, or a master’s or specialist degree for the PhD, in a relevant science or engineering field, with a strong academic record and English proficiency (all programmes are in English; no IELTS or GRE is mandatory, though a test may be set at Selection Days). For the PhD you identify and contact a Skoltech faculty supervisor and prepare a research proposal, then submit the online application with transcripts, a motivation letter, and recommendation letters, and attend Selection Days. All admitted students are automatically funded. For research-focused students, Skoltech is a strong, fully funded option.
benefits: Full tuition waiver. Monthly stipend (around RUB 40,000 MSc, RUB 75,000 PhD). Medical insurance. Academic mobility and conference funding. Access to world-class labs and equipment. A one-time airfare grant for international students.
requirements: A bachelor's for the MSc, or a master's or specialist degree for the PhD, in a relevant science or engineering field. Strong academic record. title: Seoul National University Global Scholarship
university: Seoul National University (SNU), Office of Global Affairs

details:
The Seoul National University (SNU) Global Scholarship supports international graduate students at SNU, South Korea’s most prestigious university. It combines a tuition waiver with a monthly living allowance and campus support, enabling talented students from around the world to undertake master’s and doctoral study in Seoul across all academic disciplines.

The award covers a full tuition fee waiver, a monthly living allowance of around 1,100,000 Korean won, a settlement allowance on arrival, health insurance, and Korean language training support, for the duration of the graduate programme (awarded each semester). Scholars gain access to SNU’s world-class research facilities and the experience of studying in one of Asia’s most dynamic cities.

Eligibility is for non-Korean citizens (both applicant and parents must not be Korean citizens) who hold a bachelor’s (for master’s) or a master’s (for PhD), demonstrate outstanding academic achievement, and meet the English or Korean language requirements, with at least one regular semester remaining. You apply online through your mySNU account when the Global Scholarship notice opens (or submit documents to the Office of Global Affairs), after receiving SNU admission; benefits vary by award category and individual circumstances. For international graduate students aiming at Korea, SNU is a leading, well-supported choice.
benefits: Full tuition fee waiver. Monthly living allowance of about KRW 1,100,000. Settlement allowance on arrival. Health insurance. Korean language training support. Access to SNU's world-class research facilities.
requirements: Non-Korean citizen (both applicant and parents must not be Korean citizens). A bachelor's (for master's) or a master's (for PhD). Outstanding academic achievement. required_documents: SNU online application form. Academic transcripts and degree certificates. Study plan or research proposal. Two letters of recommendation. title: Said Foundation Scholarship

details:
The Said Foundation Scholarship supports talented students from the Middle East to undertake a one-year master’s degree in the United Kingdom. The Foundation works to develop people who will contribute to the development of their home countries, focusing on nationals of Jordan, Lebanon, Palestine, and Syria.

The award is fully funded, covering full tuition fees, a living allowance, return economy airfare, and visa and NHS surcharge costs, for one year of master’s study at a UK partner university. Scholars join a community committed to giving back to their home countries and region.

Eligibility is for those who hold the nationality of and are permanently resident in Syria, Jordan, Lebanon, or Palestine, with an undergraduate degree equivalent to a UK 2:1 or higher (or in their final year), demonstrated leadership potential, and a commitment to return home to contribute to development. You apply for a one-year master’s at one of the Foundation’s UK partner universities (non-partner universities are considered only if the course is unavailable at a partner), and apply online via the Said Foundation website during the window with transcripts, a CV, three references, and an English-language certificate. For students from these countries, it is a generous, fully funded route to a UK master’s.
benefits: Full tuition fees. Living allowance. Return economy airfare. Visa and NHS surcharge costs.
requirements: National of and permanently resident in Jordan, Lebanon, Palestine, or Syria. An undergraduate degree equivalent to a UK 2:1 or higher (or in your final year). Demonstrated leadership potential. A commitment to return home to contribute to your country's development. A confirmed (or intended) offer from a UK partner university.
required_documents: Online application. Academic transcripts and certificates. Curriculum vitae. Three references. English-language certificate (e.g. IELTS). UK university offer (where available).

title: Russia Open Doors Scholarship
university: Global Universities Association (Russia), with the Russian Ministry of Science and Higher Education
description: The Open Doors: Russian Scholarship Project is run by the Global Universities Association together with Russia’s Ministry of…
details:
The Open Doors: Russian Scholarship Project is run by the Global Universities Association together with Russia’s Ministry of Science and Higher Education. It is an international competition (olympiad) that allows winners to study tuition-free at participating top Russian universities, across bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral levels, with admission granted without the usual university entrance exams.

The award covers full tuition at participating universities and a monthly government stipend, for the duration of the chosen programme, plus a one-year Russian preparatory course if needed; accommodation is not covered, so dormitory costs should be budgeted separately. Winners gain admission under the Russian government quota and access to leading universities and research labs.

Eligibility is for international citizens (excluding Russian citizens) who hold or are completing the relevant prior degree for their track (high-school completion for bachelor’s, a bachelor’s for master’s, a master’s for the doctoral track), with no formal GPA cutoff (the olympiad replaces entrance exams) and language proficiency in English or Russian depending on the programme; you cannot hold another Russian government scholarship at the same time. You register free on the Open Doors website during the window, build your portfolio, and take the online competition and second-stage assessments in your subject area. For international students considering Russia, it is a competition-based, fully funded route.
benefits: 100 percent tuition coverage at participating top Russian universities. Monthly government stipend (around RUB 5,000 to 8,000). Admission without university entrance exams. Access to leading Russian universities and research labs. A free preparatory Russian course where needed (budget separately for accommodation).
requirements: Open to international citizens (excluding Russian citizens). Hold or be completing the relevant prior degree for your track (high-school completion for bachelor's, a bachelor's for master's, a master's for the doctoral track). No official GPA cutoff (the olympiad replaces entrance exams), though an excellent record helps. Language proficiency in English or Russian depending on the programme. Cannot hold another Russian government scholarship at the same time.
required_documents: Open Doors online registration and portfolio. Prior degree certificate and transcripts (or proof of current study). Motivation and portfolio materials. Identity document or passport. Language proficiency proof as required.

title: Romanian Government Scholarship

details:
The Romanian Government Scholarship is offered by Romania’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs to support international students from outside the EU to undertake undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral study at Romanian state universities. It is part of Romania’s cooperation and cultural exchange efforts, and includes a preparatory Romanian language year where needed.

The award is fully funded, covering tuition fees, free dormitory accommodation (subject to availability), and a monthly allowance scaled by study level, for the length of the degree plus any preparatory language year. Programmes may be taught in Romanian (with the preparatory year) or, where available, in another language.

Eligibility is for citizens of non-EU countries (EU citizens are not eligible) with a good academic record meeting the scheme’s minimum averages, who are not Romanian citizens and not already beneficiaries of another Romanian state scholarship, and who will study in Romanian unless choosing an available programme in another language. You create an account on the Study in Romania platform when the call opens, upload all documents with certified translations, and rank your university and programme choices, with results and allocations announced by summer. For non-EU students seeking funded study in Europe, it is an accessible, fully funded option.
benefits: Tuition fees fully covered. Free dormitory accommodation (subject to availability). Monthly allowance scaled by study level. Free preparatory Romanian language year.
requirements: Citizen of a non-EU country (EU citizens are not eligible). Good academic record meeting the scheme's minimum averages. Not a Romanian citizen and not already a beneficiary of another Romanian state scholarship. Study in Romanian (preparatory year provided) unless choosing an available programme in another language.
required_documents: Online application on the Study in Romania platform. Legalized or apostilled diplomas and transcripts with translations. Birth certificate and passport copies. Medical certificate. CV and motivation elements as required.

title: Reach Oxford Scholarship (University of Oxford)
description: The Reach Oxford Scholarship (formerly the Oxford Student Scholarship) is offered by the University of Oxford to support…
details:
The Reach Oxford Scholarship (formerly the Oxford Student Scholarship) is offered by the University of Oxford to support students from low-income countries who, for financial or political reasons, cannot study for a degree in their own country. It is one of the few fully funded undergraduate scholarships at Oxford open to international students.

The award is fully funded, covering full course fees for the duration of the degree, an annual grant for living costs, and one return airfare per year, renewed each year subject to satisfactory progress. It enables talented students who would otherwise be unable to afford Oxford to complete an undergraduate degree there.

Eligibility is for nationals of a country on the OECD DAC list of aid recipients who are unable to fund study at Oxford, applying for (or holding an offer for) an undergraduate course other than Medicine, pursuing their first undergraduate degree, with an excellent academic record meeting Oxford’s entry standards. You first apply to Oxford via UCAS by the October deadline, sit any required admissions tests and interviews, and then submit the Reach Oxford application when it opens in January; selection takes place in spring with results by the end of May. For students from developing countries, it is a rare, fully funded route to an Oxford undergraduate degree.
benefits: Full course fees for the duration of the degree. Annual grant for living costs. One return air fare per year. Award renewed yearly subject to satisfactory progress.
requirements: National of a country on the OECD DAC list of ODA recipients. Unable to fund study at Oxford for financial or political reasons. Applying for (or holding an offer for) an undergraduate course at Oxford other than Medicine. Pursuing your first undergraduate degree. Excellent academic record meeting Oxford entry standards.
required_documents: UCAS application to Oxford (separate, first step). Scholarship application form when published in January. Financial circumstances information. Supporting statement. Documents per the published guidance.

details:
The Queen Elizabeth Commonwealth Scholarships (QECS) are offered by the Association of Commonwealth Universities through an endowment under the Commonwealth Scholarship and Fellowship Plan. They enable students from across the Commonwealth to undertake a full master’s degree at a university in another Commonwealth country, with a focus on study in low and middle-income nations and on creating change at home.

The award is fully funded, covering full tuition and course-related fees, a monthly living allowance for the full two-year award, return economy flights, a one-off arrival allowance, and a research grant for research-focused degrees, along with membership of the global Commonwealth Scholars alumni network. It supports a two-year, full-time, on-campus master’s.

Eligibility is for citizens of (or refugee-status holders in) a Commonwealth country who hold at least a completed UK 2:1 bachelor’s degree or equivalent, can study at postgraduate level in English, and are applying to a host ACU member university in a low or middle-income Commonwealth country other than their own (there is no upper age limit). You apply online through the ACU myACU portal during a cycle for a listed eligible course, and apply separately to the host university for admission. For students committed to change across the Commonwealth, QECS is a distinctive, fully funded opportunity.
benefits: Full tuition and course-related fees waived. Monthly living allowance for the full two-year award. Return economy flights from home to host country. One-off arrival allowance. Research grant (for research-focused degrees, subject to approval). Membership in the global Commonwealth Scholars alumni network.
requirements: Citizen of (or refugee-status holder in) a Commonwealth country. Hold at least a completed UK 2:1 (Upper Second-Class Honours) or equivalent. Able to study at postgraduate level in English. Committed to creating change in your home community. Applying to a participating host ACU member university in a low or middle-income Commonwealth country (typically not your home country); no upper age limit.
required_documents: Completed bachelor's degree (2:1 or equivalent). Academic transcripts and certificates. Proof of admission to an eligible host-university course. References. English proficiency where required. Passport copy.

details:
The Prince of Songkla University (PSU) Postdoctoral Fellowship is offered by the Faculty of Science at PSU, a leading research university in southern Thailand. It is aimed at early-career researchers who have recently completed a PhD and want to undertake research under an established PSU professor, strengthening the university’s international research output.

The fellowship is fully funded for the research period, providing a monthly stipend of 31,500 Thai baht, covered round-trip travel for international fellows, research support and facilities, and additional bonuses such as a publication bonus in the second year, for up to two years (the second year renewable on performance). It is a research position rather than a degree programme.

Eligibility is for researchers of any nationality who hold a PhD obtained within about the last five years, with a relevant research background and English proficiency, to conduct research under a PSU professor with active international publications and funded projects. You apply during one of the annual application windows with the required documents and a research plan agreed with a PSU host supervisor. For recent PhD graduates seeking a funded postdoctoral position in Asia, it is a solid opportunity to build a research record.
benefits: Monthly stipend of THB 31,500. Round-trip travel expenses covered. Research support and facilities. Additional bonuses and allowances (including a publication bonus in the second year).

title: PEEF Scholarship (Punjab Educational Endowment Fund)
university: Punjab Educational Endowment Fund (PEEF), Government of the Punjab

details:
The PEEF Scholarship is the flagship programme of the Punjab Educational Endowment Fund, a body of the Government of the Punjab in Pakistan, which provides a wide range of scholarships to talented students from low-income families. The programme spans school, undergraduate, and postgraduate levels, and is one of the largest needs-based scholarship schemes in the province.

The award covers full tuition, a monthly living stipend (varying by host country for overseas study), round-trip airfare, health insurance, and a book and study materials allowance, for the duration of the enrolled programme. It is designed to remove financial barriers so that academically strong students can continue their education.

Eligibility is for permanent residents of Punjab (with quota seats for AJK, Gilgit-Baltistan, the Merged Districts, ICT, and special categories such as orphans, minorities, and students with disabilities) from low-income households, who have secured at least 60 percent marks in their last annual examination and are enrolled in a government-recognised institution; for overseas study, higher academic and test thresholds apply. You apply online during the announced window via the PEEF website, then submit the printed form with documents through your institution for verification, with students already holding another scholarship usually ineligible. For students from low-income families in Punjab, PEEF is a major route to funded education.
benefits: Full tuition fees. Monthly living stipend (varies by host country for overseas study). Round-trip airfare. Health insurance. Book and study materials allowance.
requirements: Permanent resident of Punjab (with quota seats for AJK, Gilgit-Baltistan, the Merged Districts, ICT, and special categories). From a low-income household. At least 60 percent marks in your last annual examination. Enrolled in a government-recognised institution. For overseas study, higher academic and test thresholds (such as GRE and IELTS) apply; students already holding another scholarship are usually ineligible.
required_documents: PEEF online application form. Academic transcripts and certificates. GRE and IELTS or TOEFL scores (for overseas study). Income certificate. Domicile certificate (Punjab). University admission letter. Two recommendation letters. CNIC and passport.

title: Oxford Pershing Square Scholarship

details:
The Oxford Pershing Square Scholarship is offered by the University of Oxford’s Said Business School, funded by the Pershing Square Foundation, to support outstanding individuals committed to tackling major social challenges. It is tied to Oxford’s distinctive 1+1 MBA programme, which combines a one-year subject master’s with the one-year Oxford MBA.

The award is fully funded, covering full tuition for both years of the 1+1 programme (the master’s plus the MBA) and a living costs grant, along with a leadership programme and mentoring. Scholars develop the skills to create scalable solutions to global problems while studying at one of the world’s leading universities.

Eligibility is for those admitted to Oxford’s 1+1 MBA programme, of any nationality, with strong academics, leadership potential, integrity, and a clear vision for creating scalable solutions to global social challenges. You apply to both an eligible partnering one-year master’s (by its own deadline) and the Oxford MBA (by the 1+1 MBA deadline), and upload the scholarship essay answering how you intend to change the world (up to 500 words) in the Funding section of the MBA application; shortlisted candidates are interviewed. For socially driven leaders, it is a flagship fully funded route through Oxford.
benefits: Full tuition for both years (master's and MBA). Living costs grant. Leadership programme and mentoring.
requirements: Admitted to Oxford's 1+1 MBA programme. Demonstrated commitment to social impact. Strong academic and professional record. Leadership potential, integrity, and a vision for scalable solutions to global challenges. Open to all nationalities.

details:
The NUS Global Merit Scholarship is a prestigious undergraduate award from the National University of Singapore, consistently ranked among the world’s leading universities. It recognises incoming students with outstanding academic results and strong leadership, and it offers not only financial support but enrichment opportunities designed to develop well-rounded graduates.

The award is generous, covering full tuition fees, an annual living allowance of around 6,000 Singapore dollars, hostel accommodation, overseas enrichment programmes, and a computer allowance, for the normal duration of the undergraduate degree. Scholars join a community of high achievers with access to global exposure.

Eligibility is for incoming freshmen with outstanding academic results (Singapore-Cambridge GCE A level, a local polytechnic diploma, the IB Diploma, the NUS High School Diploma, or equivalent), strong leadership and co-curricular records, of any nationality. You submit the single common NUS Scholarships application alongside your NUS undergraduate admission application, and shortlisted applicants are interviewed. For top undergraduates aiming at Singapore, the Global Merit Scholarship is a leading, comprehensive award.
benefits: Full tuition fees. Annual living allowance of around S$6,000. Hostel accommodation. Overseas enrichment programmes. Computer allowance.
requirements: Outstanding academic results (GCE A level, polytechnic diploma, IB Diploma, NUS High School Diploma, or equivalent). Strong leadership and co-curricular record. All nationalities.

title: NTU Research Scholarship

details:
The NTU Research Scholarship supports outstanding international and local students to undertake a higher research degree at Nanyang Technological University in Singapore, one of Asia’s top universities. It provides a tuition subsidy and a monthly stipend so that scholars can focus on research, typically toward a PhD, within NTU’s strong research environment.

The award is fully funded for the duration of the research programme (typically up to four years for a PhD), covering full tuition together with a monthly stipend of around 2,200 Singapore dollars with potential increases, an annual research support grant, conference travel funding, and access to advanced research facilities. It is renewable each year subject to progress.

Eligibility is for students who hold a bachelor’s degree (for direct PhD) or a master’s degree with strong academic performance (First Class or Second Upper Honours or equivalent), demonstrate research aptitude, and meet English requirements; it is open to all nationalities and requires a commitment to full-time research. You apply together with your NTU graduate programme admission application, indicating your interest in the scholarship and submitting transcripts, references, and English scores, and you must not hold another financial award. For research students aiming at Singapore, it is a leading, fully funded opportunity.
benefits: Full tuition subsidy for the duration of studies (typically up to four years). Monthly stipend of around S$2,200 with potential increases. Annual research support grant. Conference travel funding. Access to state-of-the-art research facilities. The opportunity to live and study in Singapore.
requirements: A bachelor's degree (for direct PhD) or a master's degree with strong academic performance. Strong honours-level results (First Class or Second Upper Honours or equivalent). Demonstrated research aptitude and interest. English proficiency (IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL 85 for most programmes). Open to all nationalities; commitment to full-time research.

title: Mexico AMEXCID Scholarship

details:
The AMEXCID Scholarship is offered by the Government of Mexico through the Mexican Agency for International Development Cooperation, under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. It supports international students and researchers to study or carry out research in Mexico, across undergraduate, master’s, doctoral, and mobility levels, as part of Mexico’s international cooperation and cultural exchange efforts.

The award is fully funded for the chosen programme, covering full tuition at Mexican public universities, a monthly stipend, health insurance, and Spanish language training, for the duration of the studies or the research and mobility period. Scholars study at participating Mexican institutions across a wide range of fields.

Eligibility is for non-Mexican citizens (foreign students not already resident in Mexico) who meet the GPA threshold (around 8.5 on a 10-point scale), hold a bachelor’s degree for master’s study, have a good academic record, and have basic Spanish or a willingness to learn, along with a recent acceptance letter from a participating Mexican institution. You apply online in Spanish through the AMEXCID academic management system during the annual call, uploading transcripts, a study plan, the acceptance letter, and references, with selection made by AMEXCID. For students keen to study in Mexico, it is the main government scholarship.

title: McCall MacBain Scholarships at McGill University
description: The McCall MacBain Scholarships are Canada’s first comprehensive leadership-based scholarships for master’s and professional study, offered at McGill…
details:
The McCall MacBain Scholarships are Canada’s first comprehensive leadership-based scholarships for master’s and professional study, offered at McGill University in Montreal. Created by a landmark gift, they support outstanding individuals not only with full funding but with an extensive programme of mentorship, coaching, and leadership development designed to prepare them to lead and serve.

details:

Administered by ERSU Palermo, the regional authority for the right to university study, it is a need-and-merit-based grant designed to make university affordable for students from lower-income households, including international students.

The support scales with circumstances: an annual maintenance grant from around 1,425 to 8,133 euros depending on residency status and income band, exemption from university tuition fees for scholarship winners, free or subsidised canteen meals, and the option of a place in an ERSU university residence, along with support for international mobility. The grant amount depends on whether you are on-site, a commuter, or off-site. You apply through the studenti.ersupalermo.it portal using SPID or CIE (international students can register via a partnered CAF), complete the income declaration, and submit by the deadline of 22 July 2026. For students with financial need studying in Palermo, it is a generous regional scheme.

Based in Potsdam, Germany, near Berlin, it provides time, space, and a stipend for a bold, interdisciplinary idea, rather than funding the continuation of an academic degree.

The fellowship offers a stipend of 10,000 euros, living accommodation in the Einstein Forum’s villa in Potsdam, and reimbursement of travel costs, for a residency of five to six months. Fellows engage with international scholars and public intellectuals, have access to Berlin’s academic and cultural scene, and present their work publicly at the Einstein Forum.

Eligibility is open to applicants of all nationalities and academic fields who are under 35, hold at least a master’s degree or equivalent, and can propose a project in a field different from their previous research, demonstrating genuine interdisciplinary thinking; they must be able to live in Potsdam for the fellowship period. You apply through the Einstein Forum platform with a CV, a short project proposal, and letters of recommendation by the deadline. For ambitious young thinkers, it is a rare chance to explore a new intellectual direction.
benefits: Stipend of EUR 10,000. Living accommodation in the Einstein Forum villa in Potsdam. Reimbursement of travel expenses to and from Potsdam. Opportunity to engage with international scholars and public intellectuals. Access to Berlin's academic and cultural scene. Public presentation of research at the Einstein Forum.
requirements: Under 35 years of age at the time of application. Hold at least a master's degree or equivalent. Propose a project in a field different from previous research, demonstrating interdisciplinary thinking. Able to reside in Potsdam for the fellowship period (five to six months). Open to all nationalities and academic fields.
required_documents: Online application form. Project proposal in a different field from previous research (three to five pages). Curriculum vitae with a list of publications. Letters of recommendation. Degree certificates. Brief biography.
summary: The Einstein Forum Fellowship, offered by the Einstein Forum together with the Wittenstein Foundation, is an unusual award…

The Glenmore Medical Postgraduate Scholarship is offered by the University of Edinburgh, one of the UK’s leading universities, to support students from Africa to undertake postgraduate study in health and medical disciplines. It is aimed at building healthcare expertise across the continent by funding talented African students to study at Edinburgh and return to contribute to health development at home.

The award is fully funded, covering full tuition fees, a living stipend for the duration of the programme, return international airfare, and a contribution toward accommodation costs. Scholars study a full-time master’s in a health or medical field at Edinburgh’s well-regarded medical school.

Eligibility is for citizens of an African country applying for a full-time postgraduate programme in a health or medical discipline at Edinburgh, who have not previously studied there, hold the equivalent of a UK first or upper second class degree, and show a commitment to health development in Africa. You secure an offer of admission, firmly accept it, and complete the online scholarship application through the MyEd portal with a personal statement, by the deadline. For African health professionals and graduates, it is a valuable, fully funded route to advanced medical study in the UK.
benefits: Full tuition fees. Living stipend for the duration of the programme. Return international airfare. Contribution toward accommodation costs.
requirements: Citizen of an African country. Applying for a full-time postgraduate programme in a health or medical discipline at the University of Edinburgh. title: Canada-ASEAN Scholarships and Educational Exchanges (SEED)
description: The Canada-ASEAN Scholarships and Educational Exchanges for Development (SEED) programme is funded by Global Affairs Canada to bring…
details:
The Canada-ASEAN Scholarships and Educational Exchanges for Development (SEED) programme is funded by Global Affairs Canada to bring students from ASEAN member states to Canadian institutions for short-term study or research exchanges. It is designed to strengthen ties between Canada and Southeast Asia and to support progress on sustainable development goals through education.

The award covers the costs of a short exchange of roughly four to six months: visa and travel costs to and from Canada, health insurance, a living allowance ranging from around 10,200 Canadian dollars for undergraduates to 15,900 for graduate and postdoctoral exchanges, a books and supplies allowance, and a one-time establishment allowance.

Eligibility is for citizens of an ASEAN member state who are enrolled at a recognised post-secondary institution in an ASEAN country, with specific conditions by level (college, undergraduate with at least one year completed, or graduate study). A key feature is that students cannot apply directly: you identify an existing exchange agreement between your home institution and a Canadian institution, and the Canadian host applies on your behalf through the EduCanada portal before the deadline. For students from Southeast Asia seeking funded study or research time in Canada, SEED is a valuable exchange opportunity.
benefits: Visa and travel costs to and from Canada. Health insurance for the duration of the exchange. Living allowance of CAD 10,200 (undergraduate) to 15,900 (graduate or postdoc). Books and supplies allowance. One-time establishment allowance.
requirements: Citizen of an ASEAN member state (Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam). Enrolled at a recognised post-secondary institution in an ASEAN country. College exchanges: enrolled in a college or technical institute. Undergraduate exchanges: completed at least one year of study. Graduate exchanges: enrolled in a master's or PhD programme.
required_documents: Nomination by a Canadian institution. Academic transcripts. Letter of enrollment from your home institution. Study or research plan. Curriculum vitae. Passport copy. English or French language proficiency proof. Letter of support from your home institution.

title: Bologna University Study Grants (ER.GO)
university: ER.GO (Regional Authority for the Right to Higher Education, Emilia-Romagna)
description: The ER.GO study grants support students at the University of Bologna and other universities in Italy’s Emilia-Romagna region.…
details:
The ER.GO study grants support students at the University of Bologna and other universities in Italy’s Emilia-Romagna region. ER.GO is the regional authority for the right to higher education, and its grants are need-based awards designed to ensure that talented students from lower-income backgrounds, including international students, can study without financial barriers.

The support is comprehensive for those who qualify. It includes a full tuition fee waiver, an annual cash grant of around 6,500 to 7,000 euros, free meals in the university canteens, free or heavily subsidised university housing, and access to libraries, labs, and cultural facilities. The grant runs for an academic year and is renewable on meeting credit requirements.

Eligibility is based on enrolment and means: applicants must be enrolled or enrolling in a degree programme at a participating university such as Bologna, meet the income and asset thresholds set by ER.GO (based on the ISEE and related indicators), and maintain minimum credit requirements each year. Both EU and non-EU international students can apply. You apply online through the ER.GO portal by the deadline, providing income and merit documentation. For students with financial need, it is one of the most generous regional support schemes in Italy.
benefits: Full tuition fee waiver. Annual cash grant of approximately EUR 6,500 to 7,000. Free university canteen meals (lunch and dinner). Free or heavily subsidised university housing. Access to libraries, labs, and cultural facilities.
requirements: Enrolled or enrolling in a degree programme at a participating university such as the University of Bologna. Meet the income and asset thresholds set by ER.GO (based on the ISEE and related indicators). Maintain minimum credit requirements each year (varies by degree level). Open to both EU and non-EU international students.
required_documents: University of Bologna enrollment confirmation. ER.GO online application. ISEE document (income and asset declaration). Academic transcripts. Identity document or passport. Tax documentation from your home country. Residence permit (for non-EU students).

title: Bezout Labex Master’s Scholarships (France)
