details:
The Bezout Labex master’s scholarships are offered by the Bezout Laboratory of Excellence, a research cluster linked to Universite Gustave Eiffel and partner institutions in the Paris area, specialising in mathematics and computer science. The scholarships support talented international and French students to undertake a research-oriented second year of master’s study (M2), with a view to continuing into a PhD.

The award provides a monthly stipend of around 1,300 euros for 11 months, together with access to research labs and libraries, mentorship from leading researchers, and priority consideration for Bezout PhD funding on completion. It is aimed at students with a strong aptitude for research in the mathematical sciences.

Eligibility is open to international students of all nationalities who hold, or are completing, a bachelor’s degree in mathematics, computer science, or a closely related field, with a strong academic record and a good command of English; prior research experience is an advantage. You apply to the relevant master’s track in mathematics or computer science at the partner university, register through the programme pages, and selected students receive the Bezout scholarship. For aspiring researchers in mathematics and computing, it is an excellent springboard toward doctoral study in France.
benefits: Monthly stipend of approximately EUR 1,300 for 11 months. Access to research labs and libraries. Mentorship from leading researchers in mathematics and computer science. Priority consideration for Bezout PhD funding upon completion. Networking with the French mathematical sciences community.
requirements: Open to international students of all nationalities. Hold or be completing a bachelor's degree in mathematics, computer science, or a closely related field. Strong academic record with a demonstrated aptitude for research. Good command of English (courses are taught in English and French). Prior research experience or internships are advantageous.
required_documents: Completed Bezout application form. Academic transcripts and degree certificates. Curriculum vitae. Letter of motivation describing research interests. Two academic recommendation letters. English language proficiency proof.

title: Belgium Master Mind Scholarship
university: Flemish Ministry of Education and Training (Government of Flanders)

details:
The Master Mind Scholarship is awarded by the Government of Flanders, through the Flemish Ministry of Education and Training, to attract outstanding international students to master’s programmes at universities and university colleges in Flanders, the Dutch-speaking region of Belgium. It is a competitive, prestigious award intended to promote Flanders as a top study destination.

The scholarship covers a full tuition fee waiver together with a living allowance of around 10,560 euros a year and health insurance, for a master’s programme lasting one to two years depending on its credit load. Recipients study at one of the participating Flemish host institutions, which are well regarded across Europe.

Eligibility is open to non-Belgian and non-EEA citizens who have been admitted to a master’s programme at a Flemish university and who have a strong academic record. A key point about the process is that students cannot apply directly: you apply for admission to a participating host institution and express interest in the scholarship, after which the institution preselects candidates and submits applications on their behalf through the Mobility-Online system, by the host institution’s deadline. For high-achieving international students, Master Mind is a flagship route to funded master’s study in Belgium.
benefits: Full tuition fee waiver. Living allowance of around EUR 10,560 per year. Health insurance.
requirements: Non-Belgian and non-EEA citizen. Admitted to a master's programme at a Flemish university. Strong academic record.
required_documents: Admission application to a participating Flemish host institution. Academic transcripts and degree certificates. Motivation letter. Letters of recommendation. Proof of English proficiency. Passport copy.

title: Asian University for Women (AUW) Full Scholarship
description: The Asian University for Women (AUW) in Chittagong, Bangladesh, is an independent, international institution dedicated entirely to educating…
details:
The Asian University for Women (AUW) in Chittagong, Bangladesh, is an independent, international institution dedicated entirely to educating women from across Asia and the Middle East. Many of its students are the first women in their families to attend university, and a large share study on full scholarships. AUW’s mission is to develop a new generation of women leaders, and its funding is designed so that financial circumstances are never a barrier to admission.

The full scholarship is genuinely comprehensive. It covers tuition and fees, room and board on campus, books and academic materials, a laptop loan, international travel to and from the university, health services, and career and graduate-school support. The undergraduate programme runs for three years and is taught in English, within a residential community drawn from many countries.

The opportunity is open to women from an Asian or Middle Eastern country who have completed secondary education and can demonstrate academic ability and leadership potential. AUW uses holistic admissions, so there is no minimum standardised test score, and financial need is considered but does not affect the admission decision. You apply online for admission and submit the financial aid application alongside it. For talented young women seeking a transformative, fully funded undergraduate education, AUW is a remarkable opportunity.
benefits: Full tuition and fees. Room and board on campus. Books and academic materials. Laptop loan programme. International travel to and from AUW. Health services. Career counselling and graduate-school preparation.
requirements: A woman from an Asian or Middle Eastern country. Completed secondary education (12th grade or equivalent). Demonstrated academic ability and leadership potential. Proficient in English (no minimum test score; AUW uses holistic admissions). Financial need is considered but is not a barrier to admission.
required_documents: AUW online application form. Secondary school transcripts and certificates. Two essays (a personal statement and an intellectual-curiosity essay). Two recommendation letters. English proficiency evidence (a formal test is not required). Copy of national ID or passport.
summary: The Asian University for Women (AUW) in Chittagong, Bangladesh, is an independent, international institution dedicated entirely to educating…

title: UCD Global Excellence Scholarships
description: University College Dublin (UCD), one of Ireland’s leading universities, offers Global Excellence Scholarships to support outstanding non-EU international…
details:
University College Dublin (UCD), one of Ireland’s leading universities, offers Global Excellence Scholarships to support outstanding non-EU international students on eligible undergraduate and taught graduate programmes. The awards provide substantial tuition reductions, with a dedicated earlier deadline for the Pakistan region, recognising academic excellence and supporting strong international students choosing UCD.

The award is a 50 or 100 percent tuition fee scholarship for a limited number of outstanding international students, applied across the duration of the programme subject to continuous enrolment. A separate International Student Scholarship is assessed automatically at the point of offer. Scholars study in Dublin, a major European hub for global employers, with recognition as a Global Excellence Scholar.

Eligibility is for students classified as non-EU for tuition fee purposes and self-funding, who hold an offer or conditional offer for an eligible UCD programme, with a strong academic record and a holistic scholarship application; Smurfit Business School, clinical, online, part-time, January-start, off-shore, and foundation pathway programmes are excluded, and the award cannot be combined with other UCD tuition scholarships. You apply for an eligible UCD programme and obtain an offer, then submit the separate Global Excellence Scholarship application via SISWeb by your regional deadline (earlier for Pakistan). For non-EU students aiming at Ireland, it is a significant tuition award.
benefits: 50 or 100 percent of tuition fees covered. Dedicated earlier deadline for the Pakistan region. Study in Dublin, a major European hub for global employers. Recognition as a Global Excellence Scholar.
requirements: Classified as non-EU for tuition fee purposes and self-funding. Hold an offer or conditional offer for an eligible UCD programme. Strong academic record and a holistic scholarship application. Excludes Smurfit Business School, clinical, online, part-time, January-start, off-shore, and foundation pathway programmes. Cannot be combined with other UCD tuition scholarships.
required_documents: An offer or conditional offer for an eligible UCD programme. The Global Excellence Scholarship application via SISWeb. Academic transcripts and qualifications. Proof of English language proficiency.
summary: University College Dublin (UCD), one of Ireland’s leading universities, offers Global Excellence Scholarships to support outstanding non-EU international…

title: Bocconi Graduate Merit Award
description: Bocconi University in Milan is one of Europe’s most respected institutions for economics, management, and finance, and its…
details:
Bocconi University in Milan is one of Europe’s most respected institutions for economics, management, and finance, and its Graduate Merit Award is the flagship merit scholarship for international master’s students. It is designed to attract the very best applicants to Bocconi’s Master of Science programmes, regardless of financial background, and is assessed automatically from the admission application.

The award is generous: a full waiver of tuition and fees, worth roughly 13,000 to 14,000 euros a year, for the legal duration of the master’s, and renewable into the second year on meeting credit requirements. A limited number of recipients also receive free accommodation in a Bocconi residence in central Milan. A separate Bocconi International Award offers a 50 percent tuition reduction for those not selected for the full award.

Eligibility is open to applicants of all nationalities admitted to the first year of a Bocconi Master of Science programme who rank among the top applicants by academic standing. There is no separate scholarship form; your admission dossier is the basis for assessment, so applying in the earliest admission rounds gives the best chance. If selected, the award is communicated with the admission offer, and you accept it and complete enrolment by the stated deadline. For top students aiming at a leading European business school, it is a flagship route to funded study.
benefits: Full waiver of tuition and fees. Possible free accommodation in a central Milan residence. Renewable for the second year on earning the required credits. Study at a leading European business and economics university.
requirements: Admitted to the first year of a Bocconi Master of Science programme. Among the top applicants by academic standing (international, Italian, or Bocconi). Open to all nationalities. Assessed automatically from the admission application; MBA, Specialised Master's, and PhD have separate funding.
required_documents: The Bocconi MSc admission application with transcripts, test scores, essays, and references. An updated CV at the acceptance stage. No separate scholarship application form. Online scholarship acceptance within the enrolment deadline.

title: Ewha Womans University Scholarships (EGPP and ISS)
description: Ewha Womans University in Seoul is one of the world’s largest and most prestigious women’s universities, and it…
details:
Ewha Womans University in Seoul is one of the world’s largest and most prestigious women’s universities, and it offers scholarships to attract talented international women to its undergraduate and graduate programmes. The two main schemes are the Ewha Global Partnership Program (EGPP), a full-ride award for women from developing countries, and the International Students Scholarship (ISS), which offers tuition support on a tiered basis.

EGPP is comprehensive, covering full tuition and the admission fee, dormitory housing, a monthly stipend, and in some cases round-trip airfare, for up to eight semesters for undergraduates, four for master’s, and six for PhD students. The ISS provides full or partial tuition tiers, including full tuition and admission fee for one semester for holders of TOPIK Level 6, and a KOICA-Sun award covers half of tuition.

The scholarships are for female applicants only, with EGPP targeting promising women from developing countries; awards are merit-based and assessed from the admission application, and both English and Korean tracks are available, with TOPIK not required for English-taught programmes. You apply through Ewha international admissions, indicate your interest in the relevant scholarship where required, and await the admission and scholarship decision. For talented women seeking a funded education in Korea, Ewha is a leading choice.
benefits: EGPP is a full ride: tuition, admission fee, housing, stipend, and sometimes airfare. ISS provides full or partial tuition tiers. Study at a leading women's university in Seoul. Support for international women from developing countries.
requirements: Female applicants only. EGPP targets promising women from developing countries. Admitted to an Ewha programme; awards are merit-based on the admission application. English and Korean tracks; TOPIK is not required for English-taught programmes.
required_documents: Online application via Ewha international admissions. Academic transcripts and certificates. Study plan and references as required. Application fee of KRW 150,000.

title: Lancaster University Postgraduate International Scholarships
description: Lancaster University, a leading UK research university, offers postgraduate international scholarships to help overseas students fund a taught…
details:
Lancaster University, a leading UK research university, offers postgraduate international scholarships to help overseas students fund a taught master’s degree. The awards are tuition-fee discounts, with a dedicated regional scholarship for students from a set of underrepresented countries and faculty-based excellence awards for applicants from elsewhere.

The headline award is the Postgraduate International Regional Scholarship of 10,000 pounds for citizens of 14 underrepresented countries (including Pakistan). For other countries, faculty-based Master’s Excellence Scholarships apply: up to 9,000 pounds in Science and Technology, up to 20 percent of tuition in Management, 20 percent in Arts and Social Sciences, and 25 percent in Health, with Lancaster alumni receiving a further 10 percent. These are one-time awards applied to the year of study.

Eligibility is for overseas (international) fee payers holding an offer for an eligible full-time on-campus taught master’s; the Regional Scholarship requires citizenship of one of the 14 listed countries with a first-class or 2:1 background, while the faculty-based Excellence Scholarship applies to applicants from other countries. The awards are automatic: you apply for an eligible master’s, hold or accept your offer, and the relevant tuition award is applied automatically, with no separate scholarship application. For international master’s applicants, including those from Pakistan, it is a straightforward tuition reduction.
benefits: GBP 10,000 for eligible regional applicants, including Pakistan. Faculty-based awards for other countries by subject area. An additional 10 percent for Lancaster alumni. Automatic; no separate scholarship application needed.
requirements: Classified as an overseas (international) fee payer. For the Regional Scholarship, be a citizen of one of the 14 listed underrepresented countries (including Pakistan) with a first-class or 2:1 background. Hold an offer for an eligible full-time on-campus taught master's. Faculty-based Excellence Scholarship applies to applicants from other countries.

title: University of York International Masters Scholarships
description: The University of York, a Russell Group research university, offers International Masters Scholarships to support overseas students undertaking…
details:
The University of York, a Russell Group research university, offers International Masters Scholarships to support overseas students undertaking a taught master’s. The awards combine a broadly available achievement scholarship with a country-targeted award, easing the cost of a master’s at a leading UK university.

The award is a tuition reduction applied to the year of study. The International Masters Achievement Scholarship is worth up to 10,000 pounds (open to all international students), and the York Global Impact Masters Scholarship is worth 5,000 to 8,000 pounds for applicants from a defined list of countries that includes Pakistan; a GREAT Scholarship is available for some other countries. Awards can combine up to the full value of tuition.

Eligibility is for students classified as an international (overseas) fee payer holding an offer for an eligible full-time taught master’s by the stated date; the Global Impact Scholarship targets a defined list of countries, including Pakistan. You are automatically considered, with no separate scholarship application: you apply for an eligible taught master’s at York, hold your offer by the relevant date, are assessed automatically for the international scholarships, and await notification. For international master’s students aiming at the UK, it is a worthwhile, automatic award.
benefits: Up to GBP 10,000 tuition reduction on the Achievement Scholarship. GBP 5,000 to 8,000 on the Global Impact Scholarship. Awards can combine up to the full value of tuition. Study at a Russell Group university in the historic city of York.
requirements: Classified as an international (overseas) fee payer. Hold an offer for an eligible full-time taught master's by the stated date. The Global Impact Scholarship targets a defined list of countries, including Pakistan. Automatically considered; no separate scholarship application is required.

title: Queen Mary University of London International Postgraduate Scholarships
description: Queen Mary University of London (QMUL), a Russell Group university in east London, offers a range of scholarships…
details:
Queen Mary University of London (QMUL), a Russell Group university in east London, offers a range of scholarships to international students undertaking a taught master’s degree. The awards are tuition reductions across three tiers, designed to recognise academic achievement and to support strong international students choosing QMUL.

The three tiers for international taught master’s students are the Global Talent Scholarship of 5,000 pounds, the Global Excellence Scholarship of 7,000 pounds, and the President’s Global Scholarship of 10,000 pounds (up to 20 awards, with a South Asia emphasis). Each is a one-time award applied to the year of study, alongside the experience of studying at a Russell Group university in central east London.

Eligibility is for students classified as overseas (international) fee payers who hold an offer for an eligible full-time taught master’s, with at least a 2:1 for the Global Talent award and higher achievement for the Global Excellence and President’s Global awards, and which are not held together with other QMUL scholarships. You apply to an eligible QMUL master’s and obtain an offer, then complete the scholarship form sent to you after your offer and submit it before the relevant deadline (earlier for the President’s Global award). For international master’s students aiming at London, these awards meaningfully reduce tuition.
benefits: Tuition reduction of GBP 5,000, GBP 7,000, or GBP 10,000. Recognition of academic achievement. Study in central east London at a Russell Group university. The President's Global award gives priority emphasis to South Asia.
requirements: Classified as an overseas (international) fee payer. Hold an offer for an eligible full-time taught master's. At least a 2:1 for the Global Talent award, with higher achievement for Global Excellence and a UK first-class (or equivalent) profile for the President's Global award. Not held together with other QMUL scholarships.

title: King’s College London International Scholarships
description: King’s College London (KCL) is a leading research university in central London, and it offers a portfolio of…
details:
King’s College London (KCL) is a leading research university in central London, and it offers a portfolio of international scholarships to help talented overseas students fund master’s and doctoral study. These range from partial, competitive King’s-administered awards to fully funded external routes hosted at King’s, so the right option depends on the programme and the applicant’s circumstances.

King’s-administered master’s awards are mostly partial, including King’s Scholars of Tomorrow (around 5,000 pounds), faculty awards up to around 11,760 pounds, King’s Business School awards, and the CMA CGM Excellence Fund (full tuition plus a stipend for overseas fee payers). Fully funded routes hosted at King’s include the Commonwealth Shared Scholarships (full tuition, a monthly stipend of around 1,781 pounds, and airfare), King’s-CSC PhD awards, and Chevening.

Eligibility is generally for overseas fee payers with a strong academic record (first-class or high upper-second honours) who hold or are seeking an offer for an eligible King’s master’s or PhD; specific awards have their own rules, and the Commonwealth Shared Scholarships require citizenship of an eligible low or middle income Commonwealth country and inability to afford study otherwise. You apply for admission via King’s Apply by the scholarship’s internal deadline, complete any separate scholarship form, and for Commonwealth Shared, King’s nominates selected candidates to the Commission. For international students aiming at a top London university, King’s offers a range of funding.
benefits: Partial King's awards from around GBP 5,000 up to about GBP 11,760. CMA CGM Excellence Fund offering full tuition plus a stipend. Fully funded external routes hosted at King's (Commonwealth Shared, King's-CSC, Chevening). Study at a leading London research university.
requirements: Generally overseas fee payers with a strong academic record (first-class or high upper-second-class honours). Hold or be seeking an offer for an eligible King's master's or PhD. Specific awards have their own rules; Commonwealth Shared requires citizenship of an eligible low or middle income Commonwealth country and inability to afford study otherwise. Some funds are for overseas fee status only; home-fee students may be ineligible.
required_documents: An admission application via King's Apply for an eligible programme. A separate scholarship form for some awards (for example CMA CGM). Academic transcripts and references. For Commonwealth Shared, an admission application followed by King's nomination to the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission.

title: University of Otago Scholarships
description: The University of Otago, New Zealand’s oldest university, offers a range of scholarships to international students across undergraduate,…
details:
The University of Otago, New Zealand’s oldest university, offers a range of scholarships to international students across undergraduate, coursework master’s, research master’s, and doctoral study. They range from automatic entrance and global awards to stipend-bearing research scholarships, supporting international students at every level.

Support varies by award. The Global and Vice-Chancellor’s Scholarships for International Students (undergraduate and coursework master’s) provide 10,000 to 15,000 New Zealand dollars toward tuition, assessed automatically. The International Master’s Research Scholarship provides an 18,204-dollar annual stipend plus a thesis tuition waiver, and the Doctoral Scholarship provides a 33,624-dollar annual stipend plus a domestic-rate tuition waiver for 36 months (international PhD students are charged domestic tuition rates).

Eligibility is for international fee-paying students; some entrance awards require not having previously studied at a New Zealand university, and the research master’s scholarship is competitive (generally needing grades at A or A+ level), with selection based predominantly on academic merit and research potential. You apply for admission via the eVision portal, where entrance and global scholarships are assessed automatically, and apply via eVision for research awards when invited. For international students aiming at New Zealand, Otago offers strong, layered scholarship support.
benefits: Automatic entrance and global scholarships for undergraduates and coursework master's students. Stipend plus thesis tuition waiver for research master's students. Generous doctoral stipend with a tuition waiver for 36 months. Study at New Zealand's oldest university.
requirements: International fee-paying students; some entrance awards require not having previously studied at a New Zealand university. The research master's scholarship is competitive and generally needs grades at A or A+ level. Selection is based predominantly on academic merit and research potential. International PhD students at Otago are charged domestic tuition rates.
required_documents: Admission application via the eVision portal. A scholarship application via eVision after admission for research awards. Academic transcripts. Research details and grades for the research master's and doctoral awards.

title: Beijing Government Scholarship (BGS)
university: Beijing Municipal Government (via participating Beijing universities)
description: The Beijing Government Scholarship (BGS) is funded by the Beijing Municipal Government and delivered through participating universities in…
details:
The Beijing Government Scholarship (BGS) is funded by the Beijing Municipal Government and delivered through participating universities in China’s capital. It is designed to attract international students to Beijing for undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral study, and it is awarded in tiers, so the level of support varies from a tuition waiver alone up to a comprehensive, fully funded package.

The award has three categories. Category A is the most generous, covering a tuition waiver, accommodation, a living stipend, and comprehensive medical insurance. Category B covers tuition, accommodation, and insurance, while Category C covers tuition and insurance. Some universities present the award as tiered tuition coverage, so applicants should confirm the precise benefits with the host institution.

title: AIMS Scholarship (African Institute for Mathematical Sciences)
description: The African Institute for Mathematical Sciences (AIMS) offers a fully funded, pan-African master’s scholarship designed to develop the…
details:
The African Institute for Mathematical Sciences (AIMS) offers a fully funded, pan-African master’s scholarship designed to develop the continent’s next generation of scientists, problem-solvers, and leaders. Founded in 2003 and now a network of centres across Africa, AIMS delivers an intensive, residential Master’s in Mathematical Sciences that brings together top graduates from many African countries into a single, immersive learning community.

The flagship programme is a structured master’s of around ten months that builds strong foundations in the mathematical sciences alongside computing, scientific writing, and problem-solving skills. AIMS also runs specialised tracks, including the African Master’s in Machine Intelligence (AMMI), a Mathematical Epidemiology track developed with the University of Toronto, and a data science master’s developed with Google DeepMind, some of which run for around sixteen months. Teaching draws on lecturers from leading universities worldwide, and the cohort deliberately includes a high proportion of women.

The scholarship is genuinely comprehensive. It covers full tuition with no registration fees, accommodation, meals, travel, medical insurance, and a living stipend, along with around-the-clock access to computing facilities, so that students can focus entirely on their studies. The experience is structured to open doors into PhD study and research careers across academia, industry, and the public sector.

The opportunity is open to citizens and residents of African countries who hold, or expect to complete, a strong university degree in mathematics, science, or engineering with a solid mathematics component. Selection looks for mathematical ability, leadership, and a commitment to contributing to Africa’s development, and women are strongly encouraged to apply. With its blend of rigorous training, full funding, and a vibrant Pan-African community, AIMS is one of the most valuable routes into the mathematical sciences on the continent.

required_documents: Online application via the AIMS portal. Academic transcripts and a current CV. A motivation letter of around 500 words and referee contacts. Answers to written mathematics questions and a coding problem on the application site.

IE University, based in Madrid and Segovia, Spain, is a leading private institution known for business, technology, law, and the social sciences. The PhD in Management is fully funded, including tuition and living expenses.

The University of the Witwatersrand (Wits), a top South African research university, offers the Postgraduate Merit Award and a range of undergraduate scholarships to support students at every level. The merit award is applied to tuition and recognises strong academic performance, with international students signposted to major international schemes.

The award is partial funding: the University Postgraduate Merit Award provides up to about 53,800 rand toward tuition for honours, master’s, or doctoral study (by research, or by coursework and research). Undergraduate routes include a University Council Merit Scholarship (25 percent tuition for returning students averaging 75 percent or more), entrance scholarships of up to 100 percent of first-year tuition by admission points, and a Vice-Chancellor’s Scholarship for the top 20 first-time entrants (full tuition, capped accommodation, and allowances).

Hanyang University in Seoul is one of South Korea’s leading private universities, especially strong in engineering and science, and it offers a range of scholarships to attract international students. Rather than a single award, Hanyang provides tiered tuition reductions for undergraduate and graduate students, with awards tied to the admission evaluation, language ability, and academic progress.

The scholarships take the form of tuition reductions of 30 to 100 percent. Examples include the Hanyang International Scholarship for undergraduates (full, 70, or 50 percent), engineering and science graduate awards (half tuition plus part of the admission fee), TOPIK excellence awards (full tuition for level 6, half for level 5), and English proficiency and graduate-school awards. They are retained by maintaining a set GPA each semester.

The scholarships are for international students admitted to Hanyang, with awards tied to the admission evaluation, TOPIK level, English proficiency, or academic progress; English-track applicants do not need a Korean certificate, and the awards cannot be combined with GKS or other external scholarships. You apply for admission as an international student, and most scholarships are assessed automatically from your admission evaluation and language scores, with any additional documents required for specific awards. For international students aiming to study in Korea, Hanyang’s scholarships make a strong university more affordable.

The award is a tuition reduction applied to the first year. The Postgraduate High Fliers Scholarship is an automatic 5,000-pound tuition fee discount for international students domiciled in selected countries (Pakistan has been included; confirm the current list), while a separate competitive scholarship offers 10,000 pounds toward first-year tuition. Eligibility is for students classified as overseas fee payers for a taught master’s at the Birmingham UK campus starting in September, not already enrolled on a master’s programme; the High Fliers route requires being domiciled in one of the selected countries, and Dubai campus, partner-delivered, and online courses are excluded. You apply for an eligible master’s, accept your offer and pay the deposit by the deadline, and the 5,000-pound discount is applied automatically for eligible-country students; you apply separately for the competitive 10,000-pound award if required. For international master’s students from eligible countries, it is a worthwhile, partly automatic tuition award.

title: American University of Sharjah (AUS) Scholarships

details:
The American University of Sharjah (AUS), founded in 1997, is one of the United Arab Emirates’ most respected universities, known for its American-style education, striking campus, and a student body representing around 90 nationalities. To attract top international talent, AUS offers a range of merit scholarships, the most prestigious of which is the President’s Scholarship for students who have completed their secondary education outside the UAE.

The President’s Scholarship is a comprehensive, fully funded award given to up to 20 outstanding first-year students each year who enrol in the fall semester. It covers full tuition and lab fees, an application fee waiver, on-campus housing, student medical insurance, a monthly living stipend, and three round-trip flights home per year, and it can be used for any bachelor’s degree at AUS. The award is renewable for students who maintain the required academic standing.

Selection is highly competitive and weighs academic performance in grades 10 and 11 along with predicted final grades. Indicative benchmarks include three A-levels at grade A with five A-grade GCSEs, an IB Diploma of around 40 points, or a US-curriculum average near 98 percent with strong AP or SAT results, together with an IELTS of 7.0 or TOEFL iBT of 94. Applicants also submit a short video and letters of recommendation. AUS additionally offers the Chancellor’s Scholarship, automatic Merit Scholarships, and other awards for different groups of students.

Applying is linked to admission: you first apply to AUS, then complete the President’s Scholarship application before the deadline, which in recent years has fallen in mid-April for the fall intake. For ambitious international students seeking a fully funded undergraduate education in a dynamic, globally connected setting, the AUS President’s Scholarship is an outstanding option.

Graduate assistantships are available separately for master's and PhD students.

description: Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU) is a top South Korean university with strong industry links, notably to Samsung. It offers…
details:
Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU) is a top South Korean university with strong industry links, notably to Samsung. It offers a range of scholarships to international undergraduate and graduate students, mostly assessed automatically at admission, that reduce or eliminate tuition and, for some awards, add a stipend and settlement support.

Support varies by award. Admission scholarships give first-semester tuition reductions of 10 to 100 percent based on the admission evaluation, with continuing scholarships of roughly 10 to 100 percent based on GPA. STEM graduate awards start at a 50 percent first-semester waiver and can reach full tuition, and some professor-sponsored positions add a monthly stipend; the Samsung Scholarship can cover full tuition for up to eight semesters. Awards run for the standard programme duration, reviewed by GPA each semester.

Eligibility is for international students (foreign nationals whose parents also hold foreign citizenship) admitted to an SKKU programme, with a strong academic record; English-taught tracks do not require TOPIK, and STEM awards apply to natural sciences, engineering, and medicine graduate programmes. You apply through the SKKU global admissions portal, and most scholarships are assessed automatically at admission based on your evaluation; for STEM or professor-sponsored funding you align with a department or lab. For international students aiming at Korea, SKKU offers a strong, scholarship-rich environment.
benefits: Tuition reductions from 10 up to 100 percent depending on the award. Renewable continuing scholarships based on GPA. Some fully funded positions add a monthly stipend and settlement support. Strong research environment with Samsung industry links.
requirements: International students (foreign nationals whose parents also hold foreign citizenship). Admitted to an SKKU programme. Strong academic record; English-taught tracks do not require TOPIK. STEM awards apply to natural sciences, engineering, and medicine graduate programmes.
required_documents: Online application via the SKKU global admissions portal. Academic transcripts and certificates (scanned, originals later if accepted). Study plan or research proposal. Language proficiency evidence and references as required.
summary: Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU) is a top South Korean university with strong industry links, notably to Samsung. It offers…

title: University of Hong Kong (HKU) Entrance Scholarships
description: The University of Hong Kong (HKU), a world-leading and highly international university, offers entrance scholarships to attract talented…
details:
The University of Hong Kong (HKU), a world-leading and highly international university, offers entrance scholarships to attract talented non-local (international) students. These awards, made on academic merit and, for some schemes, leadership or background, range from partial support to full funding, helping international students study in English at a top Asian university.

Support varies by scheme. The top entrance scholarships cover full tuition plus accommodation and a general living allowance, while many other named awards across faculties are partial; the Belt and Road Scholarship supports students from Belt and Road countries for the duration of their studies. Awards generally run for the standard duration of the degree, subject to renewal conditions.

Eligibility is for non-local (international) students admitted to an HKU programme, with awards based on academic merit and, for some schemes, leadership or regional background; some entrance scholarships consider all admitted non-local applicants automatically, while specific schemes (for example Belt and Road) target particular regions. You apply for undergraduate admission to HKU as an international applicant, are considered for entrance scholarships (some automatically), and complete any separate scholarship application required for specific schemes. For international students aiming at Hong Kong, HKU’s entrance scholarships offer a strong, sometimes fully funded route.
benefits: Top awards cover full tuition plus accommodation and a living allowance. Study at a world-leading, highly international university in English. A range of named scholarships across faculties. Renewable for the duration of study where conditions are met.
requirements: Non-local (international) student admitted to an HKU programme. Awarded on academic merit and, for some schemes, leadership or background. Some entrance scholarships consider all admitted non-local applicants automatically. Specific schemes (for example Belt and Road) target students from particular regions.
required_documents: HKU admission application. Academic transcripts and qualifications. Personal statement and references where required. A separate scholarship form for certain schemes.
summary: The University of Hong Kong (HKU), a world-leading and highly international university, offers entrance scholarships to attract talented…

title: University of Sussex Chancellor’s International Scholarship
description: The Chancellor’s International Scholarship is offered by the University of Sussex to support talented overseas students undertaking a…
details:
The Chancellor’s International Scholarship is offered by the University of Sussex to support talented overseas students undertaking a taught master’s. It is a tuition fee discount that recognises academic excellence, with the strongest applicants from certain countries able to combine it with a Country Scholarship for a larger award.

The award is a 5,000-pound tuition fee discount; the strongest applicants from a defined list of countries (including Pakistan, Bangladesh, Egypt, India, Kenya, Nepal, Nigeria, Sri Lanka, Turkey, and Vietnam) may be selected to combine it with a Country Scholarship up to a total of 10,000 pounds. It is a one-time award applied as a fee discount (there is no cash equivalent).

Eligibility is for students classified as overseas for fee purposes and self-financing who have received and accepted an offer for an eligible full-time master’s starting in September, with exceptional academic grades (around UK first-class or equivalent), not already holding another Sussex scholarship; some courses (for example Brighton and Sussex Medical School and online courses) are excluded. You apply for an eligible master’s and accept your offer, complete the separate online scholarship application form, and submit a self-written personal statement (AI-written statements are usually unsuccessful), awaiting a decision by the end of July. For overseas master’s students aiming at the UK, it is a useful tuition award.
benefits: GBP 5,000 tuition fee discount (potentially up to GBP 10,000 for eligible-country applicants). Recognition as a top international student at Sussex. A stronger academic and professional profile. No cash equivalent; applied as a fee discount.
requirements: Classified as overseas for fee purposes and self-financing. Have received and accepted an offer for an eligible full-time master's starting September. Exceptional academic grades (around UK first-class or equivalent). Not already holding another Sussex scholarship. Some courses (for example Brighton and Sussex Medical School and online courses) are excluded.
required_documents: Your Sussex offer for an eligible master's. A self-written personal statement on your achievements, goals, and suitability. Academic transcripts and degree certificates. Proof of English language proficiency for admission.
summary: The Chancellor’s International Scholarship is offered by the University of Sussex to support talented overseas students undertaking a…

title: University of Leeds International Excellence Scholarship
description: The University of Leeds International Excellence Scholarship recognises and rewards high-achieving international students joining a taught master’s degree…
details:
The University of Leeds International Excellence Scholarship recognises and rewards high-achieving international students joining a taught master’s degree at one of the UK’s leading universities. It is a competitive, merit-based award offered as a discount on the first year’s tuition fee, helping talented students from around the world study in a research-intensive, highly international environment.

The University of Leeds, founded in 1904, is a member of the Russell Group of leading UK research universities and welcomes students from over 140 countries to its large campus in the heart of the city of Leeds in northern England. It offers a broad range of master’s programmes across business, engineering, sciences, arts, and the humanities, along with a strong reputation for employability and a vibrant, multicultural student community.

The scholarship is awarded at one of three values, GBP 3,000, GBP 6,000, or GBP 16,000, applied as a reduction on tuition fees for the first year of study. The university offers up to 500 of these awards, making it one of the more widely available international scholarships at this level, although competition for the higher-value awards is strong. The discount applies to tuition only and cannot be used for accommodation or living costs.

To be considered, you must be classified as an international student for fee purposes, hold a conditional or unconditional offer for an eligible taught master’s starting in September, and be self-funded or partially funded, since fully sponsored students are not eligible. The university looks for an excellent academic record, normally at least a UK 2:1 honours degree or its equivalent, together with strong professional and personal achievements. MBA and fully online courses are not eligible.

Applications open to offer holders and run in rounds, so applying early is wise. You apply online after receiving your course offer, submitting a separate application for each offer you hold, including a short statement on why you want to study at Leeds. The scholarship can also be combined with some other Leeds awards, up to a maximum of full tuition.
benefits: Tuition fee reduction of GBP 3,000, GBP 6,000, or GBP 16,000. Applied to the first year of study, with up to 500 awards available. Recognition of academic and personal achievement at a Russell Group university. Can be combined with some other Leeds awards up to a maximum of 100% of tuition. Join a large, diverse international community drawn from over 140 countries. Note: the award is a tuition discount only and cannot be used towards maintenance or accommodation costs.
requirements: Classified as an international student for tuition fee purposes (not open to UK fee-status students). Hold a conditional or unconditional offer for an eligible taught master's course (including MRes) starting in September. Self-funded or partially funded; fully sponsored students are not eligible. Excellent academic record, normally predicted or achieved at least a UK 2:1 honours degree or international equivalent. Strong professional and personal skills, evidenced through work experience and/or extracurricular activities. MBA programmes and fully online courses are not eligible (the MBA has its own separate scheme). If you hold offers for more than one course, a separate scholarship application is required for each.
required_documents: A conditional or unconditional offer for an eligible Leeds taught master's. Completed online scholarship application form (a separate form for each course offer you hold). A short statement (around 100 words) on why you want to study at Leeds and why you should be considered. Evidence of professional and personal achievements, such as work experience or extracurricular involvement, where relevant.
summary: The University of Leeds International Excellence Scholarship recognises and rewards high-achieving international students joining a taught master’s degree…

title: Calouste Gulbenkian Research Scholarships on Portuguese Culture for Foreigners
university: Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation (Fundacao Calouste Gulbenkian), Lisbon
description: The Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation in Lisbon is one of Portugal’s most prestigious philanthropic institutions, and this scholarship supports…
details: The Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation in Lisbon is one of Portugal’s most prestigious philanthropic institutions, and this scholarship supports non-Portuguese doctoral students and senior researchers who want to carry out a research stay in Portugal. The focus is specific: research in the humanities on topics of Portuguese culture in history, art history and literature, with the aim of producing a publication or part of a thesis. It is a short-term research grant rather than a full degree scholarship, providing a monthly allowance, a travel and installation payment and insurance for stays of a few months.
benefits: Monthly allowance of EUR 1,250 (doctoral) or EUR 2,000 (senior researcher). One-off EUR 1,000 for travel and installation. Personal accident insurance during travel. Access to Portuguese archives, libraries and research institutions.
requirements: Non-Portuguese doctoral students or senior researchers who reside abroad. Wish to conduct research in Portugal on Portuguese culture in history, art history or literature. Research must aim at a scientific article, a publication, or part of an academic thesis. May not combine the grant with another scholarship in Portugal.
required_documents: Online application via the MyGulbenkian platform. Academic certificates and curriculum vitae. A structured work plan for the research. Proof of institutional access or project approval, and a supervisor's approval letter for doctoral candidates. A motivation letter outlining goals and the importance of the scholarship.
summary: The Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation in Lisbon is one of Portugal’s most prestigious philanthropic institutions, and this scholarship supports…

title: University of Luxembourg PhD Grant (Luxembourg National Research Fund, AFR)
university: University of Luxembourg with the Luxembourg National Research Fund (FNR)
description: In Luxembourg, doctoral study is funded as a salaried research position rather than a traditional scholarship. The main…
details: In Luxembourg, doctoral study is funded as a salaried research position rather than a traditional scholarship. The main route is the Luxembourg National Research Fund (FNR) AFR PhD grant, whose ‘AFR Incoming’ strand is open to candidates of any nationality who secure a doctoral position at a Luxembourg host institution such as the University of Luxembourg. Beneficiaries are employed on a contract with a competitive salary plus a training and mobility budget. For master’s study, Luxembourg keeps enrolment fees very low (the same for international and national students) and offers the Guillaume Dupaix International Master’s Scholarship.
benefits: A salaried PhD employment contract (about EUR 44,322 per year salary contribution). EUR 6,000 training and mobility allowance plus a travel lump sum. Up to four years of funding. Master's option: very low enrolment fees and a EUR 11,000 per year master's scholarship.
requirements: AFR Incoming PhD is open to candidates of any nationality. Must secure a doctoral position at an eligible Luxembourg host institution and spend more than 50% of the time in Luxembourg. Application is submitted jointly by the candidate and the host institution. Master's scholarship: international applicants with excellent academic records, not receiving Luxembourg state financial aid.
required_documents: For AFR PhD: a joint application by candidate and host institution, including a signed joint declaration. Research project proposal and work plan. Academic transcripts, degree certificates and CV. Letters of reference and proof of English. For the master's scholarship: degree certificates, transcripts, personal statement and recommendation letters.
summary: In Luxembourg, doctoral study is funded as a salaried research position rather than a traditional scholarship. The main…

title: American University in Cairo (AUC) Excellence Scholarship
description: The American University in Cairo (AUC) is Egypt’s premier English-language university and one of the leading liberal arts…
details:
The American University in Cairo (AUC) is Egypt’s premier English-language university and one of the leading liberal arts institutions in the Middle East. Founded in 1919 and accredited in both the United States and Egypt, it serves a diverse community drawn from dozens of countries on a modern campus in New Cairo. Its Excellence Scholarship Program is the university’s flagship merit award, designed to make an AUC education accessible to outstanding students regardless of their financial means.

The Excellence Scholarship Program is not a single award but a set of highly competitive, combinable scholarships. Coverage depends on the category, and because the awards can be stacked, the strongest candidates can reach up to 100 percent of tuition. Selection recognises a mix of academic achievement, exceptional talent in areas such as athletics, music, and the performing arts, and remarkable community-service contributions, and some categories also take financial need into account. The programme is open to international students as well as Egyptian national certificate holders.

Beyond the Excellence awards, AUC offers donor-funded undergraduate scholarships and graduate fellowships, including competitive fellowships for African students pursuing a master’s degree. The exact value, eligibility, and renewal terms differ from one scholarship to another, so applicants should review the specific category that fits their profile.

Applying is straightforward and tied to admission. Prospective undergraduates indicate their interest by checking the scholarship box in the online admission application, and a complete file, including academic records, English proficiency evidence, and recommendation letters, must be submitted by the deadline. Undergraduate Excellence applications generally close in early June, while graduate fellowship deadlines vary by programme, so confirm the current date on the official site. For talented students who want a rigorous, globally recognised education in the heart of the Arab world, AUC’s Excellence Scholarships are a compelling opportunity.
funding_type: Partial to Fully Funded (up to 100% tuition)
benefits: Tuition coverage ranging from partial up to 100 percent for the very best combined awards. A place at Egypt's leading English-language, US-accredited university. Renewable for the duration of undergraduate study, subject to meeting the scholarship terms. Access to a wide range of additional donor-funded scholarships and graduate fellowships.
requirements: Outstanding students applying for admission to AUC, including international applicants and Egyptian national certificate holders. Selection is based on academic achievement, exceptional talent (for example athletics, music, or performing arts), and community service; some categories also consider financial need. Awards are tiered by category and can be combined, with the strongest candidates reaching up to 100 percent of tuition. Graduate fellowships have their own eligibility (for example, the African Graduate Fellowship is for nationals of African countries other than Egypt). English proficiency is required (international TOEFL, Academic IELTS, or Duolingo); citizenship or an English-medium school does not exempt you.
required_documents: Online admission application with the scholarship section completed. Academic transcripts and secondary school certificates. Evidence of English proficiency (TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo). Two recommendation letters from high school teachers or counsellors. Any documents required for specific donor scholarships or graduate fellowships.
summary: The American University in Cairo (AUC) is Egypt’s premier English-language university and one of the leading liberal arts…

title: Trinity College Dublin Global Excellence Postgraduate Scholarship
university: Trinity College Dublin (the University of Dublin)
description: Trinity College Dublin (the University of Dublin), Ireland’s leading university, offers the Global Excellence Postgraduate Scholarship to support…
details:
Trinity College Dublin (the University of Dublin), Ireland’s leading university, offers the Global Excellence Postgraduate Scholarship to support outstanding non-EU students undertaking a taught master’s. It is a partial tuition award designed to recognise academic achievement and to support strong international students choosing Trinity, with a dedicated earlier deadline for some regions.

The award is a one-time tuition fee reduction of 2,000 to 5,000 euros, depending on the applicant’s region, applied to first-year tuition. It can be combined with other funding sources and comes with recognition as a Trinity Global Excellence scholar and access to Trinity’s research, societies, and Dublin’s student community.

Eligibility is for students with non-EU fee status (billed at the non-EU tuition rate) who hold a conditional or firm offer for a full-time postgraduate taught programme at Trinity, with strong academic achievement (around first-class-honours equivalent); Business, Engineering, Natural Sciences, Computer Science and Statistics, and Medicine/Dentistry are excluded, and applicants from China apply for the Claddagh Scholarship instead. You apply for and receive an offer for a taught master’s, complete the online Global Excellence Scholarship form (or email your regional manager) with your offer letter and a 200-word statement, and apply early since awards are made on a rolling basis. For non-EU master’s students aiming at Ireland, it is a helpful tuition award.
benefits: One-time tuition reduction of EUR 2,000 to 5,000. Recognition as a Trinity Global Excellence scholar. Can be combined with other funding sources. Access to Trinity's research, societies, and Dublin's student community.
requirements: Non-EU fee status, billed at the non-EU tuition rate. Hold a conditional or firm offer for a full-time postgraduate taught programme at Trinity. Strong academic achievement (around first-class-honours equivalent). Business, Engineering, Natural Sciences, and Computer Science & Statistics (and Medicine/Dentistry) are excluded. Applicants from China apply for the Claddagh Scholarship instead.
required_documents: A copy of your Trinity offer letter (conditional or firm). A 200-word statement on how you will contribute to the Trinity community. Basic personal details on the online form (or the regional email application).
summary: Trinity College Dublin (the University of Dublin), Ireland’s leading university, offers the Global Excellence Postgraduate Scholarship to support…

title: Aalto University Scholarship (Excellence / Finland Scholarship)
description: The Aalto University Excellence Scholarship is the university’s flagship merit award for talented international students starting an English-taught…
details:
The Aalto University Excellence Scholarship is the university’s flagship merit award for talented international students starting an English-taught master’s degree in Finland. It is offered as a tuition fee waiver covering either 100% (Category A) or 50% (Category B) of the tuition fee for the standard two-year, 120 ECTS master’s programme. The scholarship is open to fee-paying students, meaning citizens of countries outside the EU, EEA, and Switzerland who are liable to pay tuition at Aalto.

Aalto University sits in Espoo, in the Helsinki capital region, and was formed in 2010 from the merger of Finland’s leading schools of technology, business, and art and design. It consistently ranks among the world’s strongest universities in design, architecture, and engineering, and is known for its hands-on culture, world-class laboratories, and one of Europe’s largest student startup communities. Studying here places you inside a research-driven, highly international environment with close ties to industry.

The scholarship rewards academic excellence and is highly competitive, with the number of awards per programme depending on how many fee-paying students are admitted. There is no separate application form. When you apply for admission through Finland’s national Studyinfo.fi portal, you simply indicate that you also wish to be considered for the scholarship, and admission and scholarship decisions are assessed together. This makes it one of the most straightforward leading European awards to apply for.

It is important to plan your finances realistically. The scholarship covers tuition only and does not include living costs, which Aalto estimates at around 800 euros per month. Students from a few countries can also access dedicated awards, such as the Fulbright Aalto University Graduate Award for United States citizens. For ambitious students who want a top-ranked, innovation-focused master’s in a safe, high quality of life setting, the Aalto Excellence Scholarship is an excellent route into studying in Finland.
benefits: Tuition fee waiver of 100% (Category A) or 50% (Category B) for the standard two-year master's degree. Renewable for the second year provided you progress according to your approved personal study plan. Access to Aalto's research labs, design studios, makerspaces, and a large student startup ecosystem. A merit-based award from a globally ranked university, strengthening your academic and professional profile. Country-specific options for some applicants, such as the Fulbright Aalto University Graduate Award for United States citizens. Note: the scholarship covers tuition only and does not cover living costs (budget at least 800 euros per month).
requirements: Citizen of a country outside the EU, EEA, or Switzerland who is liable to pay tuition fees at Aalto University. Applying to an English-taught master's programme at Aalto (you may apply to up to two study options in one round). Hold, or expect to complete by the stated deadline, a bachelor's degree equivalent to at least 180 ECTS or three years of full-time study. Strong academic record; the scholarship is merit-based and highly competitive. Meet the English language requirements of your programme (for example IELTS or TOEFL), unless exempt through previous English-medium study. Business programmes may require GMAT or GRE; art and design programmes assess a portfolio and may admit strong candidates through alternative eligibility based on work experience. Indicate interest by answering Yes to the scholarship question on the admission application; no separate application is required. EU, EEA, and Swiss citizens are exempt from tuition fees and are therefore not eligible for this waiver.
required_documents: Online master's application submitted via Studyinfo.fi. Bachelor's degree certificate, or proof you will complete it by the stated deadline. Official academic transcripts, with certified English translations where needed. Proof of English proficiency (for example IELTS or TOEFL), unless exempt. GMAT or GRE scores where the programme requires them. Portfolio for art and design programmes, where applicable. Passport or official identity document.
summary: The Aalto University Excellence Scholarship is the university’s flagship merit award for talented international students starting an English-taught…

title: Central European University (CEU) Scholarships
description: Central European University (CEU) is a graduate-focused, English-language university now based in Vienna, known for the social sciences,…
details:
Central European University (CEU) is a graduate-focused, English-language university now based in Vienna, known for the social sciences, humanities, law, and public policy, and accredited in both the United States and Austria. CEU offers generous, merit-based financial aid to attract talented students from around the world to its master’s and doctoral programmes.

Funding scales with the level of study. Doctoral students can receive a full tuition waiver plus a monthly stipend of roughly 1,880 to 2,000 euros gross for up to 48 months, while master’s students can receive partial to full tuition waivers plus a monthly stipend of roughly 300 to 1,000 euros. Health insurance is provided to award holders, along with research and travel support and a vibrant international community in Vienna.

Scholarships are open to applicants of all nationalities who hold a bachelor’s degree for master’s study or a master’s degree for doctoral study (final-year students may apply) and who demonstrate English proficiency unless exempt. CEU uses multi-round admissions with several financial aid deadlines, so applying early matters; doctoral applicants are automatically considered for funding. You apply through the CEU portal, complete the financial aid section by the deadline, and admission and scholarship results are communicated together. For students aiming at a funded master’s or PhD in Europe, CEU is an excellent option.
benefits: Full or partial tuition waiver depending on level and merit. Monthly living stipend (higher for doctoral students, for up to 48 months). Health insurance for award holders. Research and travel support and a vibrant international academic community in Vienna.
requirements: Open to applicants of all nationalities. Hold a bachelor's degree for master's programmes, or a master's degree for doctoral programmes (final-year students may apply). Demonstrate English proficiency unless exempt. Apply by the official financial aid deadline to be considered for funding (PhD applicants are automatically considered).
required_documents: Online application through the CEU portal, with the financial aid section completed. Academic transcripts (undergraduate and graduate where applicable). Two or more letters of recommendation. Curriculum vitae and statement of purpose (research proposal and writing sample for PhD). Proof of English proficiency if required.
summary: Central European University (CEU) is a graduate-focused, English-language university now based in Vienna, known for the social sciences,…

title: Scuola Superiore Sant’Anna PhD Scholarship
description: Scuola Superiore Sant’Anna in Pisa is one of Italy’s elite public research schools, known for its highly selective,…
details:
Scuola Superiore Sant’Anna in Pisa is one of Italy’s elite public research schools, known for its highly selective, research-intensive doctoral programmes. It offers fully funded PhD scholarships to bright graduates from Italy and abroad, selecting candidates through a competitive examination and immersing them in interdisciplinary research groups and international networks.

The award is fully funded with no tuition fees, providing a doctoral scholarship of roughly 16,000 to 17,000 euros a year (paid in installments) plus a top-up for research stays abroad, for three or four years depending on the programme and renewed annually on a successful assessment. Total support is about 87,991 euros over a three-year programme and about 113,851 over a four-year programme.

Eligibility is open to graduates from Italy and abroad who hold (or are about to hold) a qualifying degree for doctoral admission, are selected by a competitive examination assessing academic background and research aptitude, and have a strong interest in an interdisciplinary, research-intensive environment. You choose a Sant’Anna PhD programme and read its call, submit the online application with all required documents before the deadline, sit the selective admission examination (written and/or oral, sometimes remote), and enrol if admitted. For ambitious researchers, Sant’Anna offers an outstanding, fully funded doctoral experience in Italy.
benefits: Full PhD scholarship for the duration of the programme, renewed each year. No tuition fees. Additional allowance for study and research periods abroad. Personalised training within the School's research groups and international networks.
requirements: Open to bright graduates from Italy and abroad. Hold (or be about to hold) a qualifying degree for doctoral admission. Selected by a competitive examination assessing academic background and research aptitude. Strong interest in an interdisciplinary, research-intensive environment.
required_documents: Online application through the programme's call. Academic transcripts and degree certificate(s). Research statement or proposal as specified by the programme. Curriculum vitae. Letters of reference and proof of English (or Italian) as required.
summary: Scuola Superiore Sant’Anna in Pisa is one of Italy’s elite public research schools, known for its highly selective,…

title: VinUniversity Scholarship
university: VinUniversity (founded by Vingroup; partnered with Cornell University and the University of Pennsylvania)
description: VinUniversity, a private university in Vietnam founded by Vingroup in partnership with Cornell University and the University of…
details:
VinUniversity, a private university in Vietnam founded by Vingroup in partnership with Cornell University and the University of Pennsylvania, offers a range of scholarships and financial aid to undergraduate students, including international students. The awards combine merit scholarships, need-based aid, and a tuition subsidy in a global curriculum taught in English.

Support varies by award. Merit scholarships include the President’s Excellence Scholarship (a full ride covering 100 percent tuition plus living expenses and about 1,500 US dollars), the Provost’s Merit Scholarship (100 percent tuition), and the Dean’s Distinction Scholarship (80 to 90 percent tuition); need-based financial aid covers 50 to 80 percent of tuition, and a 35 percent Vingroup tuition subsidy applies to admitted students who do not receive a merit scholarship. Awards run for the full undergraduate degree, renewed each year on meeting the criteria.

Eligibility is open to international students of all nationalities admitted to a VinUniversity undergraduate programme, with outstanding academic performance plus qualities such as creativity, ambition, and resilience (for merit awards) or demonstrated financial need (for need-based aid); study is English-taught and no separate scholarship application is required. You submit the online undergraduate admission application through the VinUni portal, upload transcripts, essays, test scores, and references, and all admitted applicants are automatically assessed for merit scholarships (apply separately for need-based aid if required). For international undergraduates aiming at Vietnam, VinUniversity offers strong, well-supported scholarships.
benefits: Tuition coverage from 50 up to 100 percent depending on the award. Full-ride President's Excellence Scholarship adds living expenses (about USD 1,500). A 35 percent Vingroup tuition subsidy for non-scholarship admitted students. Access to a global curriculum with Cornell and UPenn collaboration and research with highly cited faculty.
requirements: Open to international students of all nationalities. Admitted to a VinUniversity undergraduate programme. Outstanding academic performance plus qualities such as creativity, ambition, and resilience (merit awards). Demonstrated financial need (need-based aid). English-taught study; no separate scholarship application is required (all admitted applicants are assessed automatically).
required_documents: Online admission application via the VinUni portal. Academic transcripts (translated to English or Vietnamese if needed). Essays and personal statement. Standardised test results and English proficiency certificate. Curriculum vitae and references; evidence of non-academic achievements.
summary: VinUniversity, a private university in Vietnam founded by Vingroup in partnership with Cornell University and the University of…

title: University of Manitoba Graduate Fellowship (UMGF)
university: University of Manitoba, Faculty of Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies
description: The University of Manitoba Graduate Fellowship (UMGF) is offered by the University of Manitoba’s Faculty of Graduate and…
details:
The University of Manitoba Graduate Fellowship (UMGF) is offered by the University of Manitoba’s Faculty of Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies to support research-based master’s and doctoral students, including international students. It is a merit-based living stipend that frees students to focus on thesis research within a strong research community.

The award provides an annual stipend of 20,000 Canadian dollars for master’s students (for up to two years, up to 40,000 total) or 25,000 for doctoral students (for up to four years, up to 100,000 total), with a maximum combined UMGF support of five years. It is renewed on satisfactory academic standing and may be topped up by departmental awards or Tri-Agency stipends.

Eligibility is open to students of all nationalities admitted to a full-time research-based master’s or PhD programme at Manitoba, with a minimum admission GPA of 3.0 (some departments require higher) and no grade below C+; the programme must be eligible for Canadian Tri-Agency funding (MBA, MFin, and MSCM are not eligible), and pre-master’s and occasional students are not eligible. You apply for admission to a research programme, contact your department about its UMGF process and internal deadline, and the department nominates its selected students to the Faculty. For research graduate students aiming at Canada, the UMGF is a generous stipend.
benefits: Annual stipend of CAD 20,000 (master's) or CAD 25,000 (PhD). Multi-year support, renewed on satisfactory academic standing. Frees students to focus on thesis research within a strong research community. May be topped up by departmental awards or Tri-Agency stipends.
requirements: Open to students of all nationalities. Admitted to a full-time research-based master's or PhD programme at the University of Manitoba. Minimum admission GPA of 3.0 (some departments require higher), with no grade below C+. Programme must be eligible for Canadian Tri-Agency funding (MBA, MFin, and MSCM are not eligible). Pre-master's and occasional students are not eligible.
required_documents: Complete application for admission to a master's or PhD programme. Official academic transcripts (certified translations if not in English or French). Curriculum vitae and statement of research interest. Letters of recommendation. Any additional documents requested by the department.
summary: The University of Manitoba Graduate Fellowship (UMGF) is offered by the University of Manitoba’s Faculty of Graduate and…

title: National Taiwan University (NTU) Scholarship for International Degree Students
description: National Taiwan University (NTU) is Taiwan’s leading university, and it offers scholarships to international degree-seeking students across undergraduate,…
details:
National Taiwan University (NTU) is Taiwan’s leading university, and it offers scholarships to international degree-seeking students across undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral levels. The awards combine a tuition waiver with a monthly stipend, helping talented students from around the world to study in Taipei in either English-taught or Chinese-taught programmes.

Support takes the form of a tuition and miscellaneous fee waiver of up to around 65,000 New Taiwan dollars per semester, plus a monthly living stipend (commonly 8,000 to 15,000 dollars for bachelor’s and master’s students and 10,000 to 15,000 for PhD students, higher in science and engineering). Amounts vary by award and college, and the stipend is retained by meeting the grade standard each semester.

Eligibility is for international degree-seeking students admitted to NTU under Taiwan’s regulations for international students (dual-degree students are excluded), from any country, with a strong academic record (and research experience expected for master’s and PhD applicants) and the required language proficiency. The scholarship is considered automatically through the admission application: you apply for an NTU degree programme through the online system, select the scholarship option, upload your documents, and await the combined admission and scholarship result. For international students aiming at Taiwan, NTU is a strong, well-supported choice.

details:
The Ontario Trillium Scholarship (OTS) is a prestigious doctoral award funded by the Government of Ontario and administered by participating Ontario universities in Canada. It is designed to attract the best international PhD students to the province, recognising outstanding academic achievement with substantial, renewable funding.

The award is generous, providing 40,000 Canadian dollars per year (two-thirds from the province and one-third from the university) toward tuition, living, and research costs, renewable for up to four years of doctoral study. Scholars gain access to top Ontario research facilities, supervision, and mentorship, and those who later gain permanent residency remain eligible for the balance of the award.

Eligibility is for international students holding (or eligible for) a valid Canadian study permit who are starting a full-time PhD at a participating Ontario university, with a first-class average (A- or 80 percent Ontario equivalent) generally in the last two years of full-time study, who are not currently studying at an Ontario institution and not holding certain other major Canadian awards. You apply for admission to a full-time PhD programme and submit a strong application by the programme deadline (most universities nominate automatically), and selected nominees are advised by the graduate studies office. For top international doctoral students, the OTS is a flagship opportunity in Canada.
benefits: CAD 40,000 per year toward tuition, living, and research costs. Renewable for up to four years of doctoral study. Access to top Ontario research facilities, supervision, and mentorship. Recipients who later gain permanent residency remain eligible for the balance of the award.

details:
The Global Excellence Scholarship is offered by the University of Western Australia (UWA), a leading Australian research university, to recognise high-achieving international students. It is an automatic tuition discount, tiered by academic results, that helps international students afford an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree.

The award is partial funding, providing an annual tuition fee discount for the full standard duration of the course: up to 48,000 Australian dollars over four years for undergraduate degrees, up to 24,000 over two years for postgraduate coursework, and up to 60,000 for some five-year combined degrees. The exact amount is tiered by ATAR or WAM, and it is awarded automatically with no separate application form.

Eligibility is for international (full-fee-paying) students (not Australian or New Zealand citizens or Australian permanent residents) holding an offer for an eligible undergraduate or postgraduate coursework programme at UWA, who achieve at least an ATAR equivalent of 85.00 or a UWA WAM equivalent of 65.00; some high-demand professional degrees (for example certain medicine and dentistry pathways) are excluded. You apply for admission, submit all required academic documents and transcripts, and if you meet the threshold you are automatically assessed, with the award and value confirmed in your offer letter. For high-achieving international students aiming at Australia, it is a valuable, automatic tuition award.
