details:
The Macquarie University Research Excellence Scholarship (iMQRES) is the main award for international research students at Macquarie University in Sydney, Australia. It supports talented candidates undertaking a Master of Research or a PhD, combining a tuition fee offset with a living stipend so that scholars can focus on research within the university’s priority areas.

The award covers a full international tuition fee offset for the standard duration of the degree, along with an annual living stipend of around 41,000 Australian dollars paid fortnightly; some awards add Overseas Student Health Cover, visa-cost support, and a transport concession. Scholars gain access to supervision, laboratories, and the Graduate Research Academy training programme.

Eligibility is for international students (not Australian or New Zealand citizens or Australian permanent residents) applying for a Master of Research or PhD at Macquarie, with a strong academic record and research potential; many recent awards require the qualifying degree to be completed at the time of application, and applicants must meet English requirements. You first identify a research area and supervisor aligned with Macquarie’s strategy, then submit a combined research-degree and scholarship application before the round deadline with transcripts, a proposal, a CV, and referees, and applications are ranked on merit and research fit. For international research students, it is Macquarie’s flagship funded route.

title: Amsterdam Excellence Scholarship (AES)
description: The Amsterdam Excellence Scholarship (AES) is the University of Amsterdam’s most prestigious merit scholarship, created to attract exceptionally…
details:
The Amsterdam Excellence Scholarship (AES) is the University of Amsterdam’s most prestigious merit scholarship, created to attract exceptionally talented students from outside Europe to its master’s programmes. The University of Amsterdam (UvA) is the Netherlands’ largest university and consistently ranks among the best in Europe, and the AES is reserved for a small number of truly outstanding candidates each year.

The scholarship is worth 25,000 euros, intended to cover tuition fees and living expenses for one academic year, with the possibility of an extension into a second year for eligible two-year master’s programmes. Beyond the funding, AES scholars join a dedicated community with a tailored extracurricular programme and gain access to an alumni and sponsor network, adding mentoring and connections to the financial support.

Eligibility is demanding. Applicants must hold a non-EU, non-EEA, and non-Swiss nationality, rank in the top 10 percent of their class or graduating year, and be admitted, or provisionally admitted, to an eligible UvA master’s programme for the first time. Candidates cannot already hold another full scholarship for the same period and must not be eligible for Dutch study finance. Because places are very limited, selection is highly competitive and based on academic excellence and motivation.

Applying is integrated with the master’s admission process. You apply to an eligible UvA master’s programme and tick the scholarship box on the application, then upload the AES documents, including a statement from a dean or teacher confirming your top 10 percent standing and a motivation letter of up to 500 words. The deadline is 15 January. Graduate schools shortlist candidates and a central committee selects the recipients. For top international students aiming for a master’s in Amsterdam, the AES is a flagship route to funding.
benefits: EUR 25,000 per year covering tuition and living costs. Membership of the AES community with a tailored extracurricular programme. Access to the AES alumni and sponsor network. Possible second-year extension for two-year programmes.
requirements: Hold a non-EU/EEA (and non-Swiss) nationality. Rank in the top 10 percent of your class or graduating year. Admitted, or provisionally admitted, to an eligible UvA master's programme for the first time. Not in receipt of another full scholarship for the same period of study. Not eligible for Dutch study finance (Studiefinanciering).

A letter from a dean or teacher confirming you are in the top 10 percent. One or two letters of recommendation. Motivation letter of up to 500 words, explaining why you should be nominated. Passport copy.

The award helps fee-paying students from outside Europe to study at a renowned institution in the health and life sciences, with around ten scholarships shared across its programmes each year.

The scholarship covers the full tuition fee for the chosen global master’s programme (or the KI-taught portion of jointly delivered programmes). It is a tuition-only award, so living costs, travel, and other expenses are not covered, and it is granted on merit through an assessment of your CV and qualifications.

Eligibility is for fee-paying students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who have applied to and are admissible for an eligible KI global master’s starting in the autumn, are new first-year students, have paid the master’s application fee, and meet all academic admission requirements. The process has two steps: you apply to the programme via University Admissions by the January deadline and pay the fee, then submit the separate scholarship application during the February window, with notification usually in late April. For international students aiming at a top medical university, it is a valuable tuition award.

title: EPFL Excellence Fellowship
description: The EPFL Excellence Fellowship is a prestigious merit award from the Ecole Polytechnique Federale de Lausanne, one of…
details:
The EPFL Excellence Fellowship is a prestigious merit award from the Ecole Polytechnique Federale de Lausanne, one of Europe’s top science and technology universities. It is designed to attract outstanding students to begin a master’s degree at EPFL, rewarding those with remarkable academic results who also stand out through extracurricular achievements in areas such as sport, the arts, civic life, or entrepreneurship.

EPFL, based in Lausanne on the shores of Lake Geneva, is consistently ranked among the world’s leading institutions for engineering and technology. Its community spans more than 120 nationalities, and the university is known for cutting-edge research, strong industry links, and a campus culture built around innovation and technology transfer. A master’s from EPFL is highly regarded by employers and research institutions worldwide.

The fellowship is worth CHF 10,000 per semester for up to four semesters, which can total around CHF 40,000 across a standard master’s. The funding usually covers the taught semesters of the master’s cycle plus one semester for the master’s project. External candidates also receive a guaranteed room in a student residence, and all holders receive a certificate of excellence on graduation. It is important to understand that the fellowship is financial support towards your studies and living costs, but it does not pay tuition fees or rent, which remain your responsibility.

Applying is simple and open to candidates of any nationality. There is no separate form: you apply to one EPFL master’s programme through the online application and tick the box asking to be considered for an Excellence Fellowship. Most applicants provide two recommendation letters submitted directly by their referees. Selection is handled by the Excellence Fellowships Committee after an initial screening by the academic sections. There are two application rounds each year, aligned with the master’s deadlines, and the fellowship can be renewed for the second year provided you earn at least 50 ECTS credits and maintain an average of 5.0 out of 6. For talented students aiming for a world-class technical master’s in Switzerland, this is a flagship opportunity.
benefits: CHF 10,000 per semester for up to four semesters (up to about CHF 40,000 across a standard master's). Funding covers the taught master's semesters plus one semester for the master's project (three to four semesters depending on programme). Not eligible if you already hold, or are already enrolled in, a master's degree in the same or a similar field. TOEFL or GRE scores are welcome but optional and do not affect the fellowship decision.

title: University of Westminster Full International Scholarship
description: The University of Westminster Full International Scholarship is the university’s most prestigious and competitive award, created to fully…
details:
The University of Westminster Full International Scholarship is the university’s most prestigious and competitive award, created to fully fund a talented student from a developing country through an entire undergraduate degree in London. Unlike most UK scholarships, which offer only a partial fee discount, this award removes nearly every financial barrier to studying abroad, which is why it attracts applicants from around the world each year.

The University of Westminster is a long-established public university in central London, with a strong reputation for media, design, architecture, business, law, and the sciences, and a highly international student body. Its main campuses sit close to landmarks such as Regent Street and Baker Street, placing scholarship holders at the heart of one of the world’s leading student cities.

The scholarship is genuinely comprehensive. It covers full tuition fees for the standard duration of the degree, university accommodation, a contribution towards living expenses, and return flights to and from London. Funding is renewed each year of the course, subject to satisfactory academic progress, so a successful applicant can complete their studies with their core costs met throughout.

Awards are decided on three criteria: academic excellence, demonstrated financial need, and development potential, meaning the university looks for students who will use their education to contribute to their home country. The scholarship is aimed at international, overseas fee-paying students from developing or middle-income nations; applicants from high-income countries are not eligible, and it is not open to those who already hold an equivalent or higher qualification.

Because it is so generous, competition is intense and the university funds only a small number of students, so a strong, carefully prepared application is essential. You must first apply for and receive an offer for a full-time undergraduate course at Westminster, and then submit the dedicated scholarship application with your supporting documents before the published deadline. For high-achieving students from developing countries who need full funding to study in the UK, this is one of the most valuable undergraduate scholarships available.
benefits: Full tuition fee waiver for the standard duration of the undergraduate degree. University accommodation. A contribution towards living expenses. Return flights to and from London. Renewed each year of the course, subject to satisfactory academic progress.
requirements: International, overseas fee-paying student from a developing or middle-income country; applicants from high-income countries are not eligible. Hold a conditional or unconditional offer for a full-time undergraduate degree at the University of Westminster before applying. Strong academic record, together with demonstrated financial need and development potential. Intend to use your degree to contribute to the development of your home country. Not already a graduate holding an equivalent or higher qualification (no second undergraduate or postgraduate-level applicants). Able to meet the university's English language and entry requirements for your chosen course. You may apply for only one Westminster scholarship in a given cycle.

Official academic transcripts, translated into English where required. Personal statement covering your achievements, financial need, and development goals. title: Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme (HKPFS)
description: The Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme (HKPFS) is one of Asia’s most prestigious and generous doctoral funding programmes.…
details:
The Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme (HKPFS) is one of Asia’s most prestigious and generous doctoral funding programmes. Established in 2009 by the Research Grants Council (RGC) of Hong Kong, it aims to attract the world’s best research students to pursue full-time PhD study at the territory’s leading universities. Around 400 fellowships are awarded each year, and the scheme is open to outstanding applicants of any nationality, ethnicity, or prior work background.

Fellows can study at any of the eight institutions funded by the University Grants Committee: the University of Hong Kong, the Chinese University of Hong Kong, the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, City University of Hong Kong, the Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hong Kong Baptist University, Lingnan University, and the Education University of Hong Kong. Several of these rank among the top universities in Asia and the world, offering advanced facilities, international supervision, and strong research output across the sciences, engineering, business, humanities, and social sciences.

The fellowship provides a substantial annual stipend, currently about HK$344,400 (roughly US$44,150) for the 2026/27 cohort, plus a yearly conference and research travel allowance of about HK$14,400, for up to three years. For programmes with a four-year normative period, the host university typically funds the additional year. On top of the core package, most universities add their own significant support, which can include full tuition waivers, entrance scholarships, cash awards, stipend top-ups, and guaranteed first-year accommodation, making the overall value considerably higher.

Applying involves two steps. You first submit an initial application through the RGC’s electronic system to obtain a reference number, choosing up to two programmes at one or two universities. You then submit a full PhD application to each chosen university, quoting that reference number. Selection is highly competitive and assessed under two broad panels covering science and technology, and humanities and social sciences. For researchers seeking a fully funded PhD in a dynamic, globally connected hub where East meets West, HKPFS is a standout opportunity.
benefits: Annual stipend of about HK$344,400 (roughly US$44,150) for the 2026/27 cohort, paid for up to three years. Annual conference and research-related travel allowance of about HK$14,400. A fourth year of support provided by the host university where the PhD has a four-year normative period. University add-ons at many institutions, such as tuition or composition fee waivers, entrance and cash awards, stipend top-ups, and guaranteed first-year accommodation. Access to world-class laboratories, international supervision, and a vibrant, globally connected research community. Note: stipend and allowance amounts are set by the RGC each year, so confirm the current figures for your intake.
requirements: Open to students of any nationality, ethnicity, age, or prior work experience. Seeking admission as a new full-time PhD student at one of the eight UGC-funded universities in Hong Kong. Outstanding academic record together with strong research ability and potential. Excellent communication, interpersonal, and leadership qualities. Meet the specific admission and English language requirements (for example IELTS or TOEFL) of your chosen university and programme. Able to commit to full-time doctoral study; the initial RGC application allows up to two programme choices at one or two universities. Note: applicants not selected for the fellowship may still be offered regular PhD admission with university studentships.
required_documents: Completed initial application on the RGC HKPFS electronic system (to obtain a reference number). Full PhD application to each chosen university, quoting the RGC reference number. Academic transcripts and degree certificates. Research proposal or statement of purpose. Two or more academic referee reports. Curriculum vitae. English language test scores (for example IELTS or TOEFL) if required by the programme. Passport or official identity document.
summary: The Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme (HKPFS) is one of Asia’s most prestigious and generous doctoral funding programmes.…

title: ERSU Palermo Right to Study Scholarship 2026/27 (Sicily, Italy)
university: ERSU Palermo (Ente Regionale per il Diritto allo Studio Universitario di Palermo), Regione Siciliana
description: ERSU Palermo (Ente Regionale per il Diritto allo Studio Universitario di Palermo) is the Sicilian regional agency that…
details:
ERSU Palermo (Ente Regionale per il Diritto allo Studio Universitario di Palermo) is the Sicilian regional agency that delivers right-to-study support for university students in western Sicily, on behalf of Regione Siciliana.
It pairs an annual cash maintenance grant with university tuition exemption, free or subsidised meals, and the option of a place in a university residence, for capable students from lower-income households.
It covers the University of Palermo, LUMSA Palermo, UniCamillus Cefalu, and SSML CIELS Palermo, plus the area’s AFAM institutions: the Academies of Fine Arts and the Music Conservatories in Palermo, Trapani, Agrigento, Caltanissetta, Ribera, and San Martino delle Scale.
It is open to Italian and international students alike, with students whose family lives abroad assessed through a parified income indicator (ISEEU/ISPEU parificato).
For the 2025/26 cycle the grant ranged from about EUR 1,425 to about EUR 8,133, depending on residency status and income band.
The 2026/27 call is the relevant cycle now; applications are submitted online, and in recent years the deadline has fallen at 14:00 on 22 July.
International students should prepare their parified-income documents early through the ERSU-partnered CAF, because the paperwork takes time and the deadline is firm.

title: DiSCo Lazio Right to Study Scholarship 2026/2027 (Regione Lazio, Italy)
university: DiSCo Lazio (Ente Regionale per il Diritto allo Studio e alla Conoscenza), for Regione Lazio
description: The DiSCo Lazio Right to Study Scholarship (Borsa di Studio per il Diritto allo Studio) is the regional,…
details: The DiSCo Lazio Right to Study Scholarship (Borsa di Studio per il Diritto allo Studio) is the regional, need plus merit based support scheme for university students in the Lazio region of Italy, delivered by DiSCo Lazio on behalf of Regione Lazio. It provides an annual maintenance grant, subsidised meals, the option of university accommodation, contributions for international mobility, and graduation prizes, to students enrolled at any university, AFAM institution, or higher-education institute with its legal seat in Lazio. The 2026/2027 call is open: applications run from 10 June 2026 to noon on 22 July 2026. It is open to Italian and international students alike, with international students and Italians resident abroad assessed through a parified income indicator (ISEEUP). The scheme is one of the largest of its kind in Italy and in 2025/2026 reached over 38,000 student winners.
benefits: Annual maintenance scholarship Subsidised university meals (two meals a day, about EUR 600/year of value) Option to apply for a place in DiSCo university residences (accommodation ranking extended to ISEE up to EUR 40,000 in 2025/2026) Contributions for international mobility (study or internship abroad) Graduation prizes. Under Italian right-to-study rules, scholarship winners are generally exempt from university tuition fees and the regional tax (confirm exact terms in the bando).
requirements: Enrol, or intend to enrol, at a university, AFAM institution, or higher-education institute with legal seat in Lazio (for example Sapienza, Tor Vergata, Roma Tre). Meet the income test (2025/2026 limits: ISEE up to EUR 27,948.60, ISPE up to EUR 60,757.87; international students and Italians abroad use the ISEEUP). The embassy track for each intake usually opens around April and closes between May and June depending on the country, followed by written exams and interviews at the embassy. Check the Japanese embassy in your country for the current cycle’s exact dates.

title: Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP) Fellowships
university: Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP)
description: The Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP) is a world-leading research centre for the physical and…
details:
The Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP) is a world-leading research centre for the physical and mathematical sciences, based in Trieste, Italy, and operating under a tripartite agreement between the Italian Government, UNESCO, and the International Atomic Energy Agency. It was founded in 1964 by the Pakistani Nobel laureate Abdus Salam, and from the start its mission has been to advance science in the developing world, which gives it an especially strong link to students from Pakistan, Africa, and other developing regions.

ICTP’s flagship route for graduate students is the Postgraduate Diploma Programme, an intensive one-year, pre-PhD course that has prepared talented graduates for doctoral study at leading universities in Europe and North America since 1991. The diploma is offered in Condensed Matter Physics, High Energy/Cosmology/Astroparticle Physics, Mathematics, Earth System Physics, and Quantitative Life Sciences. Each year a limited number of fully supported places, around ten per field, are reserved for students from developing countries, with particular emphasis on the least developed regions.

Beyond the diploma, ICTP runs other supported opportunities, including the Sandwich Training Educational Programme (STEP) for PhD students already enrolled in developing-country institutions, and Associateship schemes for established researchers. The centre also hosts a year-round programme of schools, workshops, and conferences.

Selected diploma students receive their studies free of tuition, along with a living stipend, accommodation, and a travel grant to and from Trieste. Selection is based on academic performance and recommendation letters, with the committee aiming for both gender balance and broad geographical representation. Applicants to the diploma are generally under 28 and hold a degree equivalent to an MSc, or an exceptionally strong BSc, in physics, mathematics, or a closely related field. For young scientists from the developing world, ICTP offers a respected and genuinely life-changing gateway into international research.
benefits: Tuition-free study on the chosen ICTP programme. Monthly living stipend during your stay at ICTP. Accommodation and a travel grant to and from Trieste for diploma students from developing countries. Access to ICTP's library, computing facilities, and research resources. Mentoring by leading physicists and mathematicians, and a strong pathway into PhD study abroad. An active global alumni network and ongoing collaboration with ICTP.
requirements: Citizen of a developing country that is a member of the UN, UNESCO, or IAEA. For the Postgraduate Diploma: hold a degree equivalent to an MSc, or an exceptionally good BSc, in physics, mathematics, or a related field. Generally under 28 years of age for the Diploma Programme (exceptions in rare cases). Strong academic record and clear research potential. Adequate subject knowledge for the chosen field (for example quantum mechanics, statistical mechanics, and electrodynamics for physics streams). Fluent in English; no IELTS or TOEFL is required, but proficiency is expected. Separate eligibility applies to STEP sandwich PhD candidates (already enrolled in a developing-country PhD) and to Associates (established researchers).
required_documents: ICTP online application for the chosen programme. Academic transcripts and degree certificates. Curriculum vitae with any research experience. Two academic recommendation letters. Statement of purpose or research interests. Passport copy. GRE Physics may be recommended for some streams but is not mandatory.
summary: The Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP) is a world-leading research centre for the physical and…

title: Stellenbosch University Postgraduate International Scholarship
description: Stellenbosch University, one of South Africa’s leading research universities, offers postgraduate scholarships to international students through its Postgraduate…
details:
Stellenbosch University, one of South Africa’s leading research universities, offers postgraduate scholarships to international students through its Postgraduate Funding Office. The awards support Honours, master’s, and doctoral students with an annual contribution toward international tuition, recognising academic merit and research potential at a top African university.

The award is partial funding, ranging from around 50,000 to 120,000 rand a year depending on degree level and academic merit, covering a significant portion of international tuition, and renewable for the duration of the programme with satisfactory progress. Scholars gain access to Stellenbosch’s world-class research facilities. The duration is one year for Honours, up to two for a master’s, and up to three for a doctorate.

Eligibility is for non-South African citizens accepted into a full-time Stellenbosch postgraduate programme, with an outstanding undergraduate record (for Honours or coursework master’s) or a strong record plus a viable research proposal and confirmed supervisor (for research master’s or PhD), who cannot hold another full scholarship, work more than 20 hours a week, or already hold a qualification at the same or higher level. You submit two applications, first for admission, then for the Postgraduate Scholarship Programme via your faculty’s link, uploading the required documents by the deadline. For international postgraduates in Africa, it is a valuable, merit-based award.
benefits: Annual award of R50,000 to R120,000 depending on level and merit. Covers a significant portion of international tuition. Renewable for the duration of the programme with satisfactory progress. Access to Stellenbosch's world-class research facilities.
requirements: Non-South African citizen accepted into a full-time Stellenbosch postgraduate programme. For Honours or coursework master's: an outstanding undergraduate academic record. For research master's or PhD: a strong record plus a viable research proposal with a confirmed supervisor. details:
The Pontificia Universidad Catolica de Chile (UC Chile) is one of Latin America’s top universities, and it offers scholarships to support international students undertaking graduate study, especially at doctoral level. The awards combine tuition support with a living stipend, helping talented students from around the world to pursue a master’s or PhD in Santiago.

The support ranges from full or partial tuition waivers to a monthly living stipend (around 500,000 to 800,000 Chilean pesos depending on the programme), with health insurance support, research travel funding for PhD students, and Spanish language support courses, for the duration of the graduate programme. Some internal awards, such as the Assistant or Instructor Scholarship, cover the full fee plus a maintenance stipend.

Eligibility is for international students (non-Chilean citizens) applying for a full-time graduate programme at PUC, with a strong academic record (typically a GPA of 5.5 or above on the Chilean scale or equivalent); PhD applicants need a master’s, and language requirements vary by programme (Spanish for most, English for some). You apply for admission to a UC Chile graduate programme, and once admitted, apply for the university’s internal scholarships through the Vice-Rectory for Research and Graduate Studies, or for external funding. For students drawn to Chile, PUC offers strong, supported graduate study.

title: University of Sao Paulo International Mobility Scholarship
university: University of Sao Paulo (USP), International Cooperation Office (AUCANI)
description: The International Mobility Scholarship is offered by the University of Sao Paulo (USP), Brazil’s leading university, through its…
details:
The International Mobility Scholarship is offered by the University of Sao Paulo (USP), Brazil’s leading university, through its International Cooperation Office (AUCANI). It supports international exchange students from partner institutions to undertake a study or research period at USP, where tuition is free for all students.

The award provides a tuition waiver (USP is tuition-free), a monthly stipend of around 2,200 reais for master’s-level students or 3,300 for doctoral-level students, university housing support or a housing allowance, a Portuguese language course, and access to USP research facilities and libraries, for the agreed exchange period (typically one or two semesters).

Eligibility is for students enrolled at a foreign higher education institution that has an exchange agreement with USP (from their second year of study onward), with a strong academic record; Portuguese is recommended but not always required (many programmes accept English-speaking students). You cannot apply directly as an individual: your home institution must officially nominate you through USP’s registration platform (Mundus), after which USP schools process the application and issue a letter of acceptance. Students generally fund their own travel and living costs beyond the stipend. For exchange students aiming at Brazil, USP offers a strong, tuition-free mobility opportunity.
benefits: Tuition waiver (tuition is free at USP for all students). Monthly stipend of around R 2,200 (master's) or R 3,300 (PhD). University housing support or a housing allowance. Portuguese language course. Access to all USP research facilities and libraries.
requirements: Open to international students from all countries enrolled at a foreign institution with an exchange agreement with USP (from your second year of study onward). required_documents: USP graduate or exchange admission application. Academic transcripts and degree certificates. Research proposal. Curriculum vitae (Lattes format preferred). Two or three academic reference letters. Passport copy. Language proficiency proof.

details:
The University of Auckland International Excellence Scholarship recognises high-achieving international students entering undergraduate and taught postgraduate study at New Zealand’s leading university. It is a renewable tuition reduction that rewards academic excellence and helps new international students with the cost of their degree.

The award provides a tuition fee reduction of 10,000 New Zealand dollars a year, renewable for the normal duration of the degree (up to four years for undergraduate), credited toward compulsory first-semester tuition fees. Up to about 50 awards are made, and the scholarship can be combined with some other university awards.

Eligibility is for new international students (not citizens, permanent residents, or resident-visa holders of New Zealand or Australia) holding a conditional or unconditional offer, enrolling full-time and on-campus in an undergraduate degree (with overseas qualifications), a Postgraduate Diploma, or a master’s of one year or more, with an admissions GPA of at least about 6.0; you are not eligible if you have done prior tertiary study in New Zealand, are a NZ school-leaver, or a distance student. You submit the scholarship application form online (applications open about six weeks before the closing date) by the deadline (around April for Semester 2, October for Semester 1). For new international students aiming at New Zealand, it is a valuable, renewable tuition award.
benefits: NZD 10,000 tuition fee reduction per year. Renewable for the normal duration of the degree (up to four years for undergraduate). Automatically assessed once the form is submitted. Combinable with other university awards in some cases. Up to about 50 awards available.

For research postgraduates aiming at Malaysia, it is a well-supported, fully funded route.

requirements: Non-Malaysian citizen (the scheme is also open to Malaysians) holding an offer for a full research master's or PhD at UM. details:
The CERN Doctoral Student Programme allows PhD students to carry out part of their doctoral research at CERN, the European Organization for Nuclear Research near Geneva, home to the world’s largest particle physics laboratory. It is aimed at students working on a thesis in applied fields relevant to CERN, including particle and accelerator physics, computing, and engineering, and it gives access to facilities and expertise that few institutions can match.

Selected students receive a monthly living allowance of around 3,632 Swiss francs, a travel allowance for one round trip between their home country and CERN, comprehensive health insurance under CERN’s own scheme, and professional development opportunities, while remaining registered as PhD students at their home university. Placements run from six to 36 months.

Eligibility is open to students enrolled in a doctoral programme at a recognised university, working on a CERN-relevant thesis, who have completed the required master’s-level coursework, have a strong STEM record, and are proficient in English or French; applicants should be nationals of a CERN Member or Associate Member State. You apply online through the CERN careers portal with your CV, motivation letter, transcripts, and thesis details, and provide referee contacts, before the relevant selection deadline (the committee meets several times a year). For doctoral researchers in physics and engineering, it is a world-class opportunity.
benefits: Monthly living allowance of around CHF 3,632. Travel allowance for one round trip between your home country and CERN. Comprehensive health insurance under CERN's own scheme. Access to CERN's world-class research facilities and computing infrastructure. Networking with thousands of scientists from around the world. Professional development workshops and seminars.
requirements: Enrolled in a doctoral programme at a recognised university at the time of application, and remaining registered throughout the period at CERN. Working on a doctoral thesis in a field relevant to CERN (particle physics, accelerator physics, computing, engineering, and similar). Completed all required master's-level coursework. title: African Leadership University Scholarship
description: African Leadership University (ALU) is a pioneering pan-African institution with campuses in Kigali, Rwanda, and Pamplemousses, Mauritius, built…
details:
African Leadership University (ALU) is a pioneering pan-African institution with campuses in Kigali, Rwanda, and Pamplemousses, Mauritius, built around a mission to develop a generation of ethical, entrepreneurial leaders for the continent. Rather than traditional majors, ALU students pursue real-world missions and work on Africa’s pressing challenges, choosing degrees such as the BSc in Entrepreneurial Leadership, the BSc in Software Engineering, and the BA in International Business and Trade. Learning is self-directed and experiential, with access to a network of hubs across several cities.

ALU’s funding is need-based and offered to admitted students who cannot otherwise afford the fees. Support ranges from partial grants, which cover part of the tuition, to full-ride scholarships, which are very limited and highly competitive. The full-ride awards, often delivered in partnership with the Mastercard Foundation and other donors, cover full tuition and additional support throughout a scholar’s studies, which can include accommodation, meals, a living allowance, and in some cases travel and a laptop. The exact terms depend on the specific scholarship contract and partnering donor.

The opportunity is aimed at talented African students who show strong academic promise, leadership potential, and an entrepreneurial mindset, alongside demonstrated financial need. Because aid is limited, a carefully evidenced application matters: students must first apply and be admitted to ALU, score well on the ALU Leadership Assessment, and then indicate and document their need for financial aid.

ALU offers an unusually practical model: graduates leave with real work experience, a strong professional network across Africa, and skills designed to stay relevant as the world changes. For ambitious young Africans who want a leadership-focused degree on the continent without the burden of full fees, ALU’s scholarships and grants are well worth pursuing. Tuition is modest by global standards, so even partial aid can make studying at ALU achievable.

Leadership potential and an entrepreneurial mindset. Full-ride scholarships are very limited and highly competitive; many applicants receive partial grants instead.

details:
The University of Bologna (Alma Mater Studiorum), one of the oldest universities in the world, offers study grants to international students to support their study in Italy. These merit-based grants, awarded through dedicated calls such as the International Talents @Unibo programme, combine a tuition-fee waiver with an annual living grant.

The award is partial funding, providing a full tuition-fee waiver (recipients pay only regional taxes, stamp duty, and insurance, around 157 euros) plus an annual study grant of around 6,500 euros, for up to two academic years (renewable subject to merit). It mainly supports second-cycle (master’s) degrees, with some calls also covering first or single-cycle programmes.

Eligibility is for international students whose qualification for admission was obtained at an institution outside the Italian education system (regardless of citizenship) matriculating at the University of Bologna, primarily in a master’s programme; you must not be enrolling in a multiple or joint programme whose fees are paid to a partner university. You apply through the dedicated online call by its deadline, providing your admission qualification and (depending on the call) GRE scores and proof of financial situation, with selection by merit. For international students aiming at Italy, a Bologna study grant offers strong, partly funded support.

The application has two parts that run in parallel. You first identify your host institution and secure admission or a supervisor there, applying to that institution directly, and then submit the CAS-ANSO scholarship application through the official ANSO portal. Both steps must be completed by the annual deadline, which typically falls at the end of March. For talented graduates aiming at a funded research degree in China, the ANSO Scholarship is a strong and well-supported option.

details:
The Turing Scheme is the UK Government’s funding programme for outgoing study and work placements abroad, managed by the Department for Education. It replaced the UK’s participation in Erasmus+ and provides grants to UK and British-overseas-territory education providers, who then offer the funding to their own students for international placements.

Funding takes the form of individual grants of 2,000 to 9,000 pounds depending on destination and disadvantaged-background status, with additional top-up grants for students with disabilities and care experience. It supports study or work placements of about four weeks up to 12 months across all subjects and degree levels, contributing to travel and living costs.

Eligibility is for students currently enrolled at a UK university (or other provider) that is participating in the Turing Scheme, with the placement at an approved overseas institution; priority is given to students from disadvantaged backgrounds, care leavers, mature students, and those with disabilities. You do not apply to Turing directly: you must be studying at a funded UK/BOT institution and apply through that institution for an approved overseas placement, with funding allocated by the institution, often by financial need. (Funding is confirmed year by year, and the UK plans to rejoin Erasmus+ from 2027.) For students at participating UK institutions, it is a useful mobility grant.

details:
The Fulbright Foreign Student Program is the flagship international exchange scheme of the US Department of State, enabling graduate students, young professionals, and artists from more than 160 countries to study and conduct research in the United States. It is one of the most prestigious and widely recognised scholarships in the world, with a vast global alumni network.

The award is fully funded and comprehensive. It covers full tuition and fees at a US university, a monthly living stipend, round-trip international airfare, accident and sickness health insurance, and a one-time settling-in allowance, along with professional development and enrichment seminars and access to the Fulbright alumni community. Some awards include further supplements.

Eligibility is for citizens or permanent residents of eligible countries who hold a bachelor’s degree by the time the grant begins, have sufficient English, meet the health requirements for a US J-1 visa, and commit to returning home for at least two years afterward. A defining feature is that you apply through the binational Fulbright Commission or US Embassy in your home country, by that country’s deadline, and eligibility and selection vary by country, with US university placement handled by IIE. For talented graduates worldwide, Fulbright is a landmark opportunity to study in the US.

One-time settling-in allowance. Professional development and enrichment seminars. Access to the Fulbright alumni network of 400,000-plus scholars. Possible additional supplements (book or computer allowance, dependent support).
requirements: Citizens and permanent residents of eligible countries (160-plus countries participate). A bachelor's degree or equivalent by the time the grant begins. Sufficient proficiency in English (TOEFL or IELTS, with minimum scores varying by country). Meet the health requirements for a US J-1 visa. Must return to your home country for at least two years after the programme. Selection considers academic excellence, leadership, and community engagement.
required_documents: Passport. Degree certificates and academic transcripts. Statement of grant purpose (study or research objective). Personal statement. Two or more academic reference letters. English language test results. Curriculum vitae.

Eligibility is broadly for citizens of a country where Rotary is active, with the academic background for graduate study, whose planned study aligns with one of Rotary’s areas of focus, and who are not Rotarians or close family of Rotarians. Crucially, you do not apply to Rotary centrally: you apply through a local Rotary club or district (found via the Rotary Club Locator), which sponsors and submits the global-grant application online, and you must secure university admission before final approval. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis (submit at least about three months before departure). The Rhodes Scholarship, administered by the Rhodes Trust at the University of Oxford, is one of the oldest and most prestigious international scholarships in the world. It brings exceptional young people from many countries to Oxford for postgraduate study, selecting not only for academic excellence but for character, leadership, and a commitment to service.

The award is fully funded, covering all university and college fees, an annual living stipend of around 18,180 pounds, return airfare, a travel grant, and health insurance, along with access to the Rhodes Trust’s global network and events. It supports two years of study at Oxford, extendable to a third year for some routes.

Eligibility is set by each Rhodes constituency: you must meet the citizenship or residency requirements of a constituency (the Global constituency covers those without a national one), are typically aged 18 to 24, and hold a strong undergraduate degree (around First Class Honours or a GPA of 3.70 or higher), while also meeting the entry requirements of your chosen Oxford graduate course. You apply through the Rhodes online system by your constituency’s deadline with a CV, personal statement, references, and transcripts, and apply separately for Oxford admission. For outstanding young leaders, the Rhodes is a flagship global scholarship.

details:
Yale University, one of the world’s leading universities, offers generous need-based financial aid to undergraduate students, including international students, through the Yale Scholarship. Rather than merit-based awards, Yale meets 100 percent of every admitted undergraduate’s demonstrated financial need for all four years with grants rather than loans.

The aid is comprehensive: it covers tuition, room, and board based on need, with no loans required, and families under 75,000 dollars in income typically pay nothing; awards can reach the full cost of attendance (up to around 90,000 dollars a year), with research and travel grants also available. International students’ need is assessed with a country-adjusted analysis.

Admission is need-blind for all applicants, including international students (your ability to pay does not affect admission). To be considered, you apply for admission and submit the financial-aid materials by the deadlines: the CSS Profile and supporting documents such as parent and student tax returns and financial statements via IDOC (international applicants use the international financial aid forms; the FAFSA applies to US citizens and eligible non-citizens). For talented students worldwide, Yale’s aid can remove the cost barrier to a top US education.

title: American University of Beirut (AUB) Scholarship
description: The American University of Beirut (AUB) is one of the oldest and most prestigious universities in the Middle…
details:
The American University of Beirut (AUB) is one of the oldest and most prestigious universities in the Middle East. Founded in 1866 and accredited in the United States, AUB follows an American liberal arts model and draws students from across the region and the world to its historic campus overlooking the Mediterranean in Beirut, Lebanon. It offers a range of financial support to help talented students manage the cost of study, primarily through need-based aid and graduate assistantships rather than a single flagship scholarship.

Financial support at AUB is awarded after admission and varies by level and programme. Undergraduate aid is largely need-based and can reduce tuition substantially, while graduate students are often supported through assistantships that combine a tuition waiver with a stipend in exchange for teaching or research work. The strongest packages can cover up to full tuition along with a stipend, and housing assistance is available for some programmes. Because awards depend on demonstrated need, academic merit, and the specific department, the exact value differs from one student to the next.

To be competitive, applicants generally need a strong academic record (a minimum GPA of around 3.2 on a 4.0 scale is a common benchmark) and solid English proficiency, typically a TOEFL score of 97 or above or an IELTS of 7.0 or higher. Requirements such as the GRE or GMAT apply to some graduate programmes. The opportunity is open to applicants of all nationalities.

The process is two stage. You first apply for admission to AUB and gain acceptance, then submit the AUB financial aid application, after which need-based awards are offered to admitted students. For students seeking a respected, US-style education in the heart of the region, AUB combines academic strength with meaningful financial support.

For self-funded international students aiming at the UK, it is a worthwhile tuition award.

title: African Union Mwalimu Nyerere Scholarship
description: The Mwalimu Nyerere African Union Scholarship Scheme is the African Union Commission’s flagship programme for postgraduate study within…
details:
The Mwalimu Nyerere African Union Scholarship Scheme is the African Union Commission’s flagship programme for postgraduate study within Africa. Named after Julius Mwalimu Nyerere, it was launched in 2007 to build and retain high-level African talent in fields critical to the continent’s development, while strengthening regional integration through intra-African student mobility. In practice this means African students are funded to pursue a master’s, and in some calls a PhD, at a reputable university in an African country other than their own.

A central feature of the scheme is its commitment to giving back. Beneficiaries sign a binding agreement to work in an African country for a period at least equal to the length of their scholarship after they graduate, so the programme is explicitly designed to reduce brain drain and keep skilled graduates on the continent. Fields of study typically span the natural sciences, engineering, health, agriculture, education, and the social sciences.

The award is run through periodic calls for applications issued by the AU Commission’s Department of Human Resources, Science and Technology, and recent rounds have often targeted specific groups, for example women in STEM or refugees and displaced persons in Africa. Because each call sets its own focus and eligible countries, applicants should always check the current call on the official African Union website before applying.

Funding generally covers tuition along with a monthly living stipend (historically around US$500) to meet costs such as food, housing, local transport, and basic medical needs, and may include travel. Applicants are citizens of African Union member states with a strong academic record who are willing to study in another African country. For young Africans committed to building the continent, this is a meaningful, values-driven scholarship, and it is worth monitoring the AU site for each new call.
benefits: Tuition fees for your master's or PhD at an African university. A monthly living stipend (historically around US$500) to cover food, housing, local transport, and basic medical costs. Travel support may be included, depending on the call. The chance to build professional skills while contributing to African development. Note: exact benefits and amounts are set in each call, so confirm the current terms on the official AU page.
requirements: Citizen of an African Union member state. Strong academic record at the relevant level (master's, or PhD in some calls). Willing to study at a reputable university in an African country other than your home country (intra-African mobility). Agree to the binding condition to work in an African country for at least the duration of the scholarship after graduating. Meet the specific focus of the current call (recent rounds have targeted, for example, women in STEM or refugees and displaced persons). Age and field limits may apply depending on the call (historically under 35 for master's and under 40 for PhD).
required_documents: Completed application form (PDF) and the Excel Applicants' Data Sheet from the African Union website. Academic transcripts and degree certificates. Proof of citizenship of an AU member state. Curriculum vitae. Research proposal (for PhD applicants). Two reference letters. A motivation essay of no more than 500 words on your field of study and its importance to Africa's development. Any documents specific to the current call (for example refugee status, where relevant).
summary: The Mwalimu Nyerere African Union Scholarship Scheme is the African Union Commission’s flagship programme for postgraduate study within…

The University of Copenhagen (UCPH), Denmark’s leading university, offers PhD fellowships as salaried positions to support doctoral researchers, including international students. Rather than a traditional scholarship, these are employed PhD positions within the university’s PhD schools, advertised against specific research projects across many departments.

The award is a salaried PhD position, providing a monthly salary of around 29,000 Danish kroner (before tax, roughly 3,900 euros), with pension contributions, paid vacation, parental leave, and a conference travel budget, for the three-year PhD programme. There is no doctoral tuition fee, and the position is full employment with benefits.

Eligibility is for those with a master’s degree in a relevant field, a strong academic record, a research profile aligned with the advertised position, and English proficiency, of any nationality. At Copenhagen, PhD fellowships are filled by searching the university’s PhD vacancy announcements and applying for an open PhD scholarship or a specific advertised position in a department; successful applicants are enrolled in the relevant PhD School and employed by the department, and non-EU/EEA applicants then arrange a Danish residence and work permit. You apply online through the specific call with your CV, transcripts, a research or motivation statement, and references by that position’s deadline. For doctoral researchers aiming at Denmark, it is a well-paid, employment-based route.

The UNIL Master’s Grant is offered by the University of Lausanne (UNIL) in Switzerland to attract talented international students to its master’s programmes. It is a competitive award that combines a monthly living grant with exemption from fixed registration fees, enabling outstanding students to study at a leading Swiss university.

The award provides a monthly grant of around 1,600 Swiss francs (for roughly ten months a year) plus exemption from the fixed registration fees (you pay only about 80 francs per semester), for the statutory minimum duration of the master’s (typically 1.5 to 2 years). Around 8 to 12 highly competitive awards are made each year.

Eligibility is for international students with an excellent academic record holding (or about to complete) a foreign university degree equivalent to a Swiss bachelor’s, who have not previously enrolled at UNIL, with C1-level French or English (per the programme’s language) and demonstrated financial need, not already residing in Switzerland. You apply online through the UNIL Master’s Grants portal by the deadline (1 November) for an eligible master’s programme (a few programmes such as Medicine and certain Law or Education tracks are excluded) and pay the application fee (around 200 francs); the scholarship application also serves as your master’s admission application. For talented international master’s students aiming at Switzerland, it is a prestigious, competitive grant.

title: Amherst College Financial Aid
description: Amherst College is one of the most selective liberal arts colleges in the United States, known for its…
details:
Amherst College is one of the most selective liberal arts colleges in the United States, known for its open curriculum, small classes, and exceptional financial aid. Located in Massachusetts, Amherst has made a landmark commitment to access: it is one of a very small number of US colleges that are need-blind for international students, meaning your ability to pay has no bearing on your chances of admission, and it pledges to meet 100 percent of every admitted student’s demonstrated financial need.

What makes Amherst’s aid especially generous is that it is entirely grant-based. Financial aid packages contain no loans, so students graduate without education debt from the college. A full-need award covers tuition, room, board, and fees, and can include a travel allowance, a book stipend, and access to funding for summer research and other opportunities. The average aid award is substantial, on the order of 66,000 US dollars per year, and because aid is based on need, the amount is tailored to each family’s circumstances.

The opportunity is open to applicants of all nationalities. Amherst looks for an exceptional academic record and genuine intellectual engagement, and it evaluates international and domestic applicants for admission on the same need-blind basis. Aid is reviewed each year, so students reapply annually to keep their award in place.

Applying for aid is part of applying for admission. Candidates submit the Common Application or Coalition Application along with the required financial aid forms, including the CSS Profile, academic transcripts, recommendation letters, and personal essays. First-year applicants typically apply by the Regular Decision deadline in early January. For high-achieving students who need full funding to study in the United States, Amherst offers one of the most supportive financial aid programmes anywhere.
benefits: Aid meets 100 percent of demonstrated financial need. Grant-based packages with no loans, covering tuition, room, board, and fees. Travel allowance and book stipend. Access to summer research funding and other opportunities.

It funds talented researchers to pursue doctoral study in Singapore’s world-class research environment.

The award is fully funded for up to four years, covering full tuition, a monthly stipend (2,500 Singapore dollars rising to 3,500 after the qualifying exam), a one-time airfare grant, and a one-time settlement allowance. Scholars work on research projects with established supervisors across biomedical, physical sciences, and engineering fields.

Eligibility is for international graduates (SINGA is primarily for those studying in Singapore for the first time; Singaporeans, PRs, and those who studied at Singapore tertiary institutions are not eligible) with a bachelor’s or master’s in science or engineering, strong academic results, a passion for research, and English proficiency. You register on the A*STAR SINGA portal, browse research projects and labs and indicate your choice of supervisor (up to two), and complete the online application with transcripts, a research proposal, and two referee reports; shortlisted candidates are interviewed. For aspiring researchers, SINGA is a leading, fully funded PhD route in Asia.
benefits: Full tuition. Monthly stipend (S$2,500 increasing to S$3,500 after the qualifying exam). One-time airfare grant. One-time settlement allowance.

The scholarship is open to international students with outstanding academic records, who hold the appropriate prior qualification for their level (a high school diploma for undergraduate study, a bachelor’s for master’s, and a master’s for PhD) and meet the English requirements. Applying is straightforward: you apply online for admission to a Bilkent programme, and admitted students are automatically considered for scholarships, with no separate scholarship application. For high-achieving students seeking a funded, English-language education in Turkey, Bilkent is a strong choice.

details:
The Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), through Student Financial Services, offers generous need-based financial aid to undergraduate students, including international students. MIT meets 100 percent of every admitted student’s demonstrated financial need with grants rather than loans, for all four years of undergraduate study.

The aid is comprehensive: it covers tuition, housing, meals, and personal expenses based on demonstrated need. Under MIT’s expanded affordability policy, families earning around 100,000 US dollars or less typically pay nothing toward the full cost, and families earning around 200,000 dollars or less pay no tuition; need-based awards average over 60,000 dollars a year. Graduate funding is provided separately through research and teaching assistantships.

Admission is need-aware for international undergraduates, but admitted international students receive the same need-based aid as domestic students, with exceptional academic achievement (often in STEM) expected. To be considered, you submit the MIT application and the financial-aid materials, including the CSS Profile and supporting documents, by the deadlines. For talented students worldwide, MIT’s aid can make a world-leading STEM education affordable; confirm the current income thresholds and deadlines on the MIT Student Financial Services site.

You identify a suitable supervisor and project, then submit an expression of interest for your preferred research programme (completing the Scholarship section); there is no separate scholarship application. For research students aiming at Australia, the UQ Research Scholarship is a leading, fully funded route.

details:
Erasmus+ is the European Union’s flagship programme for education and training, and its study exchange strand lets students spend part of their degree at a partner university in another European country. Rather than a full scholarship for a complete degree, it funds a study period abroad as part of your existing programme, with your credits recognised when you return.

The support is a mobility grant: a monthly amount of roughly 250 to 700 euros depending on the destination country, plus a travel grant, with no tuition fees charged at the host university and some insurance support. A study period abroad can last from two to twelve months.

Eligibility is for students enrolled at a higher education institution that holds an Erasmus Charter, who have completed their first year, including both EU and non-EU students at participating institutions, and who complete at least a few months abroad. You apply through your home university’s International Relations Office, which selects participants and arranges the placement at a partner institution, and you sign a Learning Agreement before you go. For students who want international experience without leaving their degree, Erasmus+ is the most established route in Europe.
benefits: Monthly grant of around EUR 250 to 700 (varies by destination country). Travel grant. No tuition fees at the host university. Insurance support.
requirements: Currently enrolled at a higher education institution holding an Erasmus Charter. Both EU and non-EU students at participating institutions. Must have completed your first year of study. Must complete at least a few months abroad.
required_documents: Application through your home university. Academic transcripts. Learning Agreement. Language proficiency. Curriculum vitae. Motivation letter.

The support typically includes free tuition at Polish public universities, a monthly stipend of around 1,500 zloty, health insurance, and in some programmes a preparatory Polish language course and a travel allowance, with the duration varying by programme (from full master’s studies to one or two semesters or research stays). Benefits differ across the programmes.

Eligibility depends on the programme: for example, the Prof. Banach Programme funds full master’s study for citizens of eligible developing countries, the Polonista Programme supports Polish-studies students and researchers, and the Anders Programme is for people of Polish origin; general requirements include a relevant prior degree and good academic standing. You choose the relevant NAWA programme, take part in the host Polish university’s own recruitment, and submit your application through the official NAWA online system during the call. For students and researchers drawn to Poland, NAWA offers a range of supported routes.

The Uppsala University Global Scholarship is offered by Uppsala University, one of Scandinavia’s oldest and most prestigious universities (founded in 1477), to support fee-paying international students undertaking a master’s. It is a highly competitive tuition-fee waiver that rewards outstanding academic achievement.

The award provides a tuition fee waiver of 75 or 100 percent for the duration of the master’s programme, renewable for the full programme duration (one to two years) subject to academic performance. It is available for a wide range of English-taught master’s programmes, with strong support services for international students; the scholarship covers the full tuition fee but not living expenses.

You then submit the separate online Uppsala scholarship application (including a motivation letter) during the scholarship round, with highly competitive merit-based selection (only about 2 percent succeed). For outstanding fee-paying master’s students aiming at Sweden, it is a prestigious award.

title: OAS Academic Scholarship
description: The OAS Academic Scholarship is offered by the Organization of American States to support graduate study and research…
details:
The OAS Academic Scholarship is offered by the Organization of American States to support graduate study and research for citizens of its member states across the Americas. Part of the OAS’s long-running commitment to human development in the region, it helps students undertake a master’s or doctoral programme at a university in a member state other than their own.

The award provides full or partial tuition, a monthly subsistence allowance, round-trip airfare, textbooks, and health insurance, for the duration of the approved programme or research period. In practice it is partial funding of up to around 10,000 US dollars, so applicants must show additional funds for living costs, and it supports study across most fields.

Eligibility is for citizens or permanent residents of an OAS member state who already hold a first (bachelor’s) degree, pursuing full-time graduate study or research at a university in a member state other than their own, with a GPA above the host university’s minimum and the required language competence (Medical Sciences and Foreign Languages are excluded). The average aid award is substantial, and many students pay significantly less than the published cost or nothing at all.

For international undergraduates aiming at Canada, these entrance scholarships are a helpful, automatic form of support.

details:

Rather than a single award, each IIT runs its own schemes, including merit-cum-means scholarships and tuition waivers for undergraduates and monthly assistantships for postgraduates.

You first gain admission through the appropriate exam (JEE for B.Tech, GATE for M.Tech, and so on), and undergraduates with family income below the set threshold apply for the merit-cum-means scholarship via the institute portal with income proof, while postgraduates receive assistantship stipends; specific schemes and amounts vary by IIT. For students aiming at India’s top technical institutes, the support makes a world-class education affordable.

Eligibility is for citizens of developing countries under the age of 35 who hold a bachelor’s degree with a minimum GPA of around 3.0, have English proficiency, and are not currently studying in Indonesia. You apply online through the KNB scholarship portal during the application window with your documents and a recommendation letter from the Indonesian Embassy or Consulate in your country, and awardees complete orientation and language preparation before studies. details:
The University of Auckland International Doctoral Scholarship supports international PhD students at New Zealand’s leading university. The award covers compulsory tuition fees (at the domestic rate, under a New Zealand government scheme for international PhD students) and a tax-free annual stipend of around 31,000 to 35,000 New Zealand dollars for up to three years (up to 42 months full-time), plus the single-student health insurance charge. You must be offered a place in an approved doctoral programme, and you are eligible for scholarship consideration before receiving your offer of place. There is no separate application: when you apply for the doctoral programme (rounds close 1 November, 1 February, 1 May, and 1 August), indicate you wish to be considered, and do not enrol before the scholarship outcome is advised. For international doctoral students aiming at New Zealand, it is a leading, fully funded option.

The award ranges from partial to full funding, covering full tuition (overseas rate) and a maintenance allowance sufficient for a single student (the most generous PhD awards are full-cost; many master’s and undergraduate awards are partial). Harvard University, through Harvard College, offers one of the most generous need-based financial aid programmes in the world to undergraduate students, including international students. Politecnico di Milano is consistently ranked among the world’s top universities for engineering, architecture, and design, and these awards recognise academic excellence with a tuition waiver and, for some, a cash award.

For talented students worldwide, UChicago’s aid can make a top US education affordable.

title: Aga Khan Foundation International Scholarship
description: The Aga Khan Foundation International Scholarship Programme (AKF ISP) is a long-running, highly competitive scholarship for outstanding students…
details:
The Aga Khan Foundation International Scholarship Programme (AKF ISP) is a long-running, highly competitive scholarship for outstanding students from selected developing countries who have no other means of financing postgraduate study. Established in 1969 and part of the Aga Khan Development Network, the programme has supported more than 1,500 scholars and is run as a global, annual competition with only a limited number of new awards each cycle.

A defining feature of the AKF ISP is its shared-funding model. Awards are made on a 50 percent grant and 50 percent loan basis, so half of the amount must be repaid. The loan carries an annual service charge of around 5 percent, requires a guarantor to co-sign, and is repaid over five years beginning six months after the funded study period. The award covers tuition and student living expenses, but it does not cover costs such as international travel, clothing, furniture, or living expenses for family members, and it is intended as a resource of last resort alongside other funding.

The programme gives priority to master’s study and considers PhD applications only in exceptional cases, where the funding is limited to the first two years. It is offered to nationals residing in a defined set of countries, which has included Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Egypt, India, Kenya, the Kyrgyz Republic, Madagascar, Mozambique, Pakistan, Syria, Tajikistan, Tanzania, and Uganda, plus applicants originally from those countries who live in Canada, France, Portugal, or the USA. It is not available for study in the United Kingdom.

Applications are decentralised and handled by local Aga Khan Foundation, Education Services, or Education Board offices, which issue forms (usually from January), interview candidates, and feed into a selection meeting held in mid-year. The award is a tuition fee reduction at one of three levels: 10,000 euros, 15,000 euros, or a full tuition waiver, for the duration of the master’s programme, with the second year subject to performance. The process has two steps: you first apply online for admission to the master’s and pay any application fee, then in the Scholarships section indicate you want the LExS and upload a motivation letter (up to 500 words) by the deadline (1 February for a September start, 1 October for a February start). For top international master’s applicants, it is a leading Dutch award.

title: AFRIKA KOMMT! Fellowship
university: AFRIKA KOMMT! (implemented by GIZ with participating German companies)
description: AFRIKA KOMMT! is one of the most prestigious leadership and corporate fellowship programmes connecting talented young African professionals…
details:
AFRIKA KOMMT! is one of the most prestigious leadership and corporate fellowship programmes connecting talented young African professionals with leading German companies. Founded in 2008 by a group of major German corporations and supported at its launch by former German Federal President Horst Koehler, it is implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft fuer Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) on behalf of the participating companies. Its purpose is to build lasting economic cooperation between Germany and Africa while developing the next generation of African business leaders.

The fellowship is a fully funded, one-year programme based in Germany and structured in three phases: preparatory German language and intercultural training (beginning in the home country), an intensive professional placement of around eight months inside a major German company, and ongoing alumni engagement after the programme. Recent intakes have offered placements at companies such as Bosch, SAP, Merck, BioNTech, Boehringer Ingelheim, and B. Braun, in senior specialist or management roles.

Because it is fully funded, fellows incur no costs to take part. The programme covers a monthly stipend to live in Germany, round-trip airfare, health insurance, accommodation support, and German language and management training, along with networking events and study tours. Fellows also receive formal certificates, including one from GIZ’s Academy for International Cooperation.

The programme targets mid-career professionals: typically African nationals under 35 with a university degree and around two to five years of relevant work experience, strong English, and clear leadership potential. The specific countries and company profiles vary from one intake to the next, so applicants should review the current profiles on the official site. Applications are submitted online in English, with candidates selecting up to two company profiles and completing assessments before an assessment centre stage. For ambitious African professionals seeking high-level international corporate experience, AFRIKA KOMMT! is a standout opportunity.
benefits: Fully funded one-year fellowship; participants incur no costs. Monthly stipend to cover living expenses in Germany. Round-trip airfare and health insurance. Accommodation support. Intensive German language training and management and leadership seminars. A professional placement of around eight months at a leading German company. Networking events, study tours, certificates (including from GIZ's Academy for International Cooperation), and an active alumni network.
requirements: African national; the programme has focused on professionals from across the continent, with specific countries varying by intake. University degree in a relevant field. Around two to five years of relevant professional work experience. Aged under 35 at the time of application. Fluent in English (the application and programme are in English); basic German is an advantage but not required. Strong leadership potential, self-motivation, teamwork, and intercultural competence. Commitment to return to Africa and apply your experience after the programme.

A short presentation on your motivation and an idea for a change initiative. A recent photograph. Proof of work experience and English proficiency. Passport copy.

The SBW Berlin Scholarship, run by the SBW Berlin (Social Better World) organisation, supports talented students from developing and emerging countries to study at universities in Berlin. It combines generous financial support with shared accommodation, mentoring, and a focus on social engagement, aiming to develop people who will contribute to positive change at home.

The Melbourne Research Scholarship, which includes the Australian Government Research Training Program, is offered by the University of Melbourne, Australia’s leading research university, to support graduate research students. There is no separate scholarship application: you apply for the graduate research course by its closing date and you are automatically considered, scored and ranked on the academic achievement of your last degree and your research potential. The award is fully funded, covering full tuition, a monthly stipend of 700 Romanian lei, free accommodation in a university dormitory, and a Romanian language course, for the full duration of the master’s programme (plus the preparatory year if needed). Recipients retain the award by passing each academic year.

Eligibility is for citizens of non-EU/EEA countries who hold a bachelor’s degree (for master’s study), are under 35, and have good academic standing; there is no application fee. You complete the online TAS application form and submit the application file (transcripts, a one-page motivation letter, and three recommendation letters, in English) by the deadline, with selection based on the quality of the documents, and selected candidates then complete the university’s admission procedure. For non-EU students seeking funded study in Europe, it is an accessible, fully funded master’s opportunity.

details:
Berea College, in Kentucky in the United States, is unusual among American colleges: every admitted student receives a no-tuition promise, so no student pays tuition. Founded on a mission of access, Berea serves students with limited financial means, including international students, and combines a rigorous liberal arts education with a required campus work programme that helps cover costs and builds experience.

For international students, the value is substantial, with tuition guaranteed and worth well over 48,000 US dollars a year. Alongside the tuition guarantee, students take part in the on-campus labour programme, receive housing and meal support, and have access to a laptop loan. Because Berea admits international students on a need-aware basis with limited places, the application is highly competitive.

The scholarship is open to international students from low-income families with a strong academic record, demonstrated financial need, and good English. You apply using the International Application for Admission and Scholarship Packet, including an essay, transcripts, and test scores, and all admitted students automatically receive the no-tuition promise. For talented students from modest backgrounds who want to study in the United States without tuition costs, Berea is one of the most distinctive opportunities available.

details:
The Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships are offered by the Swiss Confederation through the State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation to promote international exchange and research cooperation. They support young researchers from around the world to undertake research, doctoral, or postdoctoral work (and an arts master’s track for some countries) at Swiss universities and federal institutes.

The award provides a monthly living stipend of around 1,920 Swiss francs, Swiss health insurance, and other support, for a research fellowship of up to 12 months, a PhD of 12 months (renewable up to 36), or a 12-month postdoc; tuition and fees are generally not covered. Scholars work with a host supervisor at a leading Swiss institution.

Eligibility is for young researchers from an eligible country (the programme covers more than 180 countries, with country-specific deadlines) who hold at least a master’s (for research fellowships or PhD) or a PhD (for postdoctoral), or a bachelor’s for the arts master’s track, with priority for those who have not previously studied or researched in Switzerland. You must secure a letter of support from an academic host supervisor at a Swiss university or federal institute and prepare a detailed research proposal, then submit the application (via the SERI portal or your Swiss embassy) by your country’s deadline. For early-career researchers, it is a prestigious, well-supported opportunity.
