Stipendium Hungaricum is the Hungarian Government’s flagship international scholarship programme, managed by the Tempus Public Foundation. It brings thousands of students from partner countries to study in Hungary each year, across bachelor’s, master’s, doctoral, and other levels, as part of Hungary’s commitment to internationalising its higher education.

The award is fully funded, covering full tuition, a monthly living stipend (around 130,000 forints and more for higher levels), accommodation support or a contribution, health insurance, and in some cases a research or conference allowance, for the duration of the chosen programme. Scholars study at Hungarian universities across a wide range of disciplines.

Eligibility is for international students from partner countries who demonstrate strong academic performance (typically a GPA of 3.0 or equivalent), meet the English (or relevant language) requirement, and satisfy any country-specific requirements. A distinctive feature is the dual application: you submit the online application via the Tempus Public Foundation system and also apply through your country’s Sending Partner (the responsible ministry or agency), each with its own requirements and deadlines, choosing up to two study programmes in order of preference. Universities may hold entrance exams, and doctoral applicants should secure a supervisor. For students from partner countries, it is a generous, fully funded route to study in Europe.

details:
The Eiffel Excellence Scholarship Programme is run by the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs and managed by Campus France. It is one of France’s flagship awards for attracting the best international students to French universities for master’s and doctoral study, and it carries significant prestige in the French higher education system.

The award is generous, providing a monthly allowance (around 1,181 euros for master’s students and 1,400 for doctoral candidates) along with additional benefits such as international airfare, health insurance, and support for cultural activities; tuition is generally covered or waived through the host institution. Funding runs from 12 to 36 months depending on the level and year of enrolment.

A defining feature is that you cannot apply directly to Campus France: only a French higher education institution can submit your candidacy. Non-French applicants, typically up to around 25 to 30 years old depending on level, apply through the French host institution, which selects and submits the application to Campus France by the deadline (around early January). Applicants must not already be living in France. For top international students aiming at a French master’s or PhD, Eiffel is a leading opportunity.

Support is awarded on merit and varies by programme and student. The scholarship is open to international students applying to study at BI, who can demonstrate strong academic performance and good English. Applying is part of the admission process: you apply for a BI bachelor’s or master’s programme and upload a scholarship application letter in the scholarship section of the online application, by the scholarship deadline. For ambitious students drawn to a leading Nordic business school, BI’s scholarships can make study in Norway more affordable.

details:
Australia Awards Scholarships are long-term development awards funded by the Australian Government’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT). They offer people from eligible developing countries across the Asia-Pacific, Africa, and the Middle East the chance to undertake a full undergraduate or postgraduate qualification at an Australian university, with the aim of building skills and leadership that contribute to the development of their home countries.

The award is one of the most generous available. It covers full tuition for the duration of the course, return air travel, a one-time establishment allowance, a tax-free contribution to living expenses, overseas student health cover, and a compulsory introductory academic programme. Additional support can include pre-course English training, academic support, fieldwork allowances for research students, and reunion travel on longer awards.

Eligibility centres on citizenship of a participating country, a minimum level of work experience, and a commitment to return home for two years after finishing, and applicants must not already be living in Australia. Because rules and deadlines are set country by country, applicants begin by checking their own country’s page, reading the policy handbook, and applying through the OASIS portal before their national deadline. For talented professionals from developing nations, Australia Awards are a flagship route to a fully funded Australian degree.

title: Swedish Institute Scholarships
description: The Swedish Institute Scholarships for Global Professionals (SISGP), funded by the Government of Sweden and run by the…
details:
The Swedish Institute Scholarships for Global Professionals (SISGP), funded by the Government of Sweden and run by the Swedish Institute, support talented professionals from eligible countries to undertake a master’s degree in Sweden. The programme looks not only for academic strength but for leadership experience and a commitment to contributing to sustainable global development, and it includes membership of a leadership network.

The award is fully funded, covering full tuition for the one or two-year master’s, a monthly living allowance of 10,000 Swedish kronor, a one-time travel grant of 15,000 kronor, and insurance, along with membership of the SI Network for Future Global Leaders, the SI Summer Academy, and a global alumni network. Scholars gain mentorship and professional development opportunities.

Eligibility is for citizens of one of the eligible countries (around 33 to 34) with the required work experience (about 3,000 hours) and demonstrated leadership, who are liable to pay tuition fees in Sweden. You first apply for an eligible English-taught master’s at universityadmissions.se by mid-January, then apply for the SI Scholarship through the SI online portal during its window using the mandatory templates, and you must be admitted to an eligible programme by the admission results date. (SISGP replaced the former Swedish Institute Study Scholarships.) For professionals from eligible countries, it is a prestigious, fully funded award.

description: The Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarships are offered by the Government of Canada (funded by CIHR, NSERC, and SSHRC)…
details:
The Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarships are offered by the Government of Canada (funded by CIHR, NSERC, and SSHRC) to attract and retain world-class doctoral students. They are among the most generous doctoral scholarships globally, recognising academic excellence, research potential, and leadership across all disciplines.

The award provides 50,000 Canadian dollars a year for three years, with no tuition offset (the entire amount is for personal and research expenses), along with prestigious recognition, access to Vanier-Banting Secretariat events and leadership development, and networking with Canada’s top doctoral researchers. It can be combined with other awards subject to university policy.

Eligibility is for Canadian citizens, permanent residents, or international students pursuing their first doctoral degree (PhD, or the PhD portion of a joint programme such as MD/PhD) with a first-class average and demonstrated academic excellence, research potential, and leadership, who have not completed more than about 20 months of doctoral study and do not hold a prior tri-agency doctoral award. You cannot apply directly: you must be nominated by a single Canadian institution that holds a Vanier quota, so you contact the faculty of graduate studies, secure faculty support, and prepare your application in ResearchNet by the institution’s internal deadline. For outstanding doctoral students aiming at Canada, the Vanier is a flagship, fully funded scholarship.
benefits: CAD 50,000 per year for three years, one of the most generous doctoral scholarships globally. No tuition offset (the entire amount is for personal and research expenses). Prestigious recognition that enhances your academic and career profile. Access to Vanier-Banting Secretariat events and leadership development. Networking with Canada's top doctoral researchers (combinable with other awards, subject to university policy).
requirements: Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or international student pursuing your first doctoral degree. A first-class average and demonstrated academic excellence, research potential, and leadership. Not having completed more than about 20 months of doctoral study. Not holding a prior CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC doctoral award. Nominated by a single Canadian institution that holds a Vanier quota.
required_documents: Nomination and application via ResearchNet. Academic transcripts and proof of previous degrees. Research proposal. Two reference assessments and a leadership reference. Curriculum vitae. A statement on leadership and any other institution-requested materials.

details:
Turkiye Scholarships (Turkiye Burslari) is the Turkish Government’s flagship international scholarship programme, run by the Presidency for Turks Abroad and Related Communities (YTB). It is a highly competitive, fully funded scholarship that brings students from around the world to study at Turkish universities across undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral levels.

The award is fully funded, covering full tuition, a monthly stipend (around 800 to 3,000 Turkish lira depending on level), accommodation, health insurance, a return flight ticket, and a one-year Turkish language course for those without C1 Turkish, for the duration of the chosen programme. A key advantage is that a single application covers both the scholarship and university placement, with no separate admission needed.

Eligibility is for non-Turkish nationals meeting the age limits (roughly under 21 for undergraduate, under 30 for master’s, under 35 for PhD, under 45 for research) with strong academic results (around 70 percent GPA for undergraduate, higher for graduate). You apply free and individually online via the official Turkiye Scholarships platform during the window (around January to February), uploading transcripts, diploma, ID/passport, and any required test scores; selection includes evaluation and interviews. For international students worldwide, it is one of the most generous and sought-after government scholarships.
benefits: Full tuition. Monthly stipend. Accommodation. Health insurance. Turkish language course (one year). Return flight ticket.
requirements: Open to citizens of all countries except Turkey. Under 21 for bachelor's, under 30 for master's, under 35 for PhD (under 45 for research). GPA requirements: around 70 percent for bachelor's, 75 percent for master's and PhD. Strong academic results. Not currently studying in Turkiye at the same level.
required_documents: Online application via the Turkiye Scholarships platform. Academic transcripts. Diploma or certificate. ID or passport. Any required test scores. Statement of purpose. References where required.

details:
The Gates Cambridge Scholarship is one of the most prestigious international postgraduate awards in the world, funded by a landmark gift from the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation to the University of Cambridge. It brings outstanding students from outside the UK to Cambridge for full-time postgraduate study, selecting scholars who combine academic excellence with leadership and a commitment to improving the lives of others.

The award covers the full cost of study at Cambridge: full tuition fees for the duration of the degree, a generous maintenance allowance (around 19,500 pounds a year at the doctoral rate), one economy return airfare a year, inbound visa costs and the NHS health surcharge, and academic development funding, with family and fieldwork allowances where applicable and hardship support in exceptional cases.

Eligibility is open to citizens of any country outside the UK applying for an eligible full-time postgraduate course at Cambridge, with an exceptional academic record. You submit your Cambridge admission application by the relevant deadline (around mid-October for US citizens resident in the US, and early January for everyone else) and complete the Gates Cambridge section with a statement and reference; you are considered as part of the admissions process. For the very best graduate students worldwide, it is a flagship fully funded opportunity.
benefits: Full tuition fees for the duration of your degree (up to four years for PhD). Maintenance allowance (around GBP 19,500 a year at the PhD rate). One economy return airfare per year. Inbound visa costs and the NHS health surcharge. Academic development funding (up to around GBP 2,000 for conferences and research trips). Family allowance for dependents where applicable. Fieldwork funding for research students and hardship funding in exceptional cases. Access to the Gates Cambridge Scholars community and alumni network.
requirements: Citizens of any country outside the UK. Must apply for a full-time residential postgraduate course at Cambridge. Exceptional academic record. Leadership and a commitment to improving the lives of others.
required_documents: Cambridge admission application. Degree certificates and academic transcripts. Research proposal (for research courses). Two academic reference letters. Gates Cambridge statement and reference. Proof of English proficiency. Curriculum vitae.

title: Erasmus Mundus

details:
Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are prestigious, fully funded international master’s programmes run by the European Union under the Erasmus+ programme. Each is delivered by a consortium of universities in several countries, so students typically study in two or three European countries and graduate with a joint or double degree from leading institutions, across almost every field of study.

The scholarship is comprehensive. It covers full tuition for the whole programme, a monthly living allowance of around 1,400 euros, a one-time installation contribution, an annual travel allowance scaled by distance, participation costs, and health and accident insurance through the consortium. Funding covers up to 24 months of study.

Eligibility is open to students worldwide who hold a bachelor’s degree or are in their final year. You choose an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master from the official catalogue and apply directly to the consortium running it, since each has its own portal and deadline (typically October to January), requesting the scholarship within the same application. The competition is strong, but the reward is a funded, multi-country master’s from top European universities, which makes Erasmus Mundus one of the most sought-after scholarships in the world.
benefits: Full tuition fees for the entire programme (typically one to two years across two or three European countries). Monthly living allowance of around EUR 1,400 for the programme duration. One-time installation contribution of around EUR 1,000. Annual travel allowance (around EUR 2,000 to 4,000 depending on distance). Participation costs (books, lab fees, and similar) covered. Health and accident insurance through the consortium. A joint or double degree from multiple prestigious European universities.
requirements: Open to students worldwide. Hold a bachelor's degree or be in your final year of bachelor studies. Apply to a specific Erasmus Mundus Joint Master from the official catalogue. Meet the specific entry requirements of the chosen consortium.
required_documents: Academic transcripts and degree certificate (or proof of final-year status). Curriculum vitae. Motivation letter. Reference letters. Proof of English proficiency. Passport copy.

details:
The Holland Scholarship is funded by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science together with participating Dutch universities, and coordinated by Nuffic. It is designed to attract international students from outside Europe to study in the Netherlands, and is awarded to around 1,300 students each year across the participating institutions.

The scholarship is a one-time award of 5,000 euros toward the first year of study, available at 22 participating Dutch universities and universities of applied sciences. It is a partial contribution rather than full funding, and it can be combined with other funding sources such as university scholarships or personal funds to build a fuller package; it covers part of living expenses or tuition.

Eligibility is for non-EU/EEA international students applying for the first time to a participating Dutch institution, who have been accepted to an eligible bachelor’s or master’s programme, meet the institution’s requirements, and have a strong academic record, and who are not Dutch citizens or already studying in the Netherlands. You apply directly to your chosen institution by its specific deadline. For international students considering the Netherlands, it is a helpful first-year award that pairs well with other support.
benefits: One-time award of EUR 5,000 toward the first year of studies in the Netherlands. Available at 22 participating Dutch institutions. Can be combined with other funding sources. Open for both bachelor's and master's level. Awarded to approximately 1,300 students annually.
